# Bursar M1 Accounts Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Link real bank accounts through Enable Banking (account information only), keep balances and transactions in sync with consent lifecycle, notifications and encrypted backups, and ship the finished panel pages that M1 can deliver (Home, Accounts, Account detail, Connect, Transactions, Settings) on a rebuilt panel foundation. It ends deployed on the reference host with real accounts synced, the renewal path tested in the Sandbox and a passing restore test.

**Architecture:** The single Node process from M0 gains an Enable Banking client behind a method-and-path allowlist (RS256 JWT signed with the application key from a `*_FILE` secret), finance tables in the SQLCipher database, sync and notification jobs on the existing queue, scheduled tasks (daily background sync, consent lifecycle, sync health, nightly backup), an in-process event bus pushed to the panel over server-sent events, SMTP notifications and `VACUUM INTO` backups uploaded to an optional S3-compatible target. The panel is rebuilt on a route registry with React Router, an AppShell (sidebar, topbar, command palette, notifications, privacy mode, theme, density), semantic design tokens with dark mode, shared list primitives, and a Playwright QA harness that is the definition of done for every UI task.

**Tech Stack:** Node 24.21.0, pnpm 12.18.0, TypeScript 7, Hono 4, Drizzle ORM 0.45 + drizzle-kit 0.31, `better-sqlite3-multiple-ciphers` 13, `jose` 6 (RS256 signing), Zod 4, pino 10, nodemailer 10.2.1, aws4fetch 1.0.20, Vitest 5, Biome 2, React 19.3.1, Vite 8, Tailwind 4, TanStack Query 5, React Router 8.5.0, Zustand 5.0.16, lucide-react 1.61.0, Recharts 3.10.1, motion 14.6.0, `@fontsource-variable/inter` and `@fontsource-variable/manrope` 5.3.0, i18next 27, playwright-core 1.64.1 with the system Chrome, `@axe-core/playwright` 4.14.0.

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-09-bursar-design.md` (milestone M1, §14). Panel UX/UI: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-09-panel-ux-design.md` (binding for every UI task). Research notes used by this plan (gitignored, local): `.superpowers/sdd/2026-11-09-m1-accounts/{eb-api-notes.md, codebase-map.md, deps-notes.md, m0-deferred-minors.txt}`.

## Global Constraints

Every task's requirements implicitly include this section.

**Toolchain and commands**
- Every shell command runs with this prefix (Node 24.21.0; `pnpm` is a shim for pnpm 12.18.0; never the global pnpm, npm or npx):
  `cd <worktree> && export PATH="<worktree>/.superpowers/sdd/2026-11-09-m1-accounts/bin:$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:$PATH" && …`
  `<worktree>` is the absolute path of the M1 worktree; the controller writes the expanded prefix into each task brief. In the plan text the prefix is written as `<prefix> && …`.
- Package manager pnpm only. New dependency versions are exactly the pins below; `minimumReleaseAge: 1440` stays; `pnpm-lock.yaml` is committed with the `package.json` change (CI and the Dockerfile use `--frozen-lockfile`).
- Pinned versions (from `deps-notes.md`; exact pins without `^` where marked): web `react-router` 8.5.0 (exact), `zustand` ^5.0.16, `lucide-react` ^1.61.0, `recharts` ^3.10.1, `react-is` 19.3.1, `motion` 14.6.0 (exact), `@fontsource-variable/inter` ^5.3.0, `@fontsource-variable/manrope` ^5.3.0; web dev `playwright-core` 1.64.1 (exact), `@axe-core/playwright` ^4.14.0, `tsx` ^4.23.15; server `nodemailer` 10.2.1 (exact, no `@types/nodemailer`), `aws4fetch` 1.0.20 (exact). No other new dependency (no cmdk, sonner, tar, AWS SDK, date library).
- The UX doc names "React Router 7"; the major published and pinned is 8 (`deps-notes.md`). Import from `"react-router"`, and `RouterProvider` from `"react-router/dom"`.
- If an installed version's API differs from the code in a task, keep the exported names and signatures from the task's **Interfaces** block, adapt the internals following the library's documentation, and record the difference in the commit message body.
- Run `pnpm format` before `pnpm lint` in every task: Biome's formatting and import ordering are authoritative.
- Standard verification for every task: `<prefix> && pnpm format && pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test`. Paste the full Vitest summary line of each package (`Test Files … Tests …`); zero executed tests counts as a failure. A task that changes `apps/server/src/db/schema.ts` also runs `pnpm --filter @bursar/server db:generate` and shows `git status --porcelain -- apps/server/drizzle` is empty after committing.

**Repository, language and git**
- Code, comments, docs, test names and commit messages in English. Conventional Commits (`type(scope): description`). UI strings live only in `apps/web/src/i18n/it.json` and `en.json` (Italian is the default language, English is complete); server-side email text lives in `apps/server/src/notifications/templates.ts` for both languages.
- No personal identifiers in the repository or in any output: no real hostnames, domains, IPs, bank account data, names, emails. Use placeholders (`<hostname>`, `<host>`, `<dir>`) and fictional data (fictional bank names, generated IBANs with valid checksums, generic counterparties).
- Work on branch `feat/m1-accounts`. `git add` explicit paths only (never `-A` or `.`); run `git status` and `git diff --cached --stat` before each commit; never `--no-verify`; no push, merge or deploy outside the owner-gated steps of Task 24.
- **Owner gates:** steps marked **Owner gate** (credentials, real bank login, starting a long-running dev server, host access, deploy, push) need the owner's explicit go-ahead at that moment. The QA harness's ephemeral loopback server (Task 5) is a test fixture started and stopped inside the QA command, not a dev server.

**Secrets and privacy**
- Every secret comes from an environment variable or its `*_FILE` variant (`readSecret` in `config.ts`): `EB_PRIVATE_KEY`, `SMTP_PASSWORD`, `BACKUP_S3_SECRET_KEY` are new in M1. Secrets are never logged, printed, echoed in errors or committed; their values are added to `configSecrets(config)` so the log scrubber removes them.
- Never log or return in errors: provider session ids, authorisation codes, `state` values, full IBANs, transaction remittance text, JWTs, SMTP credentials. Enable Banking error messages are reduced to HTTP status, `error` code and the API's `message`.
- Banking is read-only. The Enable Banking client can reach only the allowlisted account-information operations (Task 10); a unit test proves every payment path is rejected before any network call.
- Notification emails contain no financial data: an event title and a link to the panel only.
- Tests never use the network: `fetch` is injected or stubbed; Enable Banking fixtures are shaped exactly like the documented responses (`eb-api-notes.md` §2–§9). No real credentials, no Sandbox calls in tests.

**Data rules**
- Money: integer minor units (`amount_minor` INTEGER, JS `number` that must be a safe integer) plus the ISO 4217 currency code. No floating-point arithmetic on amounts anywhere. Provider decimal strings go through `parseDecimalToMinor`; every displayed amount goes through `formatMoney` (Task 1).
- Time: stored in UTC as epoch milliseconds (INTEGER). Calendar dates are `LocalDate` strings `YYYY-MM-DD`. "Local day" logic (background caps, schedules, consent days, cash-flow buckets) uses `config.timezone` (the `TZ` setting).
- Integer autoincrement ids are used in URLs and API payloads; no id (integer or uuid) is ever shown in the UI, in toasts or in "not found" messages.
- API conventions: JSON; errors `{ "error": string, "code"?: string, "retryAt"?: number }` (English `error`, stable snake_case `code` for the UI to translate); request bodies and query strings validated with Zod schemas from `@bursar/shared`; every `/api` response that does not set its own `Cache-Control` gets `no-store` (Task 7); the two exceptions set theirs on purpose: the SSE stream `/api/events` (`no-cache, no-transform`, Task 7) and the bank logo proxy `/api/banks/logo` (`private, max-age=86400`, Task 10). Mutating requests keep the M0 Origin check; session cookies stay `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Secure` on HTTPS.
- Database changes: edit `apps/server/src/db/schema.ts`, generate with `pnpm --filter @bursar/server db:generate --name <slug>`, commit SQL + `drizzle/meta`. All M1 tables are created by Task 6 in one migration.
- Single process: one job worker, sequential jobs. Job payloads are validated with the Zod schemas of `apps/server/src/jobs/types.ts` (Task 7).

**Panel (every UI task)**
- The UX doc is binding. Pages use semantic token utilities only (`bg-bg`, `bg-surface`, `bg-surface-2`, `border-subtle`, `text-fg`, `text-muted`, `text-primary`, `bg-primary-50`, `text-accent`, `text-positive`, `text-ink`, `text-warning bg-warning-soft`, `text-danger bg-danger-soft`, `text-info bg-info-soft`); never `dark:`, `bg-white`, `text-gray-*`, `slate-*` or raw hex colours in components.
- CSP is unchanged (`style-src 'self'`, `font-src 'self'`, `img-src 'self' data:`, `connect-src 'self'`): no `<style>` element injection, no inline `<script>`, no external fonts or images (bank logos go through the server proxy of Task 10). Styles set through React's `style` prop or `motion` (CSSOM) are allowed; the QA run is the check.
- "Hidden until shipped": a route is registered and visible only when its page exists (`shipped: true` in the registry). No "coming soon", no placeholder widgets, no dead buttons, no link to a missing route.
- Every string in both locale files (the parity test fails otherwise); counts through i18next plurals; Italian copy uses typographic quotes “…” around state names and searches; buttons are verb + object with the count when they act on N items.
- Amount tones only through `amountTone` (`src/lib/tones.ts`); deadline colours only through `src/lib/thresholds.ts`; toasts only through `feedback()`; dates only through `useFormatters()`; amounts only through `<Money>`, which honours privacy mode.
- Layout rules from the trap list: global `.grid > * { min-width: 0 }`; no sticky table header inside an `overflow-x-auto` container; Zustand selectors that build objects or arrays use `useShallow`; page transitions on entry only (`key={pathname}`, no `AnimatePresence` exit around the outlet); back buttons fall back to the breadcrumb parent when `history.state?.idx === 0`.
- **UI definition of done** (UX doc §9): type check, lint and unit tests pass; `<prefix> && pnpm --filter @bursar/web qa` (Task 5) reports `0 failures` over every shipped route at 1440×900 light and dark and 390×844, with no console error, page error, CSP violation, horizontal overflow at 390 px, or "undefined"/"NaN"/"Invalid Date"/raw i18n key in the page text; the task report lists the screenshot directory, and the reviewer looks at the screenshots (hierarchy, alignment, truncation, raw ids, untranslated strings, empty and error states, dark mode).

## Out of scope for M1

Deferred M0 minors that M1 code does not touch stay deferred: config parsing hardening (lenient base64 master key, `Number()` port, numeric hostnames, half-set CF Access messages, non-enumerable `Config` secrets), `crypto.seal` AAD and `authTagLength`, HKDF known-answer test, DB file modes 0600/0700 and raw hex SQLCipher key, `owner` CHECK (id = 1), Access guard algorithm pinning and denial logging, static handler realpath/dotfile containment, session absolute lifetime and `__Host-` cookie prefix, setup-code file hardening, argon2 parameter pinning, TOTP edge cases, Dockerfile digest pins and `PNPM_STORE_DIR`, compose `cap_drop`/`no-new-privileges`/`pids_limit`, `TUNNEL_TOKEN` as a secret, CI action SHA pins and gitleaks checksum, ADR 0003 quote provenance, `sdk-gate.ts` cleanups, uncaught exception handlers, `.dockerignore` `**/data` scope.

Spec items owned by later milestones: transaction categories and recategorisation (M2), documents and the documents directory in backups (M3; the backup set format leaves room for it), report preflight sync and report notifications (M4), Claude credential and agent proposal notifications (M2), demo mode (M6), CI running the QA harness, recording scrubbed Sandbox fixtures (fixtures in M1 are built from the documented response shapes).

Folded into M1 tasks: queue running-guard, transactional `fail`, corrupt-payload handling, failure stack logging and startup recovery (T7); `FailureLimiter` sweep and size cap (T7); `/api` `Cache-Control: no-store` (T7); redaction of new secrets and identifiers (T8); `temp_store = MEMORY` (T6); static handler in-memory cache and 404 for missing `/assets/*` (T5); CSP `style-src 'self'` re-check with the real panel (T5 harness, every UI task); PSU IP follows `trustCfConnectingIp` (T13); `<html lang>` set at i18n init (T2); SetupPage QR `.catch` and 429 message (T4); compose log rotation (T23).

### Task 1: Shared money, date, IBAN and text helpers

**Files:**
- Create: `packages/shared/src/money.ts`, `packages/shared/src/dates.ts`, `packages/shared/src/iban.ts`, `packages/shared/src/text.ts`
- Modify: `packages/shared/src/index.ts`
- Test: `packages/shared/src/money.test.ts`, `packages/shared/src/dates.test.ts`, `packages/shared/src/iban.test.ts`, `packages/shared/src/text.test.ts`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: nothing new (Zod and `Intl` only).
- Produces (`@bursar/shared`):
  - `money.ts`: `class MoneyParseError extends Error`; `currencyMinorDigits(currency: string): number` (cached `Intl.NumberFormat("en", { style: "currency", currency }).resolvedOptions().maximumFractionDigits`; throws `RangeError` for an invalid code); `parseDecimalToMinor(amount: string, currency: string): number`; `minorToDecimalString(minor: bigint | number, currency: string): string` (exact, e.g. `-1234` EUR → `"-12.34"`); `interface FormatMoneyOptions { sign?: "auto" | "always" | "never"; masked?: boolean }`; `formatMoney(minor: bigint | number, currency: string, locale: string, options?: FormatMoneyOptions): string`; `const MASKED_AMOUNT = "•••••"`; `sumMinor(values: readonly number[]): number` (throws `RangeError` when the result is not a safe integer).
  - `dates.ts`: `type LocalDate = string` (`YYYY-MM-DD`); `localDateSchema` (Zod, regex plus real calendar date); `toLocalDate(instant: Date | number, timeZone: string): LocalDate`; `addDays(date: LocalDate, days: number): LocalDate`; `diffDays(a: LocalDate, b: LocalDate): number` (a − b, whole days); `startOfLocalDay(date: LocalDate, timeZone: string): number` (epoch ms, DST-safe); `localTimeOfDay(instant: Date | number, timeZone: string): string` (`HH:MM`); `calendarDaysUntil(target: Date | number, now: Date | number, timeZone: string): number` (local calendar days, negative when past); `formatRelative(instant: Date | number, now: Date | number, locale: string, timeZone: string): string`; `formatAbsolute(instant: Date | number, locale: string, timeZone: string, options?: { withTime?: boolean }): string`; `formatLocalDate(date: LocalDate, locale: string, options?: { style?: "short" | "medium" | "long"; weekday?: boolean }): string`; `formatRelativeDay(date: LocalDate, today: LocalDate, locale: string): string` (calendar-day distance between two `LocalDate`s, no time of day: "Today", "Yesterday", "3 days ago", "In 2 days" in sentence case within `RELATIVE_LIMIT_DAYS`, the medium date beyond; the one relative-day label for booking dates, used by Tasks 3, 19 and 21); `RELATIVE_LIMIT_DAYS = 45`.
  - `iban.ts`: `normalizeIban(value: string): string` (uppercase, no spaces); `isValidIban(value: string): boolean` (length per format, mod-97); `formatIban(iban: string): string` (groups of 4); `maskIban(iban: string): string` (country + check digits, bullets, last 4: `IT60 •••• •••• 1234`, the number of bullet groups fixed at 2 regardless of length); `maskIdentifier(identifier: string): string` (`•••• 1234` for non-IBAN identifiers); `identifierLast4(identifier: string): string`; `maskIbanDigitsForPrivacy(masked: string): string` (replaces the remaining digits with bullets, used by privacy mode).
  - `text.ts`: `normalizeForSearch(value: string): string` (NFD, strip combining marks, lowercase, collapse whitespace, trim), used by the server's `search_text` and the panel's search.

**Requirements:**
- `parseDecimalToMinor`: accepts `"12"`, `"12.3"`, `"12.30"`, `"-0.5"`, `"+7.00"`, leading/trailing whitespace; uses the currency's minor digits (EUR 2, JPY 0, BHD/KWD 3); extra fraction digits are accepted only when they are zeros (`"1.230"` EUR ok, `"1.234"` EUR throws); rejects thousands separators, commas, exponents, empty strings, `NaN`, values beyond `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` minor units; never uses `parseFloat` or `Number()` on the fraction (string arithmetic only). `"-0"` becomes `0`.
- `formatMoney` builds the exact decimal string and passes it to `Intl.NumberFormat(locale, { style: "currency", currency, signDisplay })` (`format(string)` is exact in Node 24 and browsers); `sign: "always"` uses `signDisplay: "exceptZero"`, `"never"` formats the absolute value; `masked: true` returns `MASKED_AMOUNT` with no digits. Tests: `it-IT` (`1.234,50 €`, Intl spacing kept as produced), `en-GB`, `bigint` input, negative values, JPY with no decimals, `-0`.
- `formatRelative`: under 45 days in either direction uses `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat(locale, { numeric: "auto" })` with minutes (< 60 min), hours (< 24 h), then calendar days in the time zone ("yesterday", "in 3 days"); "now" for under a minute; at or beyond 45 days returns `formatAbsolute` (date only). Tests with a fixed `now`, both locales, near midnight in `Europe/Rome`, a DST change day, and future instants.
- `calendarDaysUntil` counts local calendar days, not 24-hour blocks (expiry later today is 0; tomorrow at 00:30 is 1); test across DST.
- `startOfLocalDay` and `toLocalDate` round-trip for every day of a year in `Europe/Rome` and `America/New_York`.
- IBAN tests use generated fictional IBANs with valid checksums (no real account numbers); invalid checksum, wrong length and lowercase/spaced input are covered.
- `normalizeForSearch("  Caffè   ÀB ")` equals `"caffe ab"`.
- Commit: `feat(shared): add money, date, IBAN and text helpers`.

**Implementation notes (read before starting):**
- All four modules are pure TypeScript with no new dependency: `Intl` and Zod (already a dependency of `@bursar/shared`) only. No UI is touched, so no Playwright run applies to this task.
- Tests pass the time zone and the locale explicitly and never read the process time zone or locale, so results do not depend on the machine. Intl output (spacing, month abbreviations such as `Sept`) is the one the pinned Node 24.21.0 produces; if a literal differs on another ICU version, record it in the commit body instead of weakening the helper.
- Deliberate refinements of the contract text, all inside the exported signatures: `formatMoney` forces `useGrouping: "always"` because CLDR's `it-IT` data omits the thousands separator below 10 000 (`1234,50 €`), which contradicts the `1.234,50 €` required above and the UX doc's `2.340,00 €`; `normalizeForSearch` lowercases before the NFD step so that `İ` leaves no combining dot behind (same result as the specified order for every other input); `formatRelative` decides "45 days or more" on local calendar days, like the day buckets below it.
- `parseDecimalToMinor` works on the digit string: the integer and fraction digits are concatenated, range-checked as a `BigInt` and only then converted with `Number()`. There is no `parseFloat`, and no float arithmetic at any point.

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import {
  currencyMinorDigits,
  formatMoney,
  MASKED_AMOUNT,
  MoneyParseError,
  minorToDecimalString,
  parseDecimalToMinor,
  sumMinor,
} from "./money";

const NBSP = " ";

describe("currencyMinorDigits", () => {
  it("reads the minor digits from Intl", () => {
    expect(currencyMinorDigits("EUR")).toBe(2);
    expect(currencyMinorDigits("USD")).toBe(2);
    expect(currencyMinorDigits("JPY")).toBe(0);
    expect(currencyMinorDigits("BHD")).toBe(3);
    expect(currencyMinorDigits("KWD")).toBe(3);
  });

  it("accepts lowercase codes and rejects malformed ones", () => {
    expect(currencyMinorDigits("eur")).toBe(2);
    expect(() => currencyMinorDigits("EURO")).toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(() => currencyMinorDigits("12")).toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(() => currencyMinorDigits("")).toThrow(RangeError);
  });
});

describe("parseDecimalToMinor", () => {
  it("parses the plain decimal forms providers send", () => {
    expect(parseDecimalToMinor("12", "EUR")).toBe(1200);
    expect(parseDecimalToMinor("12.3", "EUR")).toBe(1230);
    expect(parseDecimalToMinor("12.30", "EUR")).toBe(1230);
    expect(parseDecimalToMinor("-0.5", "EUR")).toBe(-50);
    expect(parseDecimalToMinor("+7.00", "EUR")).toBe(700);
    expect(parseDecimalToMinor("  42.10\n", "EUR")).toBe(4210);
    expect(parseDecimalToMinor("007.50", "EUR")).toBe(750);
    expect(parseDecimalToMinor("0", "EUR")).toBe(0);
  });

  it("is exact where floating point is not", () => {
    // 4.35 * 100 === 434.99999999999994 and 0.29 * 100 === 28.999999999999996 in doubles.
    expect(parseDecimalToMinor("4.35", "EUR")).toBe(435);
    expect(parseDecimalToMinor("0.29", "EUR")).toBe(29);
    expect(parseDecimalToMinor("1.15", "EUR")).toBe(115);
    expect(parseDecimalToMinor("0.07", "EUR")).toBe(7);
  });

  it("uses the minor digits of the currency", () => {
    expect(parseDecimalToMinor("500", "JPY")).toBe(500);
    expect(parseDecimalToMinor("500.0", "JPY")).toBe(500);
    expect(parseDecimalToMinor("-1.234", "BHD")).toBe(-1234);
    expect(parseDecimalToMinor("1.5", "KWD")).toBe(1500);
    expect(parseDecimalToMinor("12.34", "eur")).toBe(1234);
  });

  it("accepts extra fraction digits only when they are zeros", () => {
    expect(parseDecimalToMinor("1.230", "EUR")).toBe(123);
    expect(parseDecimalToMinor("0.30000000000000000000", "EUR")).toBe(30);
    expect(() => parseDecimalToMinor("1.234", "EUR")).toThrow(MoneyParseError);
    expect(() => parseDecimalToMinor("1.2300001", "EUR")).toThrow(MoneyParseError);
    expect(() => parseDecimalToMinor("500.5", "JPY")).toThrow(MoneyParseError);
    expect(() => parseDecimalToMinor("1.2345", "BHD")).toThrow(MoneyParseError);
  });

  it("turns negative zero into zero", () => {
    expect(Object.is(parseDecimalToMinor("-0", "EUR"), 0)).toBe(true);
    expect(Object.is(parseDecimalToMinor("-0.00", "EUR"), 0)).toBe(true);
    expect(Object.is(parseDecimalToMinor("-0.000", "EUR"), 0)).toBe(true);
  });

  it.each([
    "",
    "   ",
    "NaN",
    "Infinity",
    "1,234.50",
    "1.234,50",
    "12,5",
    "1 000.00",
    "1_000",
    "1e3",
    "1E3",
    "1.5e1",
    "0x10",
    ".5",
    "5.",
    "--1",
    "+-1",
    "1.2.3",
    "12abc",
    "１２",
  ])("rejects %j", (input) => {
    expect(() => parseDecimalToMinor(input, "EUR")).toThrow(MoneyParseError);
  });

  it("rejects amounts beyond the safe integer range", () => {
    expect(parseDecimalToMinor("90071992547409.91", "EUR")).toBe(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER);
    expect(parseDecimalToMinor("-90071992547409.91", "EUR")).toBe(-Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER);
    expect(() => parseDecimalToMinor("90071992547409.92", "EUR")).toThrow(MoneyParseError);
    expect(() => parseDecimalToMinor("-90071992547409.92", "EUR")).toThrow(MoneyParseError);
    expect(() => parseDecimalToMinor(`1${"0".repeat(40)}`, "EUR")).toThrow(MoneyParseError);
    expect(() => parseDecimalToMinor("9007199254740992", "JPY")).toThrow(MoneyParseError);
  });

  it("throws a RangeError for an invalid currency", () => {
    expect(() => parseDecimalToMinor("1", "EURO")).toThrow(RangeError);
  });

  it("does not echo the rejected input in the error message", () => {
    expect(() => parseDecimalToMinor("secret-1,5", "EUR")).toThrow(/^Invalid decimal amount$/);
  });
});

describe("minorToDecimalString", () => {
  it("builds exact decimal strings", () => {
    expect(minorToDecimalString(-1234, "EUR")).toBe("-12.34");
    expect(minorToDecimalString(1234, "EUR")).toBe("12.34");
    expect(minorToDecimalString(5, "EUR")).toBe("0.05");
    expect(minorToDecimalString(-5, "EUR")).toBe("-0.05");
    expect(minorToDecimalString(0, "EUR")).toBe("0.00");
    expect(minorToDecimalString(-0, "EUR")).toBe("0.00");
    expect(minorToDecimalString(500, "JPY")).toBe("500");
    expect(minorToDecimalString(-7, "JPY")).toBe("-7");
    expect(minorToDecimalString(1234, "BHD")).toBe("1.234");
    expect(minorToDecimalString(7, "BHD")).toBe("0.007");
  });

  it("accepts bigint beyond the safe integer range", () => {
    expect(minorToDecimalString(12345678901234567890n, "EUR")).toBe("123456789012345678.90");
    expect(minorToDecimalString(-12345678901234567890n, "EUR")).toBe("-123456789012345678.90");
  });

  it("rejects numbers that are not safe integers", () => {
    expect(() => minorToDecimalString(1.5, "EUR")).toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(() => minorToDecimalString(Number.NaN, "EUR")).toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(() => minorToDecimalString(2 ** 53, "EUR")).toThrow(RangeError);
  });

  it("round-trips with parseDecimalToMinor", () => {
    for (const currency of ["EUR", "JPY", "BHD"]) {
      for (const minor of [0, 1, -1, 99, 100, -100, 123456, -987654321, Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER]) {
        expect(parseDecimalToMinor(minorToDecimalString(minor, currency), currency)).toBe(minor);
      }
    }
  });
});

describe("formatMoney", () => {
  it("formats it-IT with grouping from four digits and the Intl spacing", () => {
    expect(formatMoney(123450, "EUR", "it-IT")).toBe(`1.234,50${NBSP}€`);
    expect(formatMoney(99, "EUR", "it-IT")).toBe(`0,99${NBSP}€`);
    expect(formatMoney(-123450, "EUR", "it-IT")).toBe(`-1.234,50${NBSP}€`);
    expect(formatMoney(123450, "USD", "it-IT")).toBe(`1.234,50${NBSP}USD`);
  });

  it("formats en-GB", () => {
    expect(formatMoney(123450, "EUR", "en-GB")).toBe("€1,234.50");
    expect(formatMoney(-123450, "EUR", "en-GB")).toBe("-€1,234.50");
    expect(formatMoney(99, "EUR", "en-GB")).toBe("€0.99");
    expect(formatMoney(123450, "GBP", "en-GB")).toBe("£1,234.50");
  });

  it("accepts bigint input", () => {
    expect(formatMoney(123450n, "EUR", "en-GB")).toBe("€1,234.50");
    expect(formatMoney(-5n, "EUR", "en-GB")).toBe("-€0.05");
  });

  it("is exact beyond double precision", () => {
    expect(formatMoney(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, "EUR", "en-GB")).toBe("€90,071,992,547,409.91");
    expect(formatMoney(123456789012345678901n, "EUR", "en-GB")).toBe(
      "€1,234,567,890,123,456,789.01",
    );
  });

  it("follows the currency's minor digits (JPY none, BHD three)", () => {
    expect(formatMoney(1234, "JPY", "en-GB")).toBe("JP¥1,234");
    expect(formatMoney(1234, "JPY", "it-IT")).toBe(`1.234${NBSP}JPY`);
    expect(formatMoney(-500, "JPY", "en-GB")).toBe("-JP¥500");
    expect(formatMoney(1234, "BHD", "en-GB")).toBe(`BHD${NBSP}1.234`);
    expect(formatMoney(1234, "BHD", "it-IT")).toBe(`1,234${NBSP}BHD`);
    expect(formatMoney(-1234, "BHD", "en-GB")).toBe(`-BHD${NBSP}1.234`);
  });

  it("never shows a minus for zero, including -0", () => {
    expect(formatMoney(0, "EUR", "en-GB")).toBe("€0.00");
    expect(formatMoney(-0, "EUR", "en-GB")).toBe("€0.00");
    expect(formatMoney(-0, "EUR", "it-IT")).toBe(`0,00${NBSP}€`);
    expect(formatMoney(0, "EUR", "en-GB", { sign: "always" })).toBe("€0.00");
  });

  it("supports the sign modes", () => {
    expect(formatMoney(123450, "EUR", "en-GB", { sign: "always" })).toBe("+€1,234.50");
    expect(formatMoney(-123450, "EUR", "en-GB", { sign: "always" })).toBe("-€1,234.50");
    expect(formatMoney(123450, "EUR", "it-IT", { sign: "always" })).toBe(`+1.234,50${NBSP}€`);
    expect(formatMoney(-123450, "EUR", "en-GB", { sign: "never" })).toBe("€1,234.50");
    expect(formatMoney(-123450, "EUR", "it-IT", { sign: "never" })).toBe(`1.234,50${NBSP}€`);
    expect(formatMoney(-123450, "EUR", "en-GB", { sign: "auto" })).toBe("-€1,234.50");
  });

  it("masks without any digit", () => {
    expect(MASKED_AMOUNT).toBe("•••••");
    expect(formatMoney(123450, "EUR", "it-IT", { masked: true })).toBe(MASKED_AMOUNT);
    expect(formatMoney(-5, "JPY", "en-GB", { masked: true, sign: "always" })).toBe(MASKED_AMOUNT);
  });

  it("rejects a number that is not a safe integer and an invalid currency", () => {
    expect(() => formatMoney(12.5, "EUR", "en-GB")).toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(() => formatMoney(100, "EURO", "en-GB")).toThrow(RangeError);
  });
});

describe("sumMinor", () => {
  it("adds integers exactly", () => {
    expect(sumMinor([])).toBe(0);
    expect(sumMinor([1000, -250, 5])).toBe(755);
    expect(sumMinor([Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, -Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER])).toBe(0);
  });

  it("tolerates an unsafe intermediate total when the result is safe", () => {
    expect(sumMinor([Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, 10, -10])).toBe(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER);
  });

  it("throws when the result or an input is not a safe integer", () => {
    expect(() => sumMinor([Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, 1])).toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(() => sumMinor([-Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, -1])).toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(() => sumMinor([1, 0.5])).toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(() => sumMinor([Number.NaN])).toThrow(RangeError);
  });
});
```

Create `packages/shared/src/dates.test.ts`:

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import {
  addDays,
  calendarDaysUntil,
  diffDays,
  formatAbsolute,
  formatLocalDate,
  formatRelative,
  formatRelativeDay,
  localDateSchema,
  localTimeOfDay,
  RELATIVE_LIMIT_DAYS,
  startOfLocalDay,
  toLocalDate,
} from "./dates";

const ROME = "Europe/Rome";
const NEW_YORK = "America/New_York";
const HOUR = 3_600_000;
const iso = (value: string) => Date.parse(value);

describe("localDateSchema", () => {
  it("accepts real calendar dates", () => {
    for (const date of ["2026-11-09", "2024-02-29", "2000-02-29", "2026-12-31", "0999-01-01"]) {
      expect(localDateSchema.safeParse(date).success).toBe(true);
    }
  });

  it("rejects malformed strings and dates that do not exist", () => {
    for (const date of [
      "2026-02-29",
      "1900-02-29",
      "2026-13-01",
      "2026-00-10",
      "2026-04-31",
      "2026-11-00",
      "2026-1-9",
      "26-11-09",
      "2026/11/09",
      "2026-11-09T00:00:00Z",
      " 2026-11-09",
      "",
    ]) {
      expect(localDateSchema.safeParse(date).success, date).toBe(false);
    }
  });
});

describe("toLocalDate", () => {
  it("resolves the calendar date in the given time zone", () => {
    const instant = iso("2026-11-09T23:30:00Z");
    expect(toLocalDate(instant, "UTC")).toBe("2026-11-09");
    expect(toLocalDate(instant, ROME)).toBe("2026-11-10");
    expect(toLocalDate(instant, NEW_YORK)).toBe("2026-11-09");
    expect(toLocalDate(new Date(instant), ROME)).toBe("2026-11-10");
  });

  it("switches exactly at local midnight", () => {
    // Rome is UTC+1 in November: local midnight is 23:00 UTC.
    expect(toLocalDate(iso("2026-11-09T22:59:59.999Z"), ROME)).toBe("2026-11-09");
    expect(toLocalDate(iso("2026-11-09T23:00:00.000Z"), ROME)).toBe("2026-11-10");
    // New York is UTC-5 in November: local midnight is 05:00 UTC.
    expect(toLocalDate(iso("2026-11-10T04:59:59.999Z"), NEW_YORK)).toBe("2026-11-09");
    expect(toLocalDate(iso("2026-11-10T05:00:00.000Z"), NEW_YORK)).toBe("2026-11-10");
  });

  it("rejects an invalid instant", () => {
    expect(() => toLocalDate(Number.NaN, ROME)).toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(() => toLocalDate(new Date("nope"), ROME)).toThrow(RangeError);
  });
});

describe("addDays and diffDays", () => {
  it("crosses month, year and leap-day boundaries", () => {
    expect(addDays("2026-11-09", 1)).toBe("2026-11-10");
    expect(addDays("2026-11-30", 1)).toBe("2026-12-01");
    expect(addDays("2026-12-31", 1)).toBe("2027-01-01");
    expect(addDays("2027-01-01", -1)).toBe("2026-12-31");
    expect(addDays("2024-02-28", 1)).toBe("2024-02-29");
    expect(addDays("2026-02-28", 1)).toBe("2026-03-01");
    expect(addDays("2026-11-09", 0)).toBe("2026-11-09");
    expect(addDays("2026-11-09", 365)).toBe("2027-11-09");
    expect(addDays("2026-11-09", -45)).toBe("2026-09-25");
  });

  it("counts whole days in either direction", () => {
    expect(diffDays("2026-11-10", "2026-11-09")).toBe(1);
    expect(diffDays("2026-11-09", "2026-11-10")).toBe(-1);
    expect(diffDays("2026-11-09", "2026-11-09")).toBe(0);
    expect(diffDays("2027-01-01", "2026-01-01")).toBe(365);
    expect(diffDays("2025-03-01", "2024-03-01")).toBe(365);
    expect(diffDays("2024-03-01", "2023-03-01")).toBe(366);
  });

  it("agrees with itself for every day of a leap year", () => {
    let date = "2024-01-01";
    for (let index = 0; index < 366; index += 1) {
      expect(diffDays(date, "2024-01-01")).toBe(index);
      expect(addDays("2024-01-01", index)).toBe(date);
      date = addDays(date, 1);
    }
    expect(date).toBe("2025-01-01");
  });

  it("rejects invalid dates and fractional day counts", () => {
    expect(() => addDays("2026-02-30", 1)).toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(() => addDays("nope", 1)).toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(() => addDays("2026-11-09", 1.5)).toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(() => diffDays("2026-13-01", "2026-01-01")).toThrow(RangeError);
  });
});

describe("startOfLocalDay", () => {
  it("returns the first instant of the local day", () => {
    expect(startOfLocalDay("2026-11-09", "UTC")).toBe(iso("2026-11-09T00:00:00Z"));
    expect(startOfLocalDay("2026-11-09", ROME)).toBe(iso("2026-11-08T23:00:00Z"));
    expect(startOfLocalDay("2026-07-09", ROME)).toBe(iso("2026-07-08T22:00:00Z"));
    expect(startOfLocalDay("2026-11-09", NEW_YORK)).toBe(iso("2026-11-09T05:00:00Z"));
  });

  it("handles the 23-hour and 25-hour days in Europe/Rome", () => {
    const springStart = startOfLocalDay("2026-03-29", ROME);
    const springEnd = startOfLocalDay("2026-03-30", ROME);
    expect(springStart).toBe(iso("2026-03-28T23:00:00Z"));
    expect(springEnd).toBe(iso("2026-03-29T22:00:00Z"));
    expect((springEnd - springStart) / HOUR).toBe(23);

    const autumnStart = startOfLocalDay("2026-10-25", ROME);
    const autumnEnd = startOfLocalDay("2026-10-26", ROME);
    expect(autumnStart).toBe(iso("2026-10-24T22:00:00Z"));
    expect(autumnEnd).toBe(iso("2026-10-25T23:00:00Z"));
    expect((autumnEnd - autumnStart) / HOUR).toBe(25);
  });

  it("handles the 23-hour and 25-hour days in America/New_York", () => {
    const springStart = startOfLocalDay("2026-03-08", NEW_YORK);
    const springEnd = startOfLocalDay("2026-03-09", NEW_YORK);
    expect(springStart).toBe(iso("2026-03-08T05:00:00Z"));
    expect(springEnd).toBe(iso("2026-03-09T04:00:00Z"));
    expect((springEnd - springStart) / HOUR).toBe(23);

    const autumnStart = startOfLocalDay("2026-11-01", NEW_YORK);
    const autumnEnd = startOfLocalDay("2026-11-02", NEW_YORK);
    expect(autumnStart).toBe(iso("2026-11-01T04:00:00Z"));
    expect(autumnEnd).toBe(iso("2026-11-02T05:00:00Z"));
    expect((autumnEnd - autumnStart) / HOUR).toBe(25);
  });

  it.each([
    [ROME, 2026],
    [ROME, 2024],
    [NEW_YORK, 2026],
    [NEW_YORK, 2024],
  ])("round-trips with toLocalDate for every day of %s %d", (timeZone, year) => {
    let date = `${year}-01-01`;
    while (date < `${year + 1}-01-01`) {
      const start = startOfLocalDay(date, timeZone);
      expect(toLocalDate(start, timeZone), date).toBe(date);
      expect(toLocalDate(start - 1, timeZone), date).toBe(addDays(date, -1));
      date = addDays(date, 1);
    }
  });

  it("rejects an invalid date", () => {
    expect(() => startOfLocalDay("2026-02-30", ROME)).toThrow(RangeError);
  });
});

describe("localTimeOfDay", () => {
  it("formats HH:MM in the time zone", () => {
    expect(localTimeOfDay(iso("2026-11-09T13:05:00Z"), ROME)).toBe("14:05");
    expect(localTimeOfDay(iso("2026-11-09T13:05:00Z"), NEW_YORK)).toBe("08:05");
    expect(localTimeOfDay(new Date("2026-07-09T13:05:00Z"), ROME)).toBe("15:05");
  });

  it("shows midnight as 00:00, never 24:00", () => {
    expect(localTimeOfDay(iso("2026-11-09T23:00:00Z"), ROME)).toBe("00:00");
    expect(localTimeOfDay(iso("2026-11-09T23:30:00Z"), ROME)).toBe("00:30");
    expect(localTimeOfDay(iso("2026-11-10T05:00:00Z"), NEW_YORK)).toBe("00:00");
  });

  it("skips the hour that does not exist on a spring-forward day", () => {
    expect(localTimeOfDay(iso("2026-03-29T00:59:00Z"), ROME)).toBe("01:59");
    expect(localTimeOfDay(iso("2026-03-29T01:00:00Z"), ROME)).toBe("03:00");
  });
});

describe("calendarDaysUntil", () => {
  const now = iso("2026-11-09T10:00:00Z"); // 11:00 in Rome

  it("is 0 for later today and for earlier today", () => {
    expect(calendarDaysUntil(iso("2026-11-09T21:00:00Z"), now, ROME)).toBe(0);
    expect(calendarDaysUntil(iso("2026-11-08T23:30:00Z"), now, ROME)).toBe(0);
  });

  it("counts calendar days, not 24-hour blocks", () => {
    // 23:50 in Rome now, tomorrow at 00:30 is 40 minutes away and already day 1.
    expect(calendarDaysUntil(iso("2026-11-09T23:30:00Z"), iso("2026-11-09T22:50:00Z"), ROME)).toBe(
      1,
    );
    // The same target seen from New York is still today.
    expect(
      calendarDaysUntil(iso("2026-11-09T23:30:00Z"), iso("2026-11-09T22:50:00Z"), NEW_YORK),
    ).toBe(0);
    expect(calendarDaysUntil(iso("2026-11-10T22:59:00Z"), now, ROME)).toBe(1);
    expect(calendarDaysUntil(iso("2026-11-10T23:00:00Z"), now, ROME)).toBe(2);
  });

  it("is negative in the past", () => {
    expect(calendarDaysUntil(iso("2026-11-08T22:30:00Z"), now, ROME)).toBe(-1);
    expect(calendarDaysUntil(iso("2026-10-10T10:00:00Z"), now, ROME)).toBe(-30);
  });

  it("accepts Date objects", () => {
    expect(calendarDaysUntil(new Date("2026-11-12T10:00:00Z"), new Date(now), ROME)).toBe(3);
  });

  it("stays correct across a spring-forward change (23-hour day)", () => {
    // Saturday 21:00 in Rome (20:00 UTC) to Monday 00:30 CEST (22:30 UTC on Sunday): 2 calendar days, 25.5 hours.
    expect(calendarDaysUntil(iso("2026-03-29T22:30:00Z"), iso("2026-03-28T20:00:00Z"), ROME)).toBe(
      2,
    );
    // Sunday 23:30 CEST to Monday 00:10 CEST is 1 day.
    expect(calendarDaysUntil(iso("2026-03-29T22:10:00Z"), iso("2026-03-29T21:30:00Z"), ROME)).toBe(
      1,
    );
  });

  it("stays correct across a fall-back change (25-hour day)", () => {
    // Sunday 25 October 2026 has 25 hours: 00:30 CEST and 23:30 CET are the same calendar day.
    expect(calendarDaysUntil(iso("2026-10-25T22:30:00Z"), iso("2026-10-24T22:30:00Z"), ROME)).toBe(
      0,
    );
    expect(calendarDaysUntil(iso("2026-10-25T23:30:00Z"), iso("2026-10-24T22:30:00Z"), ROME)).toBe(
      1,
    );
  });

  it("stays correct across New York DST changes", () => {
    expect(
      calendarDaysUntil(iso("2026-03-09T04:30:00Z"), iso("2026-03-08T05:30:00Z"), NEW_YORK),
    ).toBe(1);
    expect(
      calendarDaysUntil(iso("2026-11-02T04:59:00Z"), iso("2026-11-01T03:59:00Z"), NEW_YORK),
    ).toBe(1);
  });
});

describe("formatAbsolute and formatLocalDate", () => {
  const instant = iso("2026-11-09T13:30:00Z");

  it("formats the date in the time zone and locale", () => {
    expect(formatAbsolute(instant, "en-GB", ROME)).toBe("9 Nov 2026");
    expect(formatAbsolute(instant, "it-IT", ROME)).toBe("9 nov 2026");

    expect(formatAbsolute(instant, "it-IT", ROME, { withTime: true })).toBe("9 nov 2026, 14:30");
    expect(formatAbsolute(instant, "en-GB", NEW_YORK, { withTime: true })).toBe(
      "9 Nov 2026, 08:30",
    );
    expect(formatAbsolute(instant, "en-GB", ROME, { withTime: false })).toBe("9 Nov 2026");
  });

  it("formats a LocalDate without any time zone shift", () => {
    expect(formatLocalDate("2026-11-09", "en-GB")).toBe("9 Nov 2026");
    expect(formatLocalDate("2026-11-09", "it-IT")).toBe("9 nov 2026");
    expect(formatLocalDate("2026-11-09", "en-GB", { style: "short" })).toBe("09/11/2026");
    expect(formatLocalDate("2026-11-09", "it-IT", { style: "short" })).toBe("09/11/2026");
    expect(formatLocalDate("2026-11-09", "en-GB", { style: "long" })).toBe("9 November 2026");
    expect(formatLocalDate("2026-11-09", "it-IT", { style: "long" })).toBe("9 novembre 2026");
  });

  it("adds the weekday on request", () => {
    expect(formatLocalDate("2026-11-09", "en-GB", { weekday: true })).toBe("Mon, 9 Nov 2026");
    expect(formatLocalDate("2026-11-09", "it-IT", { weekday: true })).toBe("lun 9 nov 2026");
    expect(formatLocalDate("2026-11-09", "en-GB", { style: "long", weekday: true })).toBe(
      "Monday, 9 November 2026",
    );
    expect(formatLocalDate("2026-11-09", "it-IT", { style: "long", weekday: true })).toBe(
      "lunedì 9 novembre 2026",
    );
  });

  it("rejects an invalid LocalDate", () => {
    expect(() => formatLocalDate("2026-02-30", "en-GB")).toThrow(RangeError);
  });
});

describe("formatRelative", () => {
  const now = iso("2026-11-09T12:00:00Z"); // 13:00 in Rome
  const relative = (instant: number, locale: string, timeZone = ROME, at = now) =>
    formatRelative(instant, at, locale, timeZone);

  it("says now for less than a minute, in both directions", () => {
    expect(relative(now, "en-GB")).toBe("now");
    expect(relative(now - 59_000, "en-GB")).toBe("now");
    expect(relative(now + 59_000, "en-GB")).toBe("now");
    expect(relative(now - 30_000, "it-IT")).toBe("ora");
  });

  it("uses minutes below an hour", () => {
    expect(relative(now - 5 * 60_000, "en-GB")).toBe("5 minutes ago");
    expect(relative(now - 5 * 60_000, "it-IT")).toBe("5 minuti fa");
    expect(relative(now - 60_000, "en-GB")).toBe("1 minute ago");
    expect(relative(now - 59 * 60_000 - 59_000, "en-GB")).toBe("59 minutes ago");
    expect(relative(now + 10 * 60_000, "en-GB")).toBe("in 10 minutes");
    expect(relative(now + 10 * 60_000, "it-IT")).toBe("tra 10 minuti");
  });

  it("uses hours below a day, also across midnight", () => {
    expect(relative(now - HOUR, "en-GB")).toBe("1 hour ago");
    expect(relative(now - 3 * HOUR, "en-GB")).toBe("3 hours ago");
    expect(relative(now - 3 * HOUR, "it-IT")).toBe("3 ore fa");
    expect(relative(now + 2 * HOUR, "en-GB")).toBe("in 2 hours");
    expect(relative(now + 2 * HOUR, "it-IT")).toBe("tra 2 ore");
    expect(relative(now - 23 * HOUR - 59 * 60_000, "en-GB")).toBe("23 hours ago");
    // 00:20 in Rome, an instant at 23:50 the evening before is 30 minutes ago, not "yesterday".
    const justAfterMidnight = iso("2026-11-09T23:20:00Z");
    expect(relative(iso("2026-11-09T22:50:00Z"), "en-GB", ROME, justAfterMidnight)).toBe(
      "30 minutes ago",
    );
  });

  it("uses calendar days in the time zone from 24 hours on", () => {
    expect(relative(now - 24 * HOUR, "en-GB")).toBe("yesterday");
    expect(relative(now - 24 * HOUR, "it-IT")).toBe("ieri");
    expect(relative(now + 24 * HOUR, "en-GB")).toBe("tomorrow");
    expect(relative(now + 24 * HOUR, "it-IT")).toBe("domani");
    expect(relative(now + 3 * 24 * HOUR, "en-GB")).toBe("in 3 days");
    expect(relative(now + 3 * 24 * HOUR, "it-IT")).toBe("tra 3 giorni");
    expect(relative(now - 10 * 24 * HOUR, "en-GB")).toBe("10 days ago");
    expect(relative(now - 10 * 24 * HOUR, "it-IT")).toBe("10 giorni fa");
  });

  it("counts calendar days near local midnight", () => {
    // 00:30 in Rome on 10 November. An instant at 23:45 on 8 November is 24 h 45 min ago
    // and two calendar days back; in New York both fall on the same evening, one day apart.
    const late = iso("2026-11-09T23:30:00Z");
    const evening = iso("2026-11-08T22:45:00Z");
    expect(relative(evening, "en-GB", ROME, late)).toBe("2 days ago");
    expect(relative(evening, "en-GB", NEW_YORK, late)).toBe("yesterday");
    // 24 h 45 min ahead of 23:15 on the 9th (Rome) lands on the 11th, two days ahead.
    const early = iso("2026-11-09T22:15:00Z");
    expect(relative(iso("2026-11-10T23:00:00Z"), "en-GB", ROME, early)).toBe("in 2 days");
    expect(relative(iso("2026-11-10T23:00:00Z"), "en-GB", NEW_YORK, early)).toBe("tomorrow");
  });

  it("counts calendar days across the Rome DST changes", () => {
    // Exactly 24 hours apart, but 00:30 CEST on the 30th is two calendar days after 23:30 CET on the 28th.
    expect(
      formatRelative(iso("2026-03-28T22:30:00Z"), iso("2026-03-29T22:30:00Z"), "en-GB", ROME),
    ).toBe("2 days ago");
    // Autumn: the 25-hour day keeps the same calendar day for 24 hours.
    expect(
      formatRelative(iso("2026-10-24T22:30:00Z"), iso("2026-10-25T22:30:00Z"), "en-GB", ROME),
    ).toBe("today");
    expect(
      formatRelative(iso("2026-10-24T22:30:00Z"), iso("2026-10-25T23:30:00Z"), "en-GB", ROME),
    ).toBe("yesterday");
  });

  it("switches to the absolute date at 45 calendar days, in both directions", () => {
    expect(RELATIVE_LIMIT_DAYS).toBe(45);
    expect(relative(iso("2026-09-26T12:00:00Z"), "en-GB")).toBe("44 days ago");
    expect(relative(iso("2026-09-25T12:00:00Z"), "en-GB")).toBe("25 Sept 2026");
    expect(relative(iso("2026-09-25T12:00:00Z"), "it-IT")).toBe("25 set 2026");
    expect(relative(iso("2026-09-01T12:00:00Z"), "en-GB")).toBe("1 Sept 2026");
    expect(relative(iso("2026-12-23T12:00:00Z"), "en-GB")).toBe("in 44 days");
    expect(relative(iso("2026-12-24T12:00:00Z"), "en-GB")).toBe("24 Dec 2026");
    expect(relative(iso("2026-12-24T12:00:00Z"), "it-IT")).toBe("24 dic 2026");
    expect(relative(iso("2026-12-24T12:00:00Z"), "en-GB")).toBe(
      formatAbsolute(iso("2026-12-24T12:00:00Z"), "en-GB", ROME),
    );
  });

  it("accepts Date objects and rejects invalid ones", () => {
    expect(formatRelative(new Date(now - HOUR), new Date(now), "en-GB", ROME)).toBe("1 hour ago");
    expect(() => formatRelative(Number.NaN, now, "en-GB", ROME)).toThrow(RangeError);
  });
});

describe("formatRelativeDay", () => {
  it("names nearby calendar days in sentence case and prints older ones as dates", () => {
    const today = "2026-11-09";
    expect(formatRelativeDay(today, today, "en-GB")).toBe("Today");
    expect(formatRelativeDay("2026-11-08", today, "en-GB")).toBe("Yesterday");
    expect(formatRelativeDay("2026-11-06", today, "en-GB")).toBe("3 days ago");
    expect(formatRelativeDay("2026-11-11", today, "en-GB")).toBe("In 2 days");
    expect(formatRelativeDay("2026-11-08", today, "it-IT")).toBe("Ieri");
    expect(formatRelativeDay("2026-09-26", today, "en-GB")).toBe("44 days ago");
    expect(formatRelativeDay("2026-09-25", today, "en-GB")).toBe(
      formatLocalDate("2026-09-25", "en-GB", { style: "medium" }),
    );
    expect(() => formatRelativeDay("2026-02-30", today, "en-GB")).toThrow(RangeError);
  });
});
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Implement `money.ts`**

Create `packages/shared/src/money.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * Money helpers. Amounts are integer minor units (a JS `number` that must be a safe integer, or a
 * `bigint`) plus an ISO 4217 currency code. Nothing here uses floating-point arithmetic on amounts:
 * parsing and formatting go through exact decimal strings.
 */

/** Thrown by `parseDecimalToMinor` when the input is not an exactly representable amount. */
export class MoneyParseError extends Error {
  constructor(message: string) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "MoneyParseError";
  }
}

/** What privacy mode shows instead of an amount. */
export const MASKED_AMOUNT = "•••••";

const minorDigitsCache = new Map<string, number>();

/**
 * Number of minor-unit digits of a currency (EUR 2, JPY 0, BHD 3), as known to `Intl`.
 * Throws `RangeError` when `currency` is not a well-formed ISO 4217 code.
 */
export function currencyMinorDigits(currency: string): number {
  const code = currency.toUpperCase();
  const cached = minorDigitsCache.get(code);
  if (cached !== undefined) return cached;
  const digits = new Intl.NumberFormat("en", {
    style: "currency",
    currency: code,
  }).resolvedOptions().maximumFractionDigits;
  if (digits === undefined) throw new RangeError("Unsupported currency");
  minorDigitsCache.set(code, digits);
  return digits;
}

const DECIMAL_PATTERN = /^([+-]?)(\d+)(?:\.(\d+))?$/;
const MAX_SAFE_BIGINT = BigInt(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER);

/**
 * Converts a provider decimal string ("12.30", "-0.5", "+7") to integer minor units.
 *
 * Only plain decimals with a `.` separator are accepted. Digits beyond the currency's minor digits
 * are accepted only when they are zeros ("1.230" EUR is fine, "1.234" EUR throws), so no amount is
 * ever silently rounded. Throws `MoneyParseError` for anything else and `RangeError` for an invalid
 * currency code. "-0" becomes `0`.
 */
export function parseDecimalToMinor(amount: string, currency: string): number {
  const digits = currencyMinorDigits(currency);
  const match = DECIMAL_PATTERN.exec(amount.trim());
  if (!match) throw new MoneyParseError("Invalid decimal amount");
  const sign = match[1];
  const integerPart = match[2] ?? "";
  const fraction = match[3] ?? "";
  if (/[1-9]/.test(fraction.slice(digits))) {
    throw new MoneyParseError("Amount has more decimals than the currency allows");
  }
  const minor = BigInt(integerPart + fraction.slice(0, digits).padEnd(digits, "0"));
  if (minor > MAX_SAFE_BIGINT) throw new MoneyParseError("Amount is too large");
  const value = Number(minor);
  return sign === "-" && value !== 0 ? -value : value;
}

function toBigInt(minor: bigint | number): bigint {
  if (typeof minor === "bigint") return minor;
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(minor)) throw new RangeError("Amount is not a safe integer");
  return BigInt(minor);
}

/** Exact decimal string of an amount in minor units: `-1234` EUR becomes `"-12.34"`, JPY `500` becomes `"500"`. */
export function minorToDecimalString(minor: bigint | number, currency: string): string {
  const digits = currencyMinorDigits(currency);
  const value = toBigInt(minor);
  const negative = value < 0n;
  const padded = (negative ? -value : value).toString().padStart(digits + 1, "0");
  const text = digits === 0 ? padded : `${padded.slice(0, -digits)}.${padded.slice(-digits)}`;
  return negative ? `-${text}` : text;
}

export interface FormatMoneyOptions {
  /** `auto` shows a minus for negatives only, `always` also shows a plus for positives, `never` formats the absolute value. */
  sign?: "auto" | "always" | "never";
  /** Returns `MASKED_AMOUNT` and no digits (privacy mode). */
  masked?: boolean;
}

const SIGN_DISPLAY = { auto: "auto", always: "exceptZero", never: "never" } as const;
const numberFormatCache = new Map<string, Intl.NumberFormat>();

function currencyFormatter(
  locale: string,
  currency: string,
  signDisplay: (typeof SIGN_DISPLAY)[keyof typeof SIGN_DISPLAY],
): Intl.NumberFormat {
  const key = `${locale}|${currency}|${signDisplay}`;
  let formatter = numberFormatCache.get(key);
  if (!formatter) {
    formatter = new Intl.NumberFormat(locale, {
      style: "currency",
      currency,
      signDisplay,
      // CLDR's it-IT data skips the thousands separator below 10 000 ("1234,50 €"); amounts in a
      // column must group alike, so grouping is forced.
      useGrouping: "always",
    });
    numberFormatCache.set(key, formatter);
  }
  return formatter;
}

/**
 * Formats integer minor units for display. The exact decimal string is handed to
 * `Intl.NumberFormat.format`, which formats strings without going through a double.
 */
export function formatMoney(
  minor: bigint | number,
  currency: string,
  locale: string,
  options: FormatMoneyOptions = {},
): string {
  if (options.masked) return MASKED_AMOUNT;
  const sign = options.sign ?? "auto";
  const decimal = minorToDecimalString(minor, currency.toUpperCase());
  return currencyFormatter(locale, currency.toUpperCase(), SIGN_DISPLAY[sign]).format(
    decimal as `${number}`,
  );
}

/** Exact sum of minor-unit amounts. Throws `RangeError` when an input or the result is not a safe integer. */
export function sumMinor(values: readonly number[]): number {
  let total = 0n;
  for (const value of values) total += toBigInt(value);
  if (total > MAX_SAFE_BIGINT || total < -MAX_SAFE_BIGINT) {
    throw new RangeError("Sum is not a safe integer");
  }
  return Number(total);
}
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Implement `dates.ts`**

Create `packages/shared/src/dates.ts`:

```ts
import { z } from "zod";

/**
 * Calendar dates and instants. Instants are epoch milliseconds (or `Date`); a calendar date is a
 * `LocalDate` string `YYYY-MM-DD` that belongs to a time zone chosen by the caller (the `TZ`
 * setting). Day arithmetic works on the proleptic Gregorian calendar with integers only, so it is
 * independent of the process time zone and of daylight saving time.
 */

/** `YYYY-MM-DD`. */
export type LocalDate = string;

/** From this many calendar days away `formatRelative` switches to an absolute date (UX doc §6). */
export const RELATIVE_LIMIT_DAYS = 45;

const MS_PER_MINUTE = 60_000;
const MS_PER_HOUR = 3_600_000;
const MS_PER_DAY = 86_400_000;
const LOCAL_DATE_PATTERN = /^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})$/;

interface Civil {
  year: number;
  month: number;
  day: number;
}

function isLeapYear(year: number): boolean {
  return (year % 4 === 0 && year % 100 !== 0) || year % 400 === 0;
}

function daysInMonth(year: number, month: number): number {
  if (month === 2) return isLeapYear(year) ? 29 : 28;
  return month === 4 || month === 6 || month === 9 || month === 11 ? 30 : 31;
}

function parseCivil(date: string): Civil | null {
  const match = LOCAL_DATE_PATTERN.exec(date);
  if (!match) return null;
  const year = Number(match[1]);
  const month = Number(match[2]);
  const day = Number(match[3]);
  if (month < 1 || month > 12 || day < 1 || day > daysInMonth(year, month)) return null;
  return { year, month, day };
}

function requireCivil(date: string): Civil {
  const civil = parseCivil(date);
  if (!civil) throw new RangeError("Invalid local date");
  return civil;
}

/** Days since 1970-01-01 for a civil date (Howard Hinnant's algorithm). */
function daysFromCivil({ year, month, day }: Civil): number {
  const y = month <= 2 ? year - 1 : year;
  const era = Math.floor(y / 400);
  const yearOfEra = y - era * 400;
  const dayOfYear = Math.floor((153 * ((month + 9) % 12) + 2) / 5) + day - 1;
  const dayOfEra =
    yearOfEra * 365 + Math.floor(yearOfEra / 4) - Math.floor(yearOfEra / 100) + dayOfYear;
  return era * 146_097 + dayOfEra - 719_468;
}

function civilFromDays(days: number): Civil {
  const z = days + 719_468;
  const era = Math.floor(z / 146_097);
  const dayOfEra = z - era * 146_097;
  const yearOfEra = Math.floor(
    (dayOfEra -
      Math.floor(dayOfEra / 1460) +
      Math.floor(dayOfEra / 36_524) -
      Math.floor(dayOfEra / 146_096)) /
      365,
  );
  const dayOfYear =
    dayOfEra - (365 * yearOfEra + Math.floor(yearOfEra / 4) - Math.floor(yearOfEra / 100));
  const monthIndex = Math.floor((5 * dayOfYear + 2) / 153);
  const day = dayOfYear - Math.floor((153 * monthIndex + 2) / 5) + 1;
  const month = monthIndex < 10 ? monthIndex + 3 : monthIndex - 9;
  return { year: yearOfEra + era * 400 + (month <= 2 ? 1 : 0), month, day };
}

function formatCivil({ year, month, day }: Civil): LocalDate {
  return `${String(year).padStart(4, "0")}-${String(month).padStart(2, "0")}-${String(day).padStart(2, "0")}`;
}

/** A `YYYY-MM-DD` string that is also a real calendar date (no 2026-02-30). */
export const localDateSchema = z
  .string()
  .regex(LOCAL_DATE_PATTERN, "Expected YYYY-MM-DD")
  .refine((value) => parseCivil(value) !== null, "Not a calendar date");

function toMs(instant: Date | number): number {
  const ms = typeof instant === "number" ? instant : instant.getTime();
  if (!Number.isFinite(ms)) throw new RangeError("Invalid instant");
  return ms;
}

const partsFormatterCache = new Map<string, Intl.DateTimeFormat>();

function partsFormatter(timeZone: string): Intl.DateTimeFormat {
  let formatter = partsFormatterCache.get(timeZone);
  if (!formatter) {
    formatter = new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", {
      timeZone,
      calendar: "gregory",
      numberingSystem: "latn",
      hourCycle: "h23",
      year: "numeric",
      month: "2-digit",
      day: "2-digit",
      hour: "2-digit",
      minute: "2-digit",
    });
    partsFormatterCache.set(timeZone, formatter);
  }
  return formatter;
}

function localParts(instant: Date | number, timeZone: string): Record<string, string> {
  const parts: Record<string, string> = {};
  for (const part of partsFormatter(timeZone).formatToParts(toMs(instant))) {
    parts[part.type] = part.value;
  }
  return parts;
}

/** The calendar date of an instant in a time zone. */
export function toLocalDate(instant: Date | number, timeZone: string): LocalDate {
  const parts = localParts(instant, timeZone);
  return `${(parts.year ?? "").padStart(4, "0")}-${parts.month}-${parts.day}`;
}

/** Adds (or subtracts) whole calendar days. Throws `RangeError` for an invalid date or a non-integer count. */
export function addDays(date: LocalDate, days: number): LocalDate {
  if (!Number.isInteger(days)) throw new RangeError("Days must be an integer");
  return formatCivil(civilFromDays(daysFromCivil(requireCivil(date)) + days));
}

/** `a - b` in whole calendar days. */
export function diffDays(a: LocalDate, b: LocalDate): number {
  return daysFromCivil(requireCivil(a)) - daysFromCivil(requireCivil(b));
}

/**
 * Epoch milliseconds of the first instant of a local day. Daylight saving time makes days 23 or 25
 * hours long (and a few zones skip midnight), so the instant is found by bisection on `toLocalDate`.
 */
export function startOfLocalDay(date: LocalDate, timeZone: string): number {
  const utcMidnight = daysFromCivil(requireCivil(date)) * MS_PER_DAY;
  // UTC offsets lie between -12:00 and +14:00, so the start of the day is inside this window.
  let before = utcMidnight - 15 * MS_PER_HOUR;
  let after = utcMidnight + 13 * MS_PER_HOUR;
  while (after - before > 1) {
    const middle = before + Math.floor((after - before) / 2);
    if (toLocalDate(middle, timeZone) >= date) after = middle;
    else before = middle;
  }
  return after;
}

/** `HH:MM` (24-hour) of an instant in a time zone. */
export function localTimeOfDay(instant: Date | number, timeZone: string): string {
  const parts = localParts(instant, timeZone);
  const hour = parts.hour === "24" ? "00" : parts.hour;
  return `${hour}:${parts.minute}`;
}

/**
 * Local calendar days from `now` to `target`, negative when `target` is in the past. Later today is
 * 0 and tomorrow at 00:30 is 1 even when it is 40 minutes away.
 */
export function calendarDaysUntil(
  target: Date | number,
  now: Date | number,
  timeZone: string,
): number {
  return diffDays(toLocalDate(target, timeZone), toLocalDate(now, timeZone));
}

const relativeFormatCache = new Map<string, Intl.RelativeTimeFormat>();

function relativeFormatter(locale: string): Intl.RelativeTimeFormat {
  let formatter = relativeFormatCache.get(locale);
  if (!formatter) {
    formatter = new Intl.RelativeTimeFormat(locale, { numeric: "auto" });
    relativeFormatCache.set(locale, formatter);
  }
  return formatter;
}

/**
 * "now", "5 minutes ago", "in 3 hours", "yesterday", "in 3 days"; from 45 calendar days away in
 * either direction the absolute date (without time) instead. Minutes and hours are elapsed time,
 * days are local calendar days.
 */
export function formatRelative(
  instant: Date | number,
  now: Date | number,
  locale: string,
  timeZone: string,
): string {
  const delta = toMs(instant) - toMs(now);
  const elapsed = Math.abs(delta);
  const formatter = relativeFormatter(locale);
  if (elapsed < MS_PER_MINUTE) return formatter.format(0, "second");
  if (elapsed < MS_PER_HOUR) return formatter.format(Math.trunc(delta / MS_PER_MINUTE), "minute");
  if (elapsed < MS_PER_DAY) return formatter.format(Math.trunc(delta / MS_PER_HOUR), "hour");
  const days = calendarDaysUntil(instant, now, timeZone);
  if (Math.abs(days) >= RELATIVE_LIMIT_DAYS) return formatAbsolute(instant, locale, timeZone);
  return formatter.format(days, "day");
}

const absoluteFormatCache = new Map<string, Intl.DateTimeFormat>();

/** Absolute date ("9 Nov 2026"), with the time ("9 Nov 2026, 14:30") when `withTime` is set. */
export function formatAbsolute(
  instant: Date | number,
  locale: string,
  timeZone: string,
  options: { withTime?: boolean } = {},
): string {
  const withTime = options.withTime === true;
  const key = `${locale}|${timeZone}|${withTime}`;
  let formatter = absoluteFormatCache.get(key);
  if (!formatter) {
    formatter = new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, {
      timeZone,
      dateStyle: "medium",
      ...(withTime ? { timeStyle: "short" as const } : {}),
    });
    absoluteFormatCache.set(key, formatter);
  }
  return formatter.format(toMs(instant));
}

const LOCAL_DATE_FIELDS = {
  short: { day: "numeric", month: "numeric", year: "numeric" },
  medium: { day: "numeric", month: "short", year: "numeric" },
  long: { day: "numeric", month: "long", year: "numeric" },
} as const;

const localDateFormatCache = new Map<string, Intl.DateTimeFormat>();

/** Formats a `LocalDate` without any time zone shift ("9 Nov 2026", with `weekday`: "Mon 9 Nov 2026"). */
export function formatLocalDate(
  date: LocalDate,
  locale: string,
  options: { style?: "short" | "medium" | "long"; weekday?: boolean } = {},
): string {
  const style = options.style ?? "medium";
  const weekday = options.weekday === true;
  const ms = daysFromCivil(requireCivil(date)) * MS_PER_DAY;
  const key = `${locale}|${style}|${weekday}`;
  let formatter = localDateFormatCache.get(key);
  if (!formatter) {
    formatter = new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, {
      timeZone: "UTC",
      ...LOCAL_DATE_FIELDS[style],
      ...(weekday ? { weekday: style === "long" ? ("long" as const) : ("short" as const) } : {}),
    });
    localDateFormatCache.set(key, formatter);
  }
  return formatter.format(ms);
}

/**
 * A booking date relative to `today`, both calendar days (no time of day, so no time zone or DST
 * shift): "Today", "Yesterday", "3 days ago", "In 2 days" within `RELATIVE_LIMIT_DAYS`, the medium
 * date beyond. Sentence case, because it stands alone in a table cell.
 */
export function formatRelativeDay(date: LocalDate, today: LocalDate, locale: string): string {
  const days = diffDays(date, today);
  if (Math.abs(days) >= RELATIVE_LIMIT_DAYS) return formatLocalDate(date, locale, { style: "medium" });
  const label = new Intl.RelativeTimeFormat(locale, { numeric: "auto" }).format(days, "day");
  return label.charAt(0).toLocaleUpperCase(locale) + label.slice(1);
}
```

- [ ] **Step 7: Implement `iban.ts` and `text.ts`**

Create `packages/shared/src/iban.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * IBAN helpers. Validation checks the country's registered length and the ISO 7064 mod-97 checksum.
 * Masking keeps only what the panel may show: country, check digits and the last four characters.
 */

/** Total IBAN length per country, from the SWIFT IBAN registry: country code followed by the length. */
const IBAN_LENGTHS: ReadonlyMap<string, number> = new Map(
  `AD24 AE23 AL28 AT20 AZ28 BA20 BE16 BG22 BH22 BI27 BR29 BY28 CH21 CR22 CY28 CZ24
   DE22 DJ27 DK18 DO28 EE20 EG29 ES24 FI18 FK18 FO18 FR27 GB22 GE22 GI23 GL18 GR27
   GT28 HR21 HU28 IE22 IL23 IQ23 IS26 IT27 JO30 KW30 KZ20 LB28 LC32 LI21 LT20 LU20
   LV21 LY25 MC27 MD24 ME22 MK19 MN20 MR27 MT31 MU30 NI28 NL18 NO15 OM23 PK24 PL28
   PS29 PT25 QA29 RO24 RS22 RU33 SA24 SC31 SD18 SE24 SI19 SK24 SM27 SO23 ST25 SV28
   TL23 TN24 TR26 UA29 VA22 VG24 XK20 YE30`
    .split(/\s+/)
    .map((entry): [string, number] => [entry.slice(0, 2), Number(entry.slice(2))]),
);

const BULLET_GROUP = "••••";

/** Uppercase with every whitespace character removed. */
export function normalizeIban(value: string): string {
  return value.replace(/\s+/g, "").toUpperCase();
}

/** Remainder modulo 97 of the rearranged IBAN, digit by digit so no big number is needed. */
function mod97(rearranged: string): number {
  let remainder = 0;
  for (const char of rearranged) {
    const digits = char >= "A" && char <= "Z" ? String(char.charCodeAt(0) - 55) : char;
    for (const digit of digits) remainder = (remainder * 10 + Number(digit)) % 97;
  }
  return remainder;
}

/** True when the value (spaces and case ignored) has a registered length for its country and a valid checksum. */
export function isValidIban(value: string): boolean {
  const iban = normalizeIban(value);
  if (!/^[A-Z]{2}\d{2}[A-Z0-9]+$/.test(iban)) return false;
  if (IBAN_LENGTHS.get(iban.slice(0, 2)) !== iban.length) return false;
  const checkDigits = Number(iban.slice(2, 4));
  if (checkDigits < 2 || checkDigits > 98) return false;
  return mod97(iban.slice(4) + iban.slice(0, 4)) === 1;
}

/** Groups of four characters separated by spaces: `IT05 A010 …`. */
export function formatIban(iban: string): string {
  return (normalizeIban(iban).match(/.{1,4}/g) ?? []).join(" ");
}

/** Last four characters of an identifier (spaces and case ignored); the whole value when it is shorter. */
export function identifierLast4(identifier: string): string {
  return normalizeIban(identifier).slice(-4);
}

/** `•••• 1234` for identifiers that are not IBANs (card or account numbers). */
export function maskIdentifier(identifier: string): string {
  const last4 = identifierLast4(identifier);
  return last4 === "" ? BULLET_GROUP : `${BULLET_GROUP} ${last4}`;
}

/**
 * `IT05 •••• •••• 1234`: country and check digits, two fixed bullet groups whatever the length,
 * last four characters. Values too short to be an IBAN fall back to `maskIdentifier`.
 */
export function maskIban(iban: string): string {
  const normalized = normalizeIban(iban);
  if (normalized.length < 12) return maskIdentifier(normalized);
  return `${normalized.slice(0, 4)} ${BULLET_GROUP} ${BULLET_GROUP} ${normalized.slice(-4)}`;
}

/** Privacy mode: replaces the digits still visible in a masked IBAN or identifier with bullets (`IT•• •••• •••• ••••`). */
export function maskIbanDigitsForPrivacy(masked: string): string {
  return masked.replace(/\d/g, "•");
}
```

Create `packages/shared/src/text.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * Search normalisation shared by the server's `search_text` column and the panel's search box:
 * lowercase, accents removed, whitespace collapsed and trimmed ("  Caffè   ÀB " becomes "caffe ab").
 * Lowercasing comes first so that characters whose lowercase form adds a combining mark
 * ("İ") are stripped as well.
 */
export function normalizeForSearch(value: string): string {
  return value.toLowerCase().normalize("NFD").replace(/\p{M}/gu, "").replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
}
```

**Contract deviations (all also reported to the plan reviewer):**
- The Files list of the skeleton is extended: `biome.json` (Biome must parse Tailwind directives, otherwise `pnpm lint` fails on `@theme`, `@utility` and `@apply`), `vite.config.ts` (CSP-safe font handling, see below), `vitest.config.ts` (so tests can read CSS text), and `ui.tsx`, `LanguageSwitcher.tsx`, `HomePage.tsx`, `SetupPage.tsx` (the Requirements ask for slate classes to be swapped in "the current pages"; these four files hold all of them). `rules.test.ts` is new.
- `tokens.test.ts` reads the stylesheets with Vite's `?raw` import instead of `fs`: `apps/web` has no `@types/node` and the plan adds no dependency, so `node:fs` would not type-check.
- `@theme inline` maps each colour as `rgb(var(--x))`, not `rgb(var(--x) / <alpha-value>)`: `<alpha-value>` is Tailwind 3 syntax. In Tailwind 4 opacity modifiers (`bg-primary/50`) work through `color-mix` on the plain value.
- `index.html` has no `class` on `<body>`: `base.css` applies `bg-bg text-fg font-sans antialiased` to `body`, so a class attribute would be redundant.

- Tests that need the text of a stylesheet or of `public/theme-init.js` import it with `?raw` (the web package has no `@types/node`, and `vitest.config.ts` now lets `*.css?raw` through, because Vitest otherwise replaces CSS with an empty string).
- Biome now parses Tailwind directives (`@theme`, `@utility`, `@apply`); later tasks may use them in `.css` files.
- `vite.config.ts` sets `build.assetsInlineLimit: 0`: with Vite's default, a small font subset is inlined as a `data:` URI, which the CSP (`font-src 'self'`) blocks. Never turn this back on.

```typescript
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import stylesheet from "../styles.css?raw";
import tokensCss from "./tokens.css?raw";

type Theme = Record<string, string>;

/** Declarations of the rule whose selector is exactly `selector`. */
function declarations(css: string, selector: string): Theme {
  const escaped = selector.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, "\\$&");
  const rule = new RegExp(`(?:^|\\n)${escaped}\\s*\\{([^}]*)\\}`).exec(css);
  if (!rule) throw new Error(`tokens.css has no rule for ${selector}`);
  const result: Theme = {};
  for (const match of (rule[1] ?? "").matchAll(/--([a-z0-9-]+)\s*:\s*([^;]+);/g)) {
    result[match[1] ?? ""] = (match[2] ?? "").trim();
  }
  return result;
}

const light = declarations(tokensCss, ":root");
const dark = declarations(tokensCss, ':root[data-theme="dark"]');

function rgb(triplet: string): [number, number, number] {
  const match = /^(\d{1,3}) (\d{1,3}) (\d{1,3})$/.exec(triplet);
  if (!match) throw new Error(`Not an RGB triplet: "${triplet}"`);
  return [Number(match[1]), Number(match[2]), Number(match[3])];
}

function hex(triplet: string): string {
  return `#${rgb(triplet)
    .map((channel) => channel.toString(16).padStart(2, "0"))
    .join("")
    .toUpperCase()}`;
}

function luminance(triplet: string): number {
  const [r, g, b] = rgb(triplet).map((channel) => {
    const value = channel / 255;
    return value <= 0.04045 ? value / 12.92 : ((value + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4;
  }) as [number, number, number];
  return 0.2126 * r + 0.7152 * g + 0.0722 * b;
}

function contrast(theme: Theme, foreground: string, background: string): number {
  const a = luminance(theme[foreground] ?? "");
  const b = luminance(theme[background] ?? "");
  return (Math.max(a, b) + 0.05) / (Math.min(a, b) + 0.05);
}

/** UX doc section 5, token table. */
const UX_TABLE: Record<"light" | "dark", Record<string, string>> = {
  light: {
    bg: "#F6F7F9",
    surface: "#FFFFFF",
    "surface-2": "#F1F3F7",
    border: "#E3E7EE",
    text: "#141A26",
    muted: "#5B6475",
    primary: "#1E2A4A",
    "primary-50": "#EEF1F8",
    accent: "#B07A22",
    positive: "#15803D",
    ink: "#334155",
    warning: "#B45309",
    "warning-bg": "#FEF3C7",
    danger: "#B91C1C",
    "danger-bg": "#FEE2E2",
    info: "#1D4ED8",
    "info-bg": "#DBEAFE",
  },
  dark: {
    bg: "#0E121B",
    surface: "#151B27",
    "surface-2": "#1C2433",
    border: "#273043",
    text: "#E7EAF1",
    muted: "#9AA4B6",
    primary: "#9DB0E0",
    "primary-50": "#1E2840",
    accent: "#D9A74A",
    positive: "#4ADE80",
    ink: "#CBD5E1",
    warning: "#FBBF24",
    "warning-bg": "#3A2A0B",
    danger: "#F87171",
    "danger-bg": "#3B1416",
    info: "#60A5FA",
    "info-bg": "#13233F",
  },
};

const SURFACES = ["bg", "surface", "surface-2"];

/** Text pairs that components really use: WCAG AA, 4.5:1. */
const TEXT_PAIRS: [string, string][] = [
  ...["text", "muted", "primary", "positive", "ink", "danger", "warning", "info"].flatMap(
    (foreground): [string, string][] => SURFACES.map((surface) => [foreground, surface]),
  ),
  ["text", "primary-50"],
  ["muted", "primary-50"],
  ["primary", "primary-50"],
  ["warning", "warning-bg"],
  ["danger", "danger-bg"],
  ["info", "info-bg"],
  // Accent badge. `text` on `accent` is 1.8:1 in dark mode, so the badge uses `on-accent`.
  ["on-accent", "accent"],
  // Label of a primary button (`bg-primary text-bg`).
  ["bg", "primary"],
];

/** Bars and dots, not text: WCAG non-text contrast, 3:1. */
const NON_TEXT_PAIRS: [string, string][] = [
  ["accent", "surface"],
  ["accent", "bg"],
];

describe("tokens.css", () => {
  it("defines the same tokens in light and dark", () => {
    const names = (theme: Theme) =>
      Object.keys(theme)
        .filter((name) => name !== "color-scheme")
        .sort();
    expect(names(dark)).toEqual(names(light).filter((name) => name !== "row-height"));
  });

  it.each(["light", "dark"] as const)("matches the UX token table in %s mode", (mode) => {
    const theme = mode === "light" ? light : dark;
    for (const [name, expected] of Object.entries(UX_TABLE[mode])) {
      expect(hex(theme[name] ?? ""), `${mode} --${name}`).toBe(expected);
    }
  });

  it.each([
    ["light", light],
    ["dark", dark],
  ] as const)("meets WCAG AA for every text pair in %s mode", (mode, theme) => {
    for (const [foreground, background] of TEXT_PAIRS) {
      const ratio = contrast(theme, foreground, background);
      expect(
        ratio,
        `${mode}: ${foreground} on ${background} is ${ratio.toFixed(2)}:1`,
      ).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(4.5);
    }
  });

  it.each([
    ["light", light],
    ["dark", dark],
  ] as const)("meets 3:1 for non-text pairs in %s mode", (mode, theme) => {
    for (const [foreground, background] of NON_TEXT_PAIRS) {
      const ratio = contrast(theme, foreground, background);
      expect(
        ratio,
        `${mode}: ${foreground} on ${background} is ${ratio.toFixed(2)}:1`,
      ).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(3);
    }
  });

  it("sets the row height per density", () => {
    expect(declarations(tokensCss, ':root[data-density="compact"]')["row-height"]).toBe("40px");
    expect(declarations(tokensCss, ':root[data-density="comfortable"]')["row-height"]).toBe("56px");
  });
});

describe("styles.css theme mapping", () => {
  const MAPPING: Record<string, string> = {
    bg: "bg",
    surface: "surface",
    "surface-2": "surface-2",
    subtle: "border",
    fg: "text",
    muted: "muted",
    primary: "primary",
    "primary-50": "primary-50",
    accent: "accent",
    "on-accent": "on-accent",
    positive: "positive",
    ink: "ink",
    warning: "warning",
    "warning-soft": "warning-bg",
    danger: "danger",
    "danger-soft": "danger-bg",
    info: "info",
    "info-soft": "info-bg",
  };

  it.each(Object.entries(MAPPING))("maps the %s utility to --%s", (utility, variable) => {
    expect(stylesheet).toContain(`--color-${utility}: rgb(var(--${variable}));`);
    expect(light[variable], `--${variable} missing in tokens.css`).toBeDefined();
  });

  it("declares the fonts and the tabular utility", () => {
    expect(stylesheet).toContain(
      '--font-sans: "Inter Variable", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif;',
    );
    expect(stylesheet).toContain(
      '--font-display: "Manrope Variable", "Inter Variable", sans-serif;',
    );
    expect(stylesheet).toMatch(/@utility tabular\s*\{\s*font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;/);
  });
});
```

```typescript
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";

// Sources of the panel, tests excluded. `?raw` gives the text without running anything.
const sources = import.meta.glob(["../**/*.{ts,tsx}", "!../**/*.test.{ts,tsx}"], {
  query: "?raw",
  import: "default",
  eager: true,
}) as Record<string, string>;

const PALETTE =
  "slate|gray|zinc|neutral|stone|red|orange|amber|yellow|lime|green|emerald|teal|cyan|sky|blue|indigo|violet|purple|fuchsia|pink|rose";

/** UX doc section 5: components use semantic utilities only. */
const FORBIDDEN: [string, RegExp][] = [
  ["dark: variant", /(?:^|[\s"'`])dark:/],
  ["bg-white / text-white / bg-black / text-black", /\b(?:bg|text)-(?:white|black)\b/],
  [
    "Tailwind palette colour",
    new RegExp(
      `\\b(?:bg|text|border|ring|divide|outline|fill|stroke|from|via|to|shadow|placeholder|accent|caret|decoration)-(?:${PALETTE})-\\d{2,3}\\b`,
    ),
  ],
  ["hex colour literal", /["'`]#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}["'`]/],
];

describe("panel sources", () => {
  it("are found", () => {
    expect(Object.keys(sources).length).toBeGreaterThan(5);
  });

  it.each(FORBIDDEN)("contain no %s", (_name, pattern) => {
    const offenders = Object.entries(sources)
      .filter(([, text]) => pattern.test(text))
      .map(([file]) => file);
    expect(offenders).toEqual([]);
  });
});
```
