```ts
    ).toBe("https://eb.example.test:8443");
  });

  it.each([
    ["http://eb.example.test", /EB_API_BASE_URL must use https/],
    ["https://eb.example.test/v1", /EB_API_BASE_URL must not contain a path/],
    ["https://eb.example.test/?x=1", /EB_API_BASE_URL must not contain a path/],
    ["https://user:pw@eb.example.test", /EB_API_BASE_URL must not contain credentials/],
    ["eb.example.test", /EB_API_BASE_URL must be an absolute https URL/],
  ])("rejects the API base URL %s", (url, message) => {
    expect(problemsOf(() => loadEnableBanking({ ...eb, EB_API_BASE_URL: url }, noFiles))).toEqual([
      expect.stringMatching(message),
    ]);
  });

  it("rejects a bad API base URL even when the integration is otherwise unset", () => {
    expect(() => loadEnableBanking({ EB_API_BASE_URL: "http://eb.example.test" }, noFiles)).toThrow(
      /EB_API_BASE_URL/,
    );
  });

  it("requires the application id and the key together", () => {
    expect(problemsOf(() => loadEnableBanking({ EB_APPLICATION_ID: APP_ID }, noFiles))).toEqual([
      "EB_PRIVATE_KEY (or EB_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE) is required when EB_APPLICATION_ID is set",
    ]);
    expect(problemsOf(() => loadEnableBanking({ EB_PRIVATE_KEY: RSA_PKCS8 }, noFiles))).toEqual([
      "EB_APPLICATION_ID is required when EB_PRIVATE_KEY (or EB_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE) is set",
    ]);
  });

  it.each(["not-a-uuid", "8f1c2b7e4d3a4f6b9a102c5d7e9b3a41", `${APP_ID}0`, `x${APP_ID.slice(1)}`])(
    "rejects the application id %s",
    (id) => {
      expect(
        problemsOf(() => loadEnableBanking({ ...eb, EB_APPLICATION_ID: id }, noFiles)),
      ).toEqual(["EB_APPLICATION_ID must be a UUID"]);
    },
  );

  it("rejects text that is not a PEM and a truncated PEM", () => {
    for (const bad of ["not a key", RSA_PKCS8.slice(0, 120)]) {
      expect(problemsOf(() => loadEnableBanking({ ...eb, EB_PRIVATE_KEY: bad }, noFiles))).toEqual([
        "EB_PRIVATE_KEY is not a valid unencrypted PEM private key (PKCS#1 or PKCS#8)",
      ]);
    }
  });

  it("rejects a key that is not RSA", () => {
    expect(
      problemsOf(() => loadEnableBanking({ ...eb, EB_PRIVATE_KEY: EC_PKCS8 }, noFiles)),
    ).toEqual(["EB_PRIVATE_KEY must be an RSA private key"]);
  });

  it("refuses the key and its _FILE variant together", () => {
    const env = { ...eb, EB_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE: "/run/secrets/eb_key" };
    expect(problemsOf(() => loadEnableBanking(env, noFiles))).toEqual([
      "EB_PRIVATE_KEY and EB_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE are both set; use one",
    ]);
  });

  it("reports an unreadable key file once, without a second 'required' problem", () => {
    const denied = () => {
      throw Object.assign(new Error("denied"), { code: "EACCES" });
    };
    const env = { EB_APPLICATION_ID: APP_ID, EB_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE: "/run/secrets/eb_key" };
    const problems = problemsOf(() => loadEnableBanking(env, denied));
    expect(problems).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(problems[0]).toMatch(/EB_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE points to \/run\/secrets\/eb_key/);
  });

  it("reports an empty key file", () => {
    const env = { EB_APPLICATION_ID: APP_ID, EB_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE: "/run/secrets/eb_key" };
    expect(
      problemsOf(() => loadEnableBanking(env, filesOf({ "/run/secrets/eb_key": "\n" }))),
    ).toEqual(["EB_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE points to an empty file"]);
  });

  it("collects the Enable Banking problems with the others in loadConfig", () => {
    const problems = problemsOf(() =>
      loadConfig({ ...baseEnv, EB_APPLICATION_ID: "nope", EB_PRIVATE_KEY: "nope" }, noFiles),
    );
    expect(problems).toContain("EB_APPLICATION_ID must be a UUID");
    expect(problems.some((problem) => problem.startsWith("EB_PRIVATE_KEY is not a valid"))).toBe(
      true,
    );
  });
});

describe("SMTP configuration", () => {
  const smtp = { SMTP_HOST: "smtp.example.test", SMTP_FROM: "Bursar <bursar@example.test>" };

  it("is null when no SMTP variable is set, also through loadConfig", () => {
    expect(loadSmtp({}, noFiles)).toBeNull();
    expect(
      loadSmtp({ SMTP_HOST: " ", SMTP_PORT: "2525", SMTP_SECURITY: "tls" }, noFiles),
    ).toBeNull();
    expect(loadConfig(baseEnv, noFiles).smtp).toBeNull();
  });

  it("applies the defaults: port 587, STARTTLS, no credentials", () => {
    expect(loadSmtp(smtp, noFiles)).toEqual({
      host: "smtp.example.test",
      port: 587,
      security: "starttls",
      user: null,
      password: null,
      from: "Bursar <bursar@example.test>",
    });
    expect(loadConfig({ ...baseEnv, ...smtp }, noFiles).smtp?.host).toBe("smtp.example.test");
  });

  it("parses an explicit configuration with a user and a password", () => {
    expect(
      loadSmtp(
        {
          ...smtp,
          SMTP_PORT: " 465 ",
          SMTP_SECURITY: "TLS",
          SMTP_USER: "mailer",
          SMTP_PASSWORD: "smtp-password-value",
        },
        noFiles,
      ),
    ).toEqual({
      host: "smtp.example.test",
      port: 465,
      security: "tls",
      user: "mailer",
      password: "smtp-password-value",
      from: "Bursar <bursar@example.test>",
    });
  });

  it("reads the password from a *_FILE path", () => {
    const env = { ...smtp, SMTP_USER: "mailer", SMTP_PASSWORD_FILE: "/run/secrets/smtp_password" };
    const config = loadSmtp(
      env,
      filesOf({ "/run/secrets/smtp_password": "smtp-password-value\n" }),
    );
    expect(config?.password).toBe("smtp-password-value");
  });

  it("allows plain SMTP on loopback hosts only", () => {
    for (const host of ["localhost", "LOCALHOST", "127.0.0.1", "127.1.2.3", "[::1]", "::1"]) {
      expect(loadSmtp({ ...smtp, SMTP_HOST: host, SMTP_SECURITY: "none" }, noFiles)?.security).toBe(
        "none",
      );
    }
    for (const host of ["smtp.example.test", "10.0.0.5", "128.0.0.1", "localhost.example.test"]) {
      expect(
        problemsOf(() => loadSmtp({ ...smtp, SMTP_HOST: host, SMTP_SECURITY: "none" }, noFiles)),
      ).toEqual(["SMTP_SECURITY=none is allowed only when SMTP_HOST is a loopback address"]);
    }
  });

  it("stores an IPv6 host without brackets", () => {
    expect(loadSmtp({ ...smtp, SMTP_HOST: "[2001:db8::25]" }, noFiles)?.host).toBe("2001:db8::25");
  });

  it("rejects a malformed host, port and security mode", () => {
    expect(problemsOf(() => loadSmtp({ ...smtp, SMTP_HOST: "bad host!" }, noFiles))).toEqual([
      "SMTP_HOST must be an IP address or a hostname",
    ]);
    for (const port of ["0", "65536", "25.5", "25abc", "-1"]) {
      expect(problemsOf(() => loadSmtp({ ...smtp, SMTP_PORT: port }, noFiles))).toEqual([
        "SMTP_PORT must be an integer between 1 and 65535",
      ]);
    }
    expect(problemsOf(() => loadSmtp({ ...smtp, SMTP_SECURITY: "ssl" }, noFiles))).toEqual([
      "SMTP_SECURITY must be one of tls, starttls, none",
    ]);
  });

  it("requires SMTP_FROM, as an address on a single line", () => {
    expect(problemsOf(() => loadSmtp({ SMTP_HOST: "smtp.example.test" }, noFiles))).toEqual([
      "SMTP_FROM is required when SMTP_HOST is set",
    ]);
    for (const from of ["Bursar", "a@example.test\nBcc: x@example.test"]) {
      expect(problemsOf(() => loadSmtp({ ...smtp, SMTP_FROM: from }, noFiles))).toEqual([
        "SMTP_FROM must be an email address or Name <address> on a single line",
      ]);
    }
  });

  it("requires the user and the password together", () => {
    const together = "SMTP_USER and SMTP_PASSWORD (or SMTP_PASSWORD_FILE) must be set together";
    expect(problemsOf(() => loadSmtp({ ...smtp, SMTP_USER: "mailer" }, noFiles))).toEqual([
      together,
    ]);
    expect(
      problemsOf(() => loadSmtp({ ...smtp, SMTP_PASSWORD: "smtp-password-value" }, noFiles)),
    ).toEqual([together]);
  });

  it("names SMTP_HOST when other SMTP variables are set without it", () => {
    const hostMissing = "SMTP_HOST is required when SMTP_FROM, SMTP_USER or SMTP_PASSWORD is set";
    expect(problemsOf(() => loadSmtp({ SMTP_FROM: "bursar@example.test" }, noFiles))).toEqual([
      hostMissing,
    ]);
    expect(problemsOf(() => loadSmtp({ SMTP_USER: "mailer" }, noFiles))).toEqual([hostMissing]);
    expect(problemsOf(() => loadSmtp({ SMTP_PASSWORD: "smtp-password-value" }, noFiles))).toEqual([
      hostMissing,
    ]);
  });

  it("refuses the password and its _FILE variant together, and reports an unreadable file", () => {
    expect(
      problemsOf(() =>
        loadSmtp(
          { ...smtp, SMTP_USER: "u", SMTP_PASSWORD: "x", SMTP_PASSWORD_FILE: "/f" },
          noFiles,
        ),
      ),
    ).toEqual(["SMTP_PASSWORD and SMTP_PASSWORD_FILE are both set; use one"]);
    const missing = () => {
      throw Object.assign(new Error("missing"), { code: "ENOENT" });
    };
    const problems = problemsOf(() =>
      loadSmtp({ ...smtp, SMTP_USER: "mailer", SMTP_PASSWORD_FILE: "/run/secrets/smtp" }, missing),
    );
    expect(problems).toEqual([
      "SMTP_PASSWORD_FILE points to /run/secrets/smtp, which cannot be read (ENOENT)",
    ]);
  });
});

describe("backup configuration", () => {
  const s3 = {
    BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT: "https://s3.example.test",
    BACKUP_S3_BUCKET: "bursar-backups",
    BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID: "access-key-id-value",
    BACKUP_S3_SECRET_KEY: "s3-secret-value-0123456789",
  };
  const dataDir = path.resolve("/srv/bursar-data");

  it("defaults to <dataDir>/backups with no S3 target", () => {
    expect(loadBackup({}, dataDir, noFiles)).toEqual({
      dir: path.join(dataDir, "backups"),
      s3: null,
    });
    expect(
      loadBackup({ BACKUP_S3_REGION: "eu-1", BACKUP_S3_PREFIX: "x" }, dataDir, noFiles).s3,
    ).toBeNull();
  });

  it("follows BURSAR_DATA_DIR and BURSAR_BACKUP_DIR through loadConfig", () => {
    const withData = loadConfig({ ...baseEnv, BURSAR_DATA_DIR: "/srv/data" }, noFiles);
    expect(withData.backup.dir).toBe(path.join(path.resolve("/srv/data"), "backups"));
    const explicit = loadConfig({ ...baseEnv, BURSAR_BACKUP_DIR: "/mnt/backups" }, noFiles);
    expect(explicit.backup.dir).toBe(path.resolve("/mnt/backups"));
    const blank = loadConfig({ ...baseEnv, BURSAR_BACKUP_DIR: "  " }, noFiles);
    expect(blank.backup.dir).toBe(path.join(blank.dataDir, "backups"));
  });

  it("parses a complete S3 target with the default region and prefix", () => {
    const backup = loadBackup(s3, dataDir, noFiles);
    expect(backup.s3).toEqual({
      endpoint: new URL("https://s3.example.test"),
      region: "auto",
      bucket: "bursar-backups",
      prefix: "bursar",
      accessKeyId: "access-key-id-value",
      secretAccessKey: "s3-secret-value-0123456789",
    });
    expect(backup.s3?.endpoint).toBeInstanceOf(URL);
  });

  it("reads the secret key from a *_FILE path", () => {
    const { BACKUP_S3_SECRET_KEY: _direct, ...rest } = s3;
    const env = { ...rest, BACKUP_S3_SECRET_KEY_FILE: "/run/secrets/s3_secret" };
    const backup = loadBackup(
      env,
      dataDir,
      filesOf({ "/run/secrets/s3_secret": "from-file-secret-value\n" }),
    );
    expect(backup.s3?.secretAccessKey).toBe("from-file-secret-value");
  });

  it("takes an explicit region and normalises the prefix", () => {
    const backup = loadBackup(
      { ...s3, BACKUP_S3_REGION: "eu-central-003", BACKUP_S3_PREFIX: "/finance/bursar/" },
      dataDir,
      noFiles,
    );
    expect(backup.s3).toMatchObject({ region: "eu-central-003", prefix: "finance/bursar" });
  });

  it.each([
    ["BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT"],
    ["BACKUP_S3_BUCKET"],
    ["BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID"],
    ["BACKUP_S3_SECRET_KEY"],
  ])("names %s when it is the only one missing", (name) => {
    const env: Record<string, string | undefined> = { ...s3, [name]: undefined };
    const problems = problemsOf(() => loadBackup(env, dataDir, noFiles));
    expect(problems).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(problems[0]).toContain(`also set ${name}`);
  });

  it("lists every missing variable when only one is set", () => {
    const problems = problemsOf(() =>
      loadBackup({ BACKUP_S3_BUCKET: "bursar-backups" }, dataDir, noFiles),
    );
    expect(problems).toEqual([
      "The S3 backup target is half configured; also set BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT, BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID, BACKUP_S3_SECRET_KEY (or BACKUP_S3_SECRET_KEY_FILE)",
    ]);
  });

  it.each([
    ["http://s3.example.test", /BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT must use https/],
    ["ftp://s3.example.test", /BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT must use https/],
    ["https://user:pw@s3.example.test", /BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT must not contain credentials/],
    ["https://s3.example.test/bucket", /BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT must not contain a path/],
    ["s3.example.test", /BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT must be an absolute https URL/],
  ])("rejects the endpoint %s", (endpoint, message) => {
    expect(
      problemsOf(() => loadBackup({ ...s3, BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT: endpoint }, dataDir, noFiles)),
    ).toEqual([expect.stringMatching(message)]);
  });

  it.each(["UPPER", "ab", "has space", "-leading", "trailing-", "a".repeat(64)])(
    "rejects the bucket name %j",
    (bucket) => {
      expect(
        problemsOf(() => loadBackup({ ...s3, BACKUP_S3_BUCKET: bucket }, dataDir, noFiles)),
      ).toEqual([expect.stringMatching(/^BACKUP_S3_BUCKET must be a valid bucket name/)]);
    },
  );

  it("rejects a bad region and bad prefixes", () => {
    expect(
      problemsOf(() => loadBackup({ ...s3, BACKUP_S3_REGION: "eu central" }, dataDir, noFiles)),
    ).toEqual(["BACKUP_S3_REGION must contain only letters, digits and hyphens"]);
    for (const prefix of ["/", "a//b", "a/../b", "..", "a b", "café"]) {
      expect(
        problemsOf(() => loadBackup({ ...s3, BACKUP_S3_PREFIX: prefix }, dataDir, noFiles)),
      ).toEqual([expect.stringMatching(/^BACKUP_S3_PREFIX must be slash-separated segments/)]);
    }
  });

  it("is collected by loadConfig with the other problems", () => {
    const problems = problemsOf(() =>
      loadConfig({ ...baseEnv, BACKUP_S3_BUCKET: "bursar-backups", TZ: "Mars/Olympus" }, noFiles),
    );
    expect(problems.some((problem) => problem.includes("TZ"))).toBe(true);
    expect(
      problems.some((problem) => problem.includes("S3 backup target is half configured")),
    ).toBe(true);
  });
});

describe("secrets never appear in configuration problems", () => {
  it("keeps every secret value out of every problem message", () => {
    const keyLines = RSA_PKCS8.trim().split("\n");
    const secrets = [
      keyLines[1] as string,
      "smtp-password-value",
      "s3-secret-value-0123456789",
      "access-key-id-value",
    ];
    const attempts: Record<string, string>[] = [
      // Wrong key kind, bad id, bad SMTP mode, bad S3 endpoint, all at once.
      {
        EB_APPLICATION_ID: "nope",
        EB_PRIVATE_KEY: EC_PKCS8,
        SMTP_HOST: "bad host!",
        SMTP_FROM: "nobody",
        SMTP_SECURITY: "ssl",
        SMTP_USER: "mailer",
        SMTP_PASSWORD: "smtp-password-value",
        BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT: "http://user:s3-secret-value-0123456789@s3.example.test",
        BACKUP_S3_BUCKET: "UPPER",
        BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID: "access-key-id-value",
        BACKUP_S3_SECRET_KEY: "s3-secret-value-0123456789",
      },
      // A truncated key (its body lines are the secret), a password without a user.
      {
        EB_APPLICATION_ID: APP_ID,
        EB_PRIVATE_KEY: RSA_PKCS8.slice(0, 120),
        SMTP_HOST: "smtp.example.test",
        SMTP_FROM: "bursar@example.test",
        SMTP_PASSWORD: "smtp-password-value",
        BACKUP_S3_SECRET_KEY: "s3-secret-value-0123456789",
      },
      // A key given together with its _FILE variant.
      {
        EB_APPLICATION_ID: APP_ID,
        EB_PRIVATE_KEY: RSA_PKCS8,
        EB_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE: "/run/secrets/eb_key",
      },
    ];
    for (const extra of attempts) {
      const error = (() => {
        try {
          loadConfig({ ...baseEnv, ...extra }, noFiles);
        } catch (caught) {
          return caught as ConfigError;
        }
        throw new Error("expected a ConfigError");
      })();
      for (const secret of secrets) {
        expect(error.message).not.toContain(secret);
        expect(error.problems.join("\n")).not.toContain(secret);
      }
    }
  });
});
```

(d) Insert the three loaders and their helpers between `loadClaudeCredential` and `loadConfig`. `loadEnableBanking`, `loadSmtp` and `loadBackup` throw one `ConfigError` carrying every problem they found; `loadConfig` collects it through `attempt`, so all problems are still reported together:


```ts
const UUID_PATTERN = /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/i;
const DEFAULT_EB_API_BASE_URL = "https://api.enablebanking.com";
const SMTP_SECURITY_MODES = ["tls", "starttls", "none"] as const;
const S3_BUCKET_PATTERN = /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]{1,61}[a-z0-9]$/;
const S3_REGION_PATTERN = /^[A-Za-z0-9-]{1,32}$/;
const S3_PREFIX_PATTERN = /^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+(\/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+)*$/;

/** An empty value counts as unset, like `setting` inside `loadConfig`. */
function envSetting(env: Env, name: string): string | undefined {
  return env[name]?.trim() || undefined;
}

/** Runs `fn`; a `ConfigError` it throws is added to `problems` instead of propagating. */
function collect<T>(problems: string[], fn: () => T): T | undefined {
  try {
    return fn();
  } catch (error) {
    if (!(error instanceof ConfigError)) throw error;
    problems.push(...error.problems);
    return undefined;
  }
}

/** Returns the bare host (IPv6 brackets removed) or undefined when it is not a host. */
function parseHostName(raw: string): string | undefined {
  const bracketed = /^\[(.*)\]$/.exec(raw);
  const host = bracketed ? (bracketed[1] as string) : raw;
  if (bracketed ? isIP(host) !== 6 : isIP(host) === 0 && !HOSTNAME_PATTERN.test(host)) {
    return undefined;
  }
  return host;
}

/**
 * Parses an https origin. The value is never echoed in a problem: a mistyped endpoint can
 * carry credentials in its userinfo.
 */
function parseHttpsOrigin(name: string, raw: string, problems: string[]): URL | undefined {
  let url: URL;
  try {
    url = new URL(raw);
  } catch {
    problems.push(`${name} must be an absolute https URL`);
    return undefined;
  }
  const problem =
    url.protocol !== "https:"
      ? "must use https"
      : !url.hostname
        ? "must have a host"
        : url.username || url.password
          ? "must not contain credentials"
          : url.pathname !== "/" || url.search || url.hash
            ? "must not contain a path, query or fragment"
            : undefined;
  if (problem) {
    problems.push(`${name} ${problem}`);
    return undefined;
  }
  return url;
}

/** Env files and orchestrators often carry a PEM on one line with literal `\n` sequences. */
function normalizePem(value: string): string {
  return value.includes("\\n") && !value.includes("\n") ? value.replaceAll("\\n", "\n") : value;
}

/** Why the value is not usable as the application key. Never includes the value. */
function rsaKeyProblem(pem: string): string | undefined {
  try {
    if (createPrivateKey(pem).asymmetricKeyType === "rsa") return undefined;
    return "EB_PRIVATE_KEY must be an RSA private key";
  } catch {
    return "EB_PRIVATE_KEY is not a valid unencrypted PEM private key (PKCS#1 or PKCS#8)";
  }
}

/**
 * Enable Banking: `EB_APPLICATION_ID` and the RSA key (`EB_PRIVATE_KEY` or `EB_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE`)
 * are set together or not at all. `EB_API_BASE_URL` is optional.
 */
export function loadEnableBanking(
  env: Env,
  readFile: ReadFile = defaultReadFile,
): EnableBankingConfig | null {
  const problems: string[] = [];
  const rawId = envSetting(env, "EB_APPLICATION_ID");
  const rawPem = collect(problems, () => readSecret(env, "EB_PRIVATE_KEY", readFile));
  const keyUnreadable = problems.length > 0;
  const keyGiven = rawPem !== undefined || keyUnreadable;

  let apiBaseUrl = DEFAULT_EB_API_BASE_URL;
  const rawBaseUrl = envSetting(env, "EB_API_BASE_URL");
  if (rawBaseUrl) {
    const parsed = parseHttpsOrigin("EB_API_BASE_URL", rawBaseUrl, problems);
    if (parsed) apiBaseUrl = parsed.origin;
  }

  if (rawId === undefined && !keyGiven) {
    if (problems.length > 0) throw new ConfigError(problems);
    return null;
  }
  if (rawId === undefined) {
    problems.push(
      "EB_APPLICATION_ID is required when EB_PRIVATE_KEY (or EB_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE) is set",
    );
  } else if (!UUID_PATTERN.test(rawId)) {
    problems.push("EB_APPLICATION_ID must be a UUID");
  }
  const privateKeyPem = rawPem === undefined ? undefined : normalizePem(rawPem);
  if (!keyGiven) {
    problems.push(
      "EB_PRIVATE_KEY (or EB_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE) is required when EB_APPLICATION_ID is set",
    );
  } else if (privateKeyPem !== undefined) {
    const keyProblem = rsaKeyProblem(privateKeyPem);
    if (keyProblem) problems.push(keyProblem);
  }
  if (problems.length > 0 || rawId === undefined || privateKeyPem === undefined) {
    throw new ConfigError(problems);
  }
  return { applicationId: rawId, privateKeyPem, apiBaseUrl };
}

/**
 * SMTP notifications: unset `SMTP_HOST` means no email. `SMTP_FROM` is required with a host,
 * `SMTP_USER` and the password (`SMTP_PASSWORD` or `SMTP_PASSWORD_FILE`) go together.
 */
export function loadSmtp(env: Env, readFile: ReadFile = defaultReadFile): SmtpConfig | null {
  const problems: string[] = [];
  const rawHost = envSetting(env, "SMTP_HOST");
  const rawFrom = envSetting(env, "SMTP_FROM");
  const user = envSetting(env, "SMTP_USER");
  const password = collect(problems, () => readSecret(env, "SMTP_PASSWORD", readFile));
  const passwordUnreadable = problems.length > 0;

  if (rawHost === undefined) {
    if (
      rawFrom !== undefined ||
      user !== undefined ||
      password !== undefined ||
      passwordUnreadable
    ) {
      problems.push("SMTP_HOST is required when SMTP_FROM, SMTP_USER or SMTP_PASSWORD is set");
    }
    if (problems.length > 0) throw new ConfigError(problems);
    return null;
  }

  const host = parseHostName(rawHost);
  if (host === undefined) problems.push("SMTP_HOST must be an IP address or a hostname");

  const rawPort = envSetting(env, "SMTP_PORT") ?? "587";
  const port = /^\d{1,5}$/.test(rawPort) ? Number(rawPort) : Number.NaN;
  if (!Number.isInteger(port) || port < 1 || port > 65535) {
    problems.push("SMTP_PORT must be an integer between 1 and 65535");
  }

  const rawSecurity = (envSetting(env, "SMTP_SECURITY") ?? "starttls").toLowerCase();
  const security = SMTP_SECURITY_MODES.find((mode) => mode === rawSecurity);
  if (!security) {
    problems.push(`SMTP_SECURITY must be one of ${SMTP_SECURITY_MODES.join(", ")}`);
  } else if (security === "none" && host !== undefined) {
    const loopbackName = isIP(host) === 6 ? `[${host}]` : host.toLowerCase();
    if (!isLoopbackHost(loopbackName)) {
      problems.push("SMTP_SECURITY=none is allowed only when SMTP_HOST is a loopback address");
    }
  }

  if (!passwordUnreadable && (user !== undefined) !== (password !== undefined)) {
    problems.push("SMTP_USER and SMTP_PASSWORD (or SMTP_PASSWORD_FILE) must be set together");
  }

  if (rawFrom === undefined) {
    problems.push("SMTP_FROM is required when SMTP_HOST is set");
  } else if (/[\r\n]/.test(rawFrom) || !rawFrom.includes("@")) {
    problems.push("SMTP_FROM must be an email address or Name <address> on a single line");
  }

  if (
    problems.length > 0 ||
    host === undefined ||
    security === undefined ||
    rawFrom === undefined
  ) {
    throw new ConfigError(problems);
  }
  return { host, port, security, user: user ?? null, password: password ?? null, from: rawFrom };
}

/**
 * Backups: the local directory always exists (default `<dataDir>/backups`). The S3-compatible
 * target is optional and needs its endpoint, bucket, access key id and secret key together.
 */
export function loadBackup(
  env: Env,
  dataDir: string,
  readFile: ReadFile = defaultReadFile,
): BackupConfig {
  const problems: string[] = [];
  const dir = path.resolve(envSetting(env, "BURSAR_BACKUP_DIR") ?? path.join(dataDir, "backups"));
  const rawEndpoint = envSetting(env, "BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT");
  const bucket = envSetting(env, "BACKUP_S3_BUCKET");
  const accessKeyId = envSetting(env, "BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID");
  const secretAccessKey = collect(problems, () =>
    readSecret(env, "BACKUP_S3_SECRET_KEY", readFile),
  );
  const secretGiven = secretAccessKey !== undefined || problems.length > 0;

  const given = [
    ["BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT", rawEndpoint !== undefined],
    ["BACKUP_S3_BUCKET", bucket !== undefined],
    ["BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID", accessKeyId !== undefined],
    ["BACKUP_S3_SECRET_KEY (or BACKUP_S3_SECRET_KEY_FILE)", secretGiven],
  ] as const;
  const missing = given.filter(([, isGiven]) => !isGiven).map(([name]) => name);
  if (missing.length === given.length) {
    if (problems.length > 0) throw new ConfigError(problems);
    return { dir, s3: null };
  }
  if (missing.length > 0) {
    problems.push(`The S3 backup target is half configured; also set ${missing.join(", ")}`);
  }

  const endpoint = rawEndpoint
    ? parseHttpsOrigin("BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT", rawEndpoint, problems)
    : undefined;
  if (bucket !== undefined && !S3_BUCKET_PATTERN.test(bucket)) {
    problems.push(
      "BACKUP_S3_BUCKET must be a valid bucket name (3 to 63 lowercase letters, digits, dots, hyphens)",
    );
  }
  const region = envSetting(env, "BACKUP_S3_REGION") ?? "auto";
  if (!S3_REGION_PATTERN.test(region)) {
    problems.push("BACKUP_S3_REGION must contain only letters, digits and hyphens");
  }
  const prefix = (envSetting(env, "BACKUP_S3_PREFIX") ?? "bursar").replace(/^\/+|\/+$/g, "");
  if (
    !S3_PREFIX_PATTERN.test(prefix) ||
    prefix.split("/").some((segment) => segment === "." || segment === "..")
  ) {
    problems.push(
      "BACKUP_S3_PREFIX must be slash-separated segments of letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-'",
    );
  }

  if (
    problems.length > 0 ||
    endpoint === undefined ||
    bucket === undefined ||
    accessKeyId === undefined ||
    secretAccessKey === undefined
  ) {
    throw new ConfigError(problems);
  }
  return { dir, s3: { endpoint, region, bucket, prefix, accessKeyId, secretAccessKey } };
}
```

```ts
    expect(result.changed).toEqual(["consentDays"]);
    expect(rows()).toEqual([{ key: "consentDays", value: "120", updatedAt: now }]);
  });

  it("rejects an invalid patch and writes nothing, not even the valid keys", () => {
    expect(() => store.update({ consentDays: 90, backgroundSyncCap: 5 })).toThrow();
    expect(() => store.update({ unknownKey: true } as never)).toThrow();
    expect(rows()).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("rolls back every key when a write fails midway", () => {
    t.sqlite.exec(
      "CREATE TRIGGER fail_on_locale BEFORE INSERT ON settings WHEN NEW.key = 'locale' BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'forced failure'); END",
    );
    expect(() => store.update({ consentDays: 90, locale: "en" })).toThrow(/forced failure/);
    expect(rows()).toEqual([]);
    expect(store.get()).toEqual(SETTINGS_DEFAULTS);
  });

  it("is shared by two store instances over the same database", () => {
    new SettingsStore(t.db, () => now).update({ consentDays: 60 });
    expect(store.get().consentDays).toBe(60);
  });
});
```

- [ ] **Step 15: Implement the settings store**

Create `apps/server/src/settings/store.ts`:


```ts
import {
  SETTINGS_DEFAULTS,
  type SettingsPatch,
  type SettingsValues,
  settingsPatchSchema,
  settingsValuesSchema,
} from "@bursar/shared";
import type { BursarDb } from "../db";
import { settings } from "../db/schema";

const SETTINGS_KEYS = Object.keys(SETTINGS_DEFAULTS) as (keyof SettingsValues)[];

/**
 * Owner settings, one row per key with a JSON value. A missing row, invalid JSON, an unknown
 * key or a value that no longer passes its schema all read as the default for that key, so a
 * damaged row can never stop the service from starting or a page from loading.
 */
export class SettingsStore {
  constructor(
    private readonly db: BursarDb,
    private readonly now: () => number = Date.now,
  ) {}

  get(): SettingsValues {
    const stored = new Map(
      this.db
        .select()
        .from(settings)
        .all()
        .map((row) => [row.key, row.value]),
    );
    const values: Record<string, unknown> = { ...SETTINGS_DEFAULTS };
    for (const key of SETTINGS_KEYS) {
      const raw = stored.get(key);
      if (raw === undefined) continue;
      let candidate: unknown;
      try {
        candidate = JSON.parse(raw);
      } catch {
        continue;
      }
      const parsed = settingsValuesSchema.shape[key].safeParse(candidate);
      if (parsed.success) values[key] = parsed.data;
    }
    return values as SettingsValues;
  }

  /**
   * Applies a patch. Only keys whose effective value changes are written, all in one
   * transaction, and `changed` lists them in schema order. Throws a `ZodError` for a patch
   * that does not satisfy `settingsPatchSchema`; nothing is written in that case.
   */
  update(patch: SettingsPatch): { values: SettingsValues; changed: (keyof SettingsValues)[] } {
    const valid = settingsPatchSchema.parse(patch);
    return this.db.transaction((tx) => {
      const current = this.get();
      const changed: (keyof SettingsValues)[] = [];
      const at = this.now();
      for (const key of SETTINGS_KEYS) {
        const next = valid[key];
        if (next === undefined || next === current[key]) continue;
        const value = JSON.stringify(next);
        tx.insert(settings)
          .values({ key, value, updatedAt: at })
          .onConflictDoUpdate({ target: settings.key, set: { value, updatedAt: at } })
          .run();
        changed.push(key);
      }
      return { values: this.get(), changed };
    });
  }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 19: Implement the settings routes**

Create `apps/server/src/settings/routes.ts`:


```ts
import { type SettingsResponse, type SettingsValues, settingsPatchSchema } from "@bursar/shared";
import { Hono } from "hono";
import type { AuditLog } from "../audit";
import type { EventBus } from "../events/bus";
import type { AppEnv } from "../http/app";
import type { SettingsStore } from "./store";

export interface SettingsRouteDeps {
  store: SettingsStore;
  audit: AuditLog;
  bus: EventBus;
  /** Read-only facts about the deployment, built once from the configuration. */
  system: SettingsResponse["system"];
}

export function settingsRoutes(deps: SettingsRouteDeps): Hono<AppEnv> {
  const routes = new Hono<AppEnv>();
  const respond = (values: SettingsValues): SettingsResponse => ({
    values,
    system: deps.system,
  });

  routes.get("/", (c) => c.json(respond(deps.store.get())));

  routes.patch("/", async (c) => {
    const parsed = settingsPatchSchema.safeParse(await c.req.json().catch(() => null));
    if (!parsed.success) {
      return c.json({ error: "Invalid settings", code: "invalid_settings" }, 400);
    }
    const { values, changed } = deps.store.update(parsed.data);
    if (changed.length > 0) {
      // Key names only: values such as the notification email never reach the audit log.
      deps.audit.record({
        actor: "user",
        action: "settings.update",
        target: "settings",
        details: { keys: changed.join(",") },
      });
      deps.bus.publish({ type: "settings.updated" });
    }
    return c.json(respond(values));
  });

  return routes;
}
```

Replace `apps/server/.env.example` with the following. Every new line is commented out and carries an angle-bracket value, so copying the file never enables an integration by accident, and nothing in it looks like a secret:


```sh
# Local development. Copy to apps/server/.env (gitignored).
# The panel dev server runs on port 5173 and proxies /api here, so the public URL is the Vite origin.
BURSAR_PUBLIC_URL=http://localhost:5173
TZ=Europe/Rome
BURSAR_HOST=127.0.0.1
BURSAR_PORT=8080
BURSAR_DATA_DIR=./data
BURSAR_MASTER_KEY_FILE=./data/master_key
BURSAR_LOG_LEVEL=debug

# Enable Banking (read-only account information). Set the id and the key together.
# Create an application in the Enable Banking control panel, upload its certificate, and keep
# the matching RSA private key in a file that is never committed (*.pem is gitignored).
# Use EB_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE (a path) or EB_PRIVATE_KEY (the PEM, with literal \n for line breaks).
# EB_APPLICATION_ID=<application-uuid>
# EB_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE=./data/eb_private_key.pem
# EB_API_BASE_URL=https://api.enablebanking.com

# Email notifications. Without SMTP_HOST no email is sent.
# SMTP_SECURITY is tls (implicit TLS, usually port 465), starttls (default, port 587) or none
# (plain; accepted only for a loopback host such as a local mail catcher on port 1025).
# SMTP_USER and the password go together; use SMTP_PASSWORD_FILE or SMTP_PASSWORD.
# SMTP_HOST=<smtp-host>
# SMTP_PORT=587
# SMTP_SECURITY=starttls
# SMTP_USER=<smtp-user>
# SMTP_PASSWORD_FILE=./data/smtp_password
# SMTP_FROM=Bursar <bursar@<your-domain>>

# Backups. The local directory is always used; default <BURSAR_DATA_DIR>/backups.
# BURSAR_BACKUP_DIR=./data/backups
# Optional second copy on an S3-compatible service. The four values below go together;
# the secret can also be given as BACKUP_S3_SECRET_KEY.
# BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT=https://<s3-endpoint>
# BACKUP_S3_BUCKET=<bucket-name>
# BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID=<access-key-id>
# BACKUP_S3_SECRET_KEY_FILE=./data/s3_secret_key
# BACKUP_S3_REGION=auto
# BACKUP_S3_PREFIX=bursar
```

- Test: `packages/shared/src/notifications.test.ts`, `apps/server/src/notifications/service.test.ts`, `mailer.test.ts`, `templates.test.ts`, `email-job.test.ts`, `routes.test.ts`, `wiring.test.ts`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: Task 6 `notifications` table, `NotificationEvent`; Task 7 `JobQueue.enqueueUnique`, `EMAIL_JOB`, `emailPayloadSchema`, `emailDedupeKey`, `parsePayload`, `PermanentJobError`, `EventBus`; Task 8 `SettingsStore`, `Config["smtp"]`.
- Produces:
  - `@bursar/shared` `notifications.ts`: `notificationItemSchema` → `NotificationItem { id: number; event: NotificationEvent; params: Record<string, string | number>; link: string | null; createdAt: number; readAt: number | null }`; `NotificationListResponse { items: NotificationItem[]; unread: number }`; `TestEmailResponse { sent: true }`.
  - `notifications/keys.ts`: `notificationKeys = { consentExpiring(connectionId: number, validUntil: number, threshold: 14 | 3): string; consentExpired(connectionId: number, validUntil: number): string; connectionError(connectionId: number, at: number): string; syncFailing(accountId: number, since: LocalDate | "never"): string; backupFailing(localDate: LocalDate): string }` (stable strings, e.g. `consent-expiring:<id>:<validUntil>:14`).
  - `notifications/service.ts`: `interface RaiseInput { event: NotificationEvent; dedupeKey: string; params: Record<string, string | number>; link: string | null }`; `class NotificationService { constructor(deps: { db: BursarDb; queue: JobQueue; bus: EventBus; settings: SettingsStore; emailEnabled: () => boolean; now?: () => number }); raise(input: RaiseInput): number | null; list(limit: number): NotificationListResponse; markRead(id: number): boolean; markAllRead(): number; get(id: number): NotificationItem | null; setEmailStatus(id: number, status: "sent" | "failed" | "skipped", error?: string): void }` (`raise` inserts or returns `null` on a dedupe hit; publishes `notification.created`; enqueues `notify.email` with `emailDedupeKey(id)` and sets `email_status = pending` only when `emailEnabled()` and settings have `emailNotifications` and a `notificationEmail`, else `skipped`).
  - `notifications/mailer.ts`: `interface MailMessage { to: string; subject: string; text: string }`; `interface Mailer { send(message: MailMessage): Promise<void>; verify(): Promise<void> }`; `createSmtpMailer(smtp: NonNullable<Config["smtp"]>): Mailer` (nodemailer per deps-notes: `secure` for `tls`, `requireTLS` for `starttls`, `ignoreTLS` for `none`, `tls.minVersion: "TLSv1.2"`, timeouts 10/10/20 s, `from` = `smtp.from`); `class MemoryMailer implements Mailer { sent: MailMessage[]; failNext?: Error }` (tests and QA).
  - `notifications/templates.ts`: `renderEmail(input: { event: NotificationEvent | "test"; locale: "it" | "en"; panelUrl: string }): { subject: string; text: string }` (subject "Bursar: <event title>", body = title sentence + link + a footer saying details are in the panel; no params, no amounts, no bank or account names).
  - `notifications/email-job.ts`: `emailJobHandler(deps: { service: NotificationService; mailer: Mailer | null; settings: SettingsStore; publicUrl: URL }): JobHandler` (missing mailer or recipient → `skipped`; send failure → rethrow for retry; on the last attempt mark `failed` with a reduced error message (no credentials)).
  - `notifications/routes.ts`: `notificationRoutes(deps: { service: NotificationService; mailer: Mailer | null; settings: SettingsStore; publicUrl: URL }): Hono<AppEnv>` mounted at `/api/notifications`: `GET /?limit=<1..50, default 6>` → `NotificationListResponse`; `POST /:notificationId/read` → 204 (404 `{ error: "Not found" }`); `POST /read-all` → `{ updated: number }`; `POST /test-email` → 202 `TestEmailResponse` | 409 `{ error, code: "smtp_not_configured" }` | 409 `{ error, code: "recipient_missing" }` | 502 `{ error: "The mail server refused the message", code: "smtp_failed" }` (no server response text).
  - `server.ts`: `StartOverrides` gains `mailer?: Mailer | null`; `mailer = overrides.mailer !== undefined ? overrides.mailer : config.smtp ? createSmtpMailer(config.smtp) : null`; registers `EMAIL_JOB`; mounts the router; exposes `notifications` for later tasks.

**Additions beyond the contract** (new names only; nothing above is renamed or changed):
- `@bursar/shared`: `NOTIFICATION_DEFAULT_LIMIT = 6`, `NOTIFICATION_MAX_LIMIT = 50`, `notificationParamsSchema`, `notificationListQuerySchema`, `notificationListResponseSchema`, `testEmailResponseSchema` (the types named in the contract are inferred from these).
- `mailer.ts`: `smtpTransportOptions(smtp): SMTPTransportOptions` (the pure mode-to-options mapping, unit-tested without a network) and `describeMailError(error: unknown): string` (`"SMTP delivery failed (EAUTH, 535)"`: only the nodemailer error code and the SMTP status number, never the server text).
- `templates.ts`: `type EmailLocale = "it" | "en"`, `type EmailEvent = NotificationEvent | "test"`, `emailTitle(event, locale): string`, `panelUrlFor(publicUrl: URL, link: string | null): string` (absolute panel URL; a link that is not a panel path, such as `https://…`, `//host` or `javascript:…`, falls back to the panel home).
- `service.ts`: `EMAIL_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 4` (email jobs are enqueued with `maxAttempts: 4`, retried after 30 s, 2 min and 8 min by the queue backoff), `NotificationServiceDeps`.
- Test support (not shipped): `startSmtpStub()` in `test/smtp-stub.ts` (a loopback plain-text SMTP server, so the real nodemailer path is exercised with `security: "none"` and no mail leaves the machine) and `createNotificationFixture()` in `test/notifications.ts`.

**Behaviour decided here** (the contract leaves it open):
- `markRead(id)` is idempotent: `true` whenever the notification exists (an already-read one keeps its original `readAt`), `false` only for an unknown id. The route answers 204 or 404 accordingly.
- `raise` opens no transaction of its own so a caller can call it inside `FinanceRepository.transaction` (Drizzle's top-level `transaction` cannot nest). If queueing the email job throws, the notification stays, is marked `skipped`, and the error is rethrown.
- `emailJobHandler` re-reads the recipient, the language and the `emailNotifications` switch when the job runs: a job still queued after the owner disabled email, removed the address or changed language behaves according to the current settings (`skipped` or the new language).
- A delivery error is stored and thrown as `describeMailError(error)` only; on the last attempt (`job.attempts >= job.maxAttempts`) `email_status` becomes `failed` first. A failed email never changes or hides the panel notification.
- `GET /api/notifications` answers 400 `{ "error": "Invalid request" }` for a `limit` outside 1 to 50 or not an integer. A malformed or unknown id on `POST /:notificationId/read` is a 404 `{ "error": "Not found" }` that does not echo the id.
- `POST /test-email` sends synchronously (so the owner sees an SMTP failure immediately) and answers 202. It checks the mailer first (`smtp_not_configured`), then the recipient (`recipient_missing`). It ignores the `emailNotifications` switch: a test must work before the switch is turned on.

`apps/server/src/test/smtp-stub.ts`:

```ts
import net from "node:net";

export interface SmtpStub {
  host: string;
  port: number;
  /** Raw DATA section of every accepted message (headers and body). */
  messages: string[];
  close(): Promise<void>;
}

/**
 * A minimal plain-text SMTP server on the loopback interface, enough for nodemailer to connect,
 * verify and deliver one message. Tests use it with `security: "none"`, so no mail ever leaves
 * the machine. `rejectRecipients` makes it answer `550` to RCPT TO.
 */
export async function startSmtpStub(
  options: { rejectRecipients?: boolean } = {},
): Promise<SmtpStub> {
  const messages: string[] = [];
  const sockets = new Set<net.Socket>();
  const server = net.createServer((socket) => {
    sockets.add(socket);
    socket.on("close", () => sockets.delete(socket));
    socket.on("error", () => {});
    let buffer = "";
    let inData = false;
    const reply = (line: string) => socket.write(`${line}\r\n`);
    reply("220 stub ESMTP");
    socket.on("data", (chunk) => {
      buffer += chunk.toString("utf8");
      for (;;) {
        if (inData) {
          const end = buffer.indexOf("\r\n.\r\n");
          if (end === -1) return;
          messages.push(buffer.slice(0, end));
          buffer = buffer.slice(end + 5);
          inData = false;
          reply("250 queued");
          continue;
        }
        const eol = buffer.indexOf("\r\n");
        if (eol === -1) return;
        const line = buffer.slice(0, eol);
        buffer = buffer.slice(eol + 2);
        const verb = line.slice(0, 4).toUpperCase();
        if (verb === "EHLO") socket.write("250-stub\r\n250 8BITMIME\r\n");
        else if (verb === "RCPT" && options.rejectRecipients) reply("550 no such mailbox");
        else if (verb === "DATA") {
          inData = true;
          reply("354 go ahead");
        } else if (verb === "QUIT") {
          reply("221 bye");
          socket.end();
        } else reply("250 ok");
      }
    });
  });
  await new Promise<void>((resolve) => server.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", resolve));
  const address = server.address();
  if (typeof address !== "object" || address === null) throw new Error("SMTP stub did not bind");
  return {
    host: "127.0.0.1",
    port: address.port,
    messages,
    close: () =>
      new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
        for (const socket of sockets) socket.destroy();
        server.close(() => resolve());
      }),
  };
}
```

```ts
import type { ServerEvent } from "@bursar/shared";
import { eq } from "drizzle-orm";
import { notifications } from "../db/schema";
import { EventBus } from "../events/bus";
import { JobQueue } from "../jobs/queue";
import { MemoryMailer } from "../notifications/mailer";
import { NotificationService } from "../notifications/service";
import { SettingsStore } from "../settings/store";
import { createTestDatabase, type TestDatabase } from "./db";

export const TEST_PUBLIC_URL = new URL("https://bursar.example.test");
export const TEST_RECIPIENT = "owner@example.test";

export interface NotificationFixture {
  t: TestDatabase;
  queue: JobQueue;
  bus: EventBus;
  settings: SettingsStore;
  service: NotificationService;
  mailer: MemoryMailer;
  /** Every event published on the bus. */
  events: ServerEvent[];
  /** Mutable clock shared by the queue and the service. */
  clock: { now: number };
  /** Mutable switch behind `emailEnabled` (true: a mailer is configured). */
  mail: { enabled: boolean };
  emailRow(id: number): { status: string; sentAt: number | null; error: string | null } | null;
  dispose(): void;
}

/** Real database, queue, bus, settings and service; email enabled with a recipient set. */
export function createNotificationFixture(): NotificationFixture {
  const t = createTestDatabase();
  const clock = { now: 1_700_000_000_000 };
  const mail = { enabled: true };
  const now = () => clock.now;
  const queue = new JobQueue(t.sqlite, now);
  const bus = new EventBus();
  const events: ServerEvent[] = [];
  bus.subscribe((event) => events.push(event));
  const settings = new SettingsStore(t.db, now);
  settings.update({ notificationEmail: TEST_RECIPIENT });
  const service = new NotificationService({
    db: t.db,
    queue,
    bus,
    settings,
    emailEnabled: () => mail.enabled,
    now,
  });
  return {
    t,
    queue,
    bus,
    settings,
    service,
    mailer: new MemoryMailer(),
    events,
    clock,
    mail,
    emailRow: (id) => {
      const row = t.db.select().from(notifications).where(eq(notifications.id, id)).get();
      return row
        ? { status: row.emailStatus, sentAt: row.emailSentAt, error: row.emailError }
        : null;
    },
    dispose: () => t.dispose(),
  };
}
```

```ts
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";
import { emailDedupeKey } from "../jobs/types";
import { createNotificationFixture, type NotificationFixture } from "../test/notifications";
import { notificationKeys } from "./keys";
import type { RaiseInput } from "./service";

const expiring = (overrides: Partial<RaiseInput> = {}): RaiseInput => ({
  event: "consent_expiring",
  dedupeKey: notificationKeys.consentExpiring(1, 1_800_000_000_000, 14),
  params: { bankName: "Banca Esempio", days: 14 },
  link: "/accounts",
  ...overrides,
});

describe("notificationKeys", () => {
  it("builds stable strings", () => {
    expect(notificationKeys.consentExpiring(7, 1_800_000_000_000, 14)).toBe(
      "consent-expiring:7:1800000000000:14",
    );
    expect(notificationKeys.consentExpiring(7, 1_800_000_000_000, 3)).toBe(
      "consent-expiring:7:1800000000000:3",
    );
    expect(notificationKeys.consentExpired(7, 1_800_000_000_000)).toBe(
      "consent-expired:7:1800000000000",
    );
    expect(notificationKeys.connectionError(7, 1_700_000_000_000)).toBe(
      "connection-error:7:1700000000000",
    );
    expect(notificationKeys.syncFailing(4, "2026-11-01")).toBe("sync-failing:4:2026-11-01");
    expect(notificationKeys.syncFailing(4, "never")).toBe("sync-failing:4:never");
    expect(notificationKeys.backupFailing("2026-11-09")).toBe("backup-failing:2026-11-09");
  });

  it("gives a renewed consent a new key and keeps thresholds apart", () => {
    const before = notificationKeys.consentExpiring(1, 1_800_000_000_000, 14);
    expect(notificationKeys.consentExpiring(1, 1_810_000_000_000, 14)).not.toBe(before);
    expect(notificationKeys.consentExpiring(1, 1_800_000_000_000, 3)).not.toBe(before);
  });
});

describe("NotificationService", () => {
  let f: NotificationFixture;

  beforeEach(() => {
    f = createNotificationFixture();
  });
  afterEach(() => f.dispose());

  it("stores a notification and tells the panel", () => {
    const id = f.service.raise(expiring());
    expect(id).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(f.service.list(10)).toEqual({
      items: [
        {
          id,
          event: "consent_expiring",
          params: { bankName: "Banca Esempio", days: 14 },
          link: "/accounts",
          createdAt: f.clock.now,
          readAt: null,
        },
      ],
      unread: 1,
    });
    expect(f.events).toEqual([{ type: "notification.created", id, event: "consent_expiring" }]);
  });

  it("returns null for a repeated dedupe key and publishes nothing more", () => {
    expect(f.service.raise(expiring())).not.toBeNull();
    expect(f.service.raise(expiring({ params: { bankName: "Other", days: 13 } }))).toBeNull();
    expect(f.service.list(10).items).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(f.events).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(f.queue.findActive(emailDedupeKey(1))).not.toBeNull();
    expect(f.service.raise(expiring({ dedupeKey: "other" }))).not.toBeNull();
  });

  it("queues one email job when email is available, switched on and a recipient is set", () => {
    const id = f.service.raise(expiring());
    if (id === null) throw new Error("expected a notification");
    expect(f.queue.findActive(emailDedupeKey(id))).toMatchObject({ status: "queued" });
    expect(f.emailRow(id)).toEqual({ status: "pending", sentAt: null, error: null });
    const job = f.queue.claimNext();
    expect(job).toMatchObject({
      type: "notify.email",
      payload: { notificationId: id },
      maxAttempts: 4,
    });
  });

  it("does not queue an email when no mailer is configured", () => {
    f.mail.enabled = false;
    const id = f.service.raise(expiring());
    if (id === null) throw new Error("expected a notification");
    expect(f.queue.findActive(emailDedupeKey(id))).toBeNull();
    expect(f.emailRow(id)?.status).toBe("skipped");
  });

  it("does not queue an email when the setting is off or the recipient is missing", () => {
    f.settings.update({ emailNotifications: false });
    const off = f.service.raise(expiring({ dedupeKey: "off" }));
    f.settings.update({ emailNotifications: true, notificationEmail: null });
    const noRecipient = f.service.raise(expiring({ dedupeKey: "no-recipient" }));
    for (const id of [off, noRecipient]) {
      if (id === null) throw new Error("expected a notification");
      expect(f.queue.findActive(emailDedupeKey(id))).toBeNull();
      expect(f.emailRow(id)?.status).toBe("skipped");
    }
    expect(f.service.list(10).items).toHaveLength(2);
  });

  it("joins a transaction the caller already opened", () => {
    let committed: number | null = null;
    f.t.sqlite.transaction(() => {
      committed = f.service.raise(expiring({ dedupeKey: "inside-commit" }));
    })();
    expect(committed).not.toBeNull();
    expect(f.service.list(10).items).toHaveLength(1);

    expect(() =>
      f.t.sqlite.transaction(() => {
        f.service.raise(expiring({ dedupeKey: "inside-rollback" }));
        throw new Error("caller failed");
      })(),
    ).toThrow("caller failed");
    expect(f.service.list(10).items).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(f.queue.findActive(emailDedupeKey(2))).toBeNull();
  });

  it("keeps the notification, marked skipped, when the email job cannot be queued", () => {
    vi.spyOn(f.queue, "enqueueUnique").mockImplementation(() => {
      throw new Error("database is busy");
    });
    expect(() => f.service.raise(expiring())).toThrow("database is busy");
    const { items } = f.service.list(10);
    expect(items).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(f.emailRow(items[0]?.id ?? 0)?.status).toBe("skipped");
  });

  it("lists newest first, limited, with the total unread count", () => {
    for (let n = 1; n <= 5; n += 1) {
      f.clock.now += 1_000;
      f.service.raise(expiring({ dedupeKey: `k${n}`, params: { n } }));
    }
    const { items, unread } = f.service.list(3);
    expect(items.map((item) => item.params.n)).toEqual([5, 4, 3]);
    expect(unread).toBe(5);
  });

  it("breaks a tie on the creation time by id", () => {
    f.service.raise(expiring({ dedupeKey: "a", params: { n: 1 } }));
    f.service.raise(expiring({ dedupeKey: "b", params: { n: 2 } }));
    expect(f.service.list(10).items.map((item) => item.params.n)).toEqual([2, 1]);
  });

  it("marks one notification read, idempotently, and reports a missing one", () => {
    const id = f.service.raise(expiring());
    if (id === null) throw new Error("expected a notification");
    f.clock.now += 5_000;
    const readAt = f.clock.now;
    expect(f.service.markRead(id)).toBe(true);
    f.clock.now += 5_000;
    expect(f.service.markRead(id)).toBe(true);
    expect(f.service.get(id)?.readAt).toBe(readAt);
    expect(f.service.list(10).unread).toBe(0);
    expect(f.service.markRead(9_999)).toBe(false);
  });

  it("marks everything read and counts only the notifications that changed", () => {
    const first = f.service.raise(expiring({ dedupeKey: "a" }));
    f.service.raise(expiring({ dedupeKey: "b" }));
    f.service.raise(expiring({ dedupeKey: "c" }));
    if (first === null) throw new Error("expected a notification");
    f.service.markRead(first);
    expect(f.service.markAllRead()).toBe(2);
    expect(f.service.markAllRead()).toBe(0);
    expect(f.service.list(10).unread).toBe(0);
  });

  it("records the email outcome", () => {
    const id = f.service.raise(expiring());
    if (id === null) throw new Error("expected a notification");
    f.clock.now += 1_000;
    f.service.setEmailStatus(id, "sent");
    expect(f.emailRow(id)).toEqual({ status: "sent", sentAt: f.clock.now, error: null });
    f.service.setEmailStatus(id, "failed", "x".repeat(500));
    expect(f.emailRow(id)).toMatchObject({ status: "failed", sentAt: null });
    expect(f.emailRow(id)?.error).toHaveLength(200);
    f.service.setEmailStatus(id, "skipped");
    expect(f.emailRow(id)).toEqual({ status: "skipped", sentAt: null, error: null });
  });

  it("returns null for an unknown id", () => {
    expect(f.service.get(123)).toBeNull();
  });

  it("tolerates unreadable params and hides events this build does not know", () => {
    f.t.sqlite
      .prepare(
        `INSERT INTO notifications (event, dedupe_key, params, link, created_at, email_status)
         VALUES ('consent_expired', 'bad-params', 'not json', NULL, ?, 'skipped'),
                ('report_ready', 'future-event', '{}', NULL, ?, 'skipped')`,
      )
      .run(f.clock.now, f.clock.now);
    const { items } = f.service.list(10);
    expect(items).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(items[0]).toMatchObject({ event: "consent_expired", params: {}, link: null });
  });
});
```

```ts
import { afterEach, describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import type { Config } from "../config";
import { type SmtpStub, startSmtpStub } from "../test/smtp-stub";
import { createSmtpMailer, describeMailError, MemoryMailer, smtpTransportOptions } from "./mailer";

type Smtp = NonNullable<Config["smtp"]>;

const smtp = (overrides: Partial<Smtp> = {}): Smtp => ({
  host: "smtp.example.test",
  port: 587,
  security: "starttls",
  user: "bursar",
  password: "not-a-real-password",
  from: "Bursar <bursar@example.test>",
  ...overrides,
});

describe("smtpTransportOptions", () => {
  it("requires the STARTTLS upgrade in starttls mode", () => {
    expect(smtpTransportOptions(smtp())).toMatchObject({
      host: "smtp.example.test",
      port: 587,
      secure: false,
      requireTLS: true,
      ignoreTLS: false,
      auth: { user: "bursar", pass: "not-a-real-password" },
      tls: { minVersion: "TLSv1.2" },
      connectionTimeout: 10_000,
      greetingTimeout: 10_000,
      socketTimeout: 20_000,
    });
  });

  it("uses implicit TLS in tls mode", () => {
    expect(smtpTransportOptions(smtp({ security: "tls", port: 465 }))).toMatchObject({
      port: 465,
      secure: true,
      requireTLS: false,
      ignoreTLS: false,
    });
  });

  it("turns TLS off only in none mode", () => {
    expect(smtpTransportOptions(smtp({ security: "none", host: "127.0.0.1" }))).toMatchObject({
      secure: false,
      requireTLS: false,
      ignoreTLS: true,
    });
  });

  it("sends no credentials when none are configured", () => {
    expect(smtpTransportOptions(smtp({ user: null, password: null })).auth).toBeUndefined();
  });
});

describe("MemoryMailer", () => {
  it("records messages", async () => {
    const mailer = new MemoryMailer();
    await mailer.send({ to: "owner@example.test", subject: "Subject", text: "Body" });
    expect(mailer.sent).toEqual([{ to: "owner@example.test", subject: "Subject", text: "Body" }]);
  });

  it("fails once when asked to, then recovers", async () => {
    const mailer = new MemoryMailer();
    mailer.failNext = new Error("boom");
    await expect(mailer.send({ to: "a@example.test", subject: "s", text: "t" })).rejects.toThrow(
      "boom",
    );
    expect(mailer.sent).toHaveLength(0);
    await mailer.send({ to: "a@example.test", subject: "s", text: "t" });
    expect(mailer.sent).toHaveLength(1);
    mailer.failNext = new Error("verify failed");
    await expect(mailer.verify()).rejects.toThrow("verify failed");
    await expect(mailer.verify()).resolves.toBeUndefined();
  });
});

describe("describeMailError", () => {
  it("keeps only the error code and the SMTP status", () => {
    const error = Object.assign(new Error("535 5.7.8 bad credentials for mario@example.test"), {
      code: "EAUTH",
      responseCode: 535,
      response: "535 5.7.8 bad credentials for mario@example.test",
    });
    expect(describeMailError(error)).toBe("SMTP delivery failed (EAUTH, 535)");
  });

  it("falls back to a generic message", () => {
    expect(describeMailError(new Error("secret-token in the message"))).toBe(
      "SMTP delivery failed",
    );
    expect(describeMailError("a string")).toBe("SMTP delivery failed");
    expect(describeMailError(Object.assign(new Error("x"), { code: "not a code!" }))).toBe(
      "SMTP delivery failed",
    );
  });
});

describe("createSmtpMailer", () => {
  let stub: SmtpStub | null = null;
  afterEach(async () => {
    await stub?.close();
    stub = null;
  });

  const loopback = (port: number): Smtp =>
    smtp({ host: "127.0.0.1", port, security: "none", user: null, password: null });

  it("delivers a plain-text message through an SMTP server", async () => {
    stub = await startSmtpStub();
    const mailer = createSmtpMailer(loopback(stub.port));
    await mailer.verify();
    await mailer.send({
      to: "owner@example.test",
      subject: "Bursar: Test message",
      text: "Test message.\n\nhttps://bursar.example.test/settings\n",
    });
    expect(stub.messages).toHaveLength(1);
    const message = stub.messages[0] ?? "";
    expect(message).toContain("From: Bursar <bursar@example.test>");
    expect(message).toContain("To: owner@example.test");
    expect(message).toContain("Subject: Bursar: Test message");
    expect(message).toContain("https://bursar.example.test/settings");
  });

  it("rejects when the server refuses the recipient, with a reducible error", async () => {
    stub = await startSmtpStub({ rejectRecipients: true });
    const mailer = createSmtpMailer(loopback(stub.port));
    const error = await mailer.send({ to: "owner@example.test", subject: "s", text: "t" }).then(
      () => null,
      (caught: unknown) => caught,
    );
    expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(Error);
    expect(describeMailError(error)).toBe("SMTP delivery failed (EENVELOPE, 550)");
  });

  it("rejects when nothing listens on the port", async () => {
    stub = await startSmtpStub();
    const port = stub.port;
    await stub.close();
    stub = null;
    const mailer = createSmtpMailer(loopback(port));
    await expect(
      mailer.send({ to: "owner@example.test", subject: "s", text: "t" }),
    ).rejects.toThrow();
  });
});
```

```ts
import { notificationEventSchema } from "@bursar/shared";
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { emailTitle, panelUrlFor, renderEmail } from "./templates";

const EVENTS = [...notificationEventSchema.options, "test"] as const;
const LOCALES = ["it", "en"] as const;
const PANEL_URL = "https://bursar.example.test/accounts";

describe("renderEmail", () => {
  it.each(LOCALES.flatMap((locale) => EVENTS.map((event) => ({ locale, event }))))(
    "renders $event in $locale as a title and a panel link",
    ({ locale, event }) => {
      const { subject, text } = renderEmail({ event, locale, panelUrl: PANEL_URL });
      expect(subject).toBe(`Bursar: ${emailTitle(event, locale)}`);
      expect(text.startsWith(`${emailTitle(event, locale)}.\n`)).toBe(true);
      expect(text).toContain(`\n${PANEL_URL}\n`);
      expect(text).not.toMatch(/undefined|\{|\}/);
      // The only digits in a message belong to the panel URL.
      expect(`${subject}\n${text.replace(PANEL_URL, "")}`).not.toMatch(/\d/);
    },
  );

  it("has a different title for every event and each language", () => {
    for (const locale of LOCALES) {
      const titles = EVENTS.map((event) => emailTitle(event, locale));
      expect(new Set(titles).size).toBe(EVENTS.length);
    }
    expect(emailTitle("backup_failing", "it")).not.toBe(emailTitle("backup_failing", "en"));
  });

  it("mentions that no financial data is included", () => {
    expect(renderEmail({ event: "test", locale: "en", panelUrl: PANEL_URL }).text).toContain(
      "contains no financial data",
    );
    expect(renderEmail({ event: "test", locale: "it", panelUrl: PANEL_URL }).text).toContain(
      "non contiene dati finanziari",
    );
  });
});

describe("panelUrlFor", () => {
  const publicUrl = new URL("https://bursar.example.test");

  it("resolves panel paths, keeping the fragment", () => {
    expect(panelUrlFor(publicUrl, "/accounts/12")).toBe("https://bursar.example.test/accounts/12");
    expect(panelUrlFor(publicUrl, "/settings#backups")).toBe(
      "https://bursar.example.test/settings#backups",
    );
  });

  it("falls back to the panel home for no link or anything that is not a panel path", () => {
    for (const link of [
      null,
      "",
      "accounts",
      "https://evil.example.test/",
      "//evil.example.test/",
      "/\\evil.example.test",
      "javascript:alert(1)",
    ]) {
      expect(panelUrlFor(publicUrl, link)).toBe("https://bursar.example.test/");
    }
  });
});
```

`apps/server/src/notifications/email-job.test.ts`:

```ts
import { notificationEventSchema } from "@bursar/shared";
import { pino } from "pino";
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { EMAIL_JOB } from "../jobs/types";
import { type JobHandler, JobWorker } from "../jobs/worker";
import {
  createNotificationFixture,
  type NotificationFixture,
  TEST_PUBLIC_URL,
  TEST_RECIPIENT,
} from "../test/notifications";
import { emailJobHandler } from "./email-job";
import { notificationKeys } from "./keys";
import type { Mailer } from "./mailer";
import { renderEmail } from "./templates";

const logger = pino({ level: "silent" });
const HOUR_MS = 3_600_000;

describe("emailJobHandler", () => {
  let f: NotificationFixture;

  const worker = (mailer: Mailer | null = f.mailer): JobWorker =>
    new JobWorker(
      f.queue,
      new Map<string, JobHandler>([
        [
          EMAIL_JOB,
          emailJobHandler({
            service: f.service,
            mailer,
            settings: f.settings,
            publicUrl: TEST_PUBLIC_URL,
          }),
        ],
      ]),
      logger,
    );

  const raise = (params: Record<string, string | number> = { bankName: "Banca Esempio" }) => {
    const id = f.service.raise({
      event: "consent_expiring",
      dedupeKey: notificationKeys.consentExpiring(12, 1_800_000_000_000, 3),
      params,
      link: "/accounts/12",
    });
    if (id === null) throw new Error("expected a notification");
    return id;
  };

  beforeEach(() => {
    f = createNotificationFixture();
  });
  afterEach(() => f.dispose());

  it("sends the email, in the configured language, and marks it sent", async () => {
    const id = raise();
    f.settings.update({ locale: "en" });
    f.clock.now += 2_000;
    expect(await worker().runOnce()).toBe(true);
    const expected = renderEmail({
      event: "consent_expiring",
      locale: "en",
      panelUrl: "https://bursar.example.test/accounts/12",
    });
    expect(f.mailer.sent).toEqual([{ to: TEST_RECIPIENT, ...expected }]);
    expect(f.emailRow(id)).toEqual({ status: "sent", sentAt: f.clock.now, error: null });
  });

  it("leaks no parameter, amount, bank name or other digit into any message", async () => {
    const leakyParams = {
      bankName: "Banca Esempio",
      accountName: "Conto Casa",
      amount: 123456,
      days: 3,
      iban: "IT60X0542811101000000123456",
    };
    const w = worker();
    for (const locale of ["it", "en"] as const) {
      f.settings.update({ locale });
      for (const event of notificationEventSchema.options) {
        f.service.raise({
          event,
          dedupeKey: `${event}:${locale}`,
          params: leakyParams,
          link: "/accounts/12",
        });
        await w.runOnce();
      }
    }
    expect(f.mailer.sent).toHaveLength(10);
    for (const { subject, text, to } of f.mailer.sent) {
      expect(to).toBe(TEST_RECIPIENT);
      const everything = `${subject}\n${text}`;
      for (const secret of ["Banca", "Esempio", "Conto Casa", "123456", "IT60", "iban", "€"]) {
        expect(everything).not.toContain(secret);
      }
      expect(text).toContain("\nhttps://bursar.example.test/accounts/12\n");
      const withoutUrl = everything.replace("https://bursar.example.test/accounts/12", "");
      expect(withoutUrl).not.toMatch(/\d/);
    }
  });

  it("retries a failed delivery with a reduced error and succeeds on the next attempt", async () => {
    const id = raise();
    const w = worker();
    f.mailer.failNext = Object.assign(new Error("535 bad credentials for secret-user"), {
      code: "EAUTH",
      responseCode: 535,
    });
    await w.runOnce();
    const jobId = f.queue.findActive(`email:${id}`)?.id;
    if (jobId === undefined) throw new Error("expected the job to be queued again");
    expect(f.queue.get(jobId)).toMatchObject({
      status: "queued",
      attempts: 1,
      lastError: "SMTP delivery failed (EAUTH, 535)",
    });
    expect(f.emailRow(id)?.status).toBe("pending");
    expect(await w.runOnce()).toBe(false);

    f.clock.now += HOUR_MS;
    await w.runOnce();
    expect(f.queue.get(jobId)?.status).toBe("succeeded");
    expect(f.emailRow(id)?.status).toBe("sent");
    expect(f.mailer.sent).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  it("marks the notification failed on the last attempt and keeps it in the panel", async () => {
    const id = raise();
    const jobId = f.queue.findActive(`email:${id}`)?.id;
    if (jobId === undefined) throw new Error("expected the job to be queued");
    const w = worker();
    for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= 4; attempt += 1) {
      f.mailer.failNext = Object.assign(new Error("password hunter2 rejected"), {
        code: "ECONNECTION",
      });
      f.clock.now += HOUR_MS;
      await w.runOnce();
      expect(f.emailRow(id)?.status).toBe(attempt < 4 ? "pending" : "failed");
    }
    expect(f.queue.get(jobId)).toMatchObject({
      status: "failed",
      attempts: 4,
      lastError: "SMTP delivery failed (ECONNECTION)",
    });
    expect(f.emailRow(id)).toEqual({
      status: "failed",
      sentAt: null,
      error: "SMTP delivery failed (ECONNECTION)",
    });
    expect(f.service.get(id)).not.toBeNull();
    expect(f.mailer.sent).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  it("skips when there is no mailer, no recipient or the setting was switched off", async () => {
    const noMailer = raise();
    await worker(null).runOnce();
    expect(f.emailRow(noMailer)?.status).toBe("skipped");

    const noRecipient = f.service.raise({
      event: "consent_expired",
      dedupeKey: "a",
      params: {},
      link: null,
    });
    f.settings.update({ notificationEmail: null });
    await worker().runOnce();
    expect(f.emailRow(noRecipient ?? 0)?.status).toBe("skipped");

    f.settings.update({ notificationEmail: TEST_RECIPIENT });
    const switchedOff = f.service.raise({
      event: "consent_expired",
      dedupeKey: "b",
      params: {},
      link: null,
    });
    f.settings.update({ emailNotifications: false });
    await worker().runOnce();
    expect(f.emailRow(switchedOff ?? 0)?.status).toBe("skipped");
    expect(f.mailer.sent).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  it("falls back to the panel home for a link that is not a panel path", async () => {
    f.service.raise({
      event: "connection_error",
      dedupeKey: "odd-link",
      params: {},
      link: "https://evil.example.test/phish",
    });
    await worker().runOnce();
    expect(f.mailer.sent[0]?.text).toContain("\nhttps://bursar.example.test/\n");
    expect(f.mailer.sent[0]?.text).not.toContain("evil");
  });

  it("completes quietly when the notification no longer exists", async () => {
    const jobId = f.queue.enqueue(EMAIL_JOB, { notificationId: 9_999 });
    await worker().runOnce();
    expect(f.queue.get(jobId)?.status).toBe("succeeded");
    expect(f.mailer.sent).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  it("fails a job with an invalid payload permanently", async () => {
    const jobId = f.queue.enqueue(EMAIL_JOB, { notificationId: "twelve" });
    await worker().runOnce();
    expect(f.queue.get(jobId)?.status).toBe("failed");
    expect(f.mailer.sent).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

```ts
import { notificationListResponseSchema } from "@bursar/shared";
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { createTestApp, type TestApp } from "../test/app";
import {
  createNotificationFixture,
  type NotificationFixture,
  TEST_PUBLIC_URL,
  TEST_RECIPIENT,
} from "../test/notifications";
import type { Mailer } from "./mailer";
import { notificationRoutes } from "./routes";
import { renderEmail } from "./templates";

describe("notification routes", () => {
  let f: NotificationFixture;

  const mount = (mailer: Mailer | null = f.mailer): Promise<TestApp> =>
    createTestApp({
      database: f.t,
      routers: [
        {
          prefix: "/api/notifications",
          router: notificationRoutes({
            service: f.service,
            mailer,
            settings: f.settings,
            publicUrl: TEST_PUBLIC_URL,
          }),
        },
      ],
    });

  /** A 204 has no body, so this goes through the raw app instead of `json()`. */
  const markRead = (app: TestApp, id: number): Promise<Response> =>
    Promise.resolve(
      app.app.request(`/api/notifications/${id}/read`, {
        method: "POST",
        headers: { origin: app.origin, cookie: app.cookie },
      }),
    );

  const raiseMany = (count: number) => {
    for (let n = 1; n <= count; n += 1) {
      f.clock.now += 1_000;
      f.service.raise({
        event: "sync_failing",
        dedupeKey: `sync-failing:${n}:never`,
        params: { accountName: `Account ${n}` },
        link: `/accounts/${n}`,
      });
    }
  };

  beforeEach(() => {
    f = createNotificationFixture();
  });
  afterEach(() => f.dispose());

  it("requires a session", async () => {
    const { app } = await mount();
    const response = await app.request("/api/notifications");
    expect(response.status).toBe(401);
  });

  it("lists the newest six by default with the unread count", async () => {
    const app = await mount();
    raiseMany(8);
    const response = await app.json("/api/notifications");
    expect(response.status).toBe(200);
    expect(response.headers.get("cache-control")).toBe("no-store");
    const body = notificationListResponseSchema.parse(response.body);
    expect(body.unread).toBe(8);
    expect(body.items).toHaveLength(6);
    expect(body.items[0]).toMatchObject({
      event: "sync_failing",
      params: { accountName: "Account 8" },
      link: "/accounts/8",
      readAt: null,
    });
  });

  it("honours the limit and rejects values outside 1 to 50", async () => {
    const app = await mount();
    raiseMany(4);
    const two = notificationListResponseSchema.parse(
      (await app.json("/api/notifications?limit=2")).body,
    );
    expect(two.items).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(two.unread).toBe(4);
    for (const limit of ["0", "51", "abc", "-1", "2.5"]) {
      const response = await app.json(`/api/notifications?limit=${limit}`);
      expect(response.status).toBe(400);
      expect(response.body).toEqual({ error: "Invalid request" });
    }
  });

  it("marks one notification read", async () => {
    const app = await mount();
    raiseMany(2);
    const first = notificationListResponseSchema.parse((await app.json("/api/notifications")).body)
      .items[0];
    const response = await markRead(app, first?.id ?? 0);
    expect(response.status).toBe(204);
    expect(await response.text()).toBe("");
    const after = notificationListResponseSchema.parse((await app.json("/api/notifications")).body);
    expect(after.unread).toBe(1);
    expect(after.items.find((item) => item.id === first?.id)?.readAt).not.toBeNull();
    expect((await markRead(app, first?.id ?? 0)).status).toBe(204);
  });

  it("answers 404 for an unknown or malformed id, without echoing it", async () => {
    const app = await mount();
    for (const id of ["999", "0", "abc", "1.5", "-3"]) {
      const response = await app.json(`/api/notifications/${id}/read`, { method: "POST" });
      expect(response.status).toBe(404);
      expect(response.body).toEqual({ error: "Not found" });
    }
  });

  it("marks everything read", async () => {
    const app = await mount();
    raiseMany(3);
    expect((await app.json("/api/notifications/read-all", { method: "POST" })).body).toEqual({
      updated: 3,
    });
    expect((await app.json("/api/notifications/read-all", { method: "POST" })).body).toEqual({
      updated: 0,
    });
    expect(
      notificationListResponseSchema.parse((await app.json("/api/notifications")).body).unread,
    ).toBe(0);
  });

  describe("POST /test-email", () => {
    it("sends a test message to the notification address in the configured language", async () => {
      const app = await mount();
      f.settings.update({ locale: "en" });
      const response = await app.json("/api/notifications/test-email", { method: "POST" });
      expect(response.status).toBe(202);
      expect(response.body).toEqual({ sent: true });
      expect(f.mailer.sent).toEqual([
        {
          to: TEST_RECIPIENT,
          ...renderEmail({
            event: "test",
            locale: "en",
            panelUrl: "https://bursar.example.test/settings",
          }),
        },
      ]);
    });

    it("answers 409 smtp_not_configured when there is no mailer", async () => {
      const app = await mount(null);
      const response = await app.json("/api/notifications/test-email", { method: "POST" });
      expect(response.status).toBe(409);
      expect(response.body).toEqual({
        error: "SMTP is not configured",
        code: "smtp_not_configured",
      });
    });

    it("answers 409 recipient_missing when no address is set", async () => {
      const app = await mount();
      f.settings.update({ notificationEmail: null });
      const response = await app.json("/api/notifications/test-email", { method: "POST" });
      expect(response.status).toBe(409);
      expect(response.body).toEqual({
        error: "No notification email address is set",
        code: "recipient_missing",
      });
      expect(f.mailer.sent).toHaveLength(0);
    });

    it("answers 502 smtp_failed without the server's error text", async () => {
      const app = await mount();
      f.mailer.failNext = Object.assign(
        new Error("535 5.7.8 Authentication failed for bursar-user: password hunter2"),
        { code: "EAUTH", responseCode: 535 },
      );
      const response = await app.json("/api/notifications/test-email", { method: "POST" });
      expect(response.status).toBe(502);
      expect(response.body).toEqual({
        error: "The mail server refused the message",
        code: "smtp_failed",
      });
      const serialised = JSON.stringify(response.body);
      for (const leaked of ["535", "hunter2", "bursar-user", "EAUTH"]) {
        expect(serialised).not.toContain(leaked);
      }
    });
  });
});
```

`apps/server/src/notifications/wiring.test.ts` boots the real server through `startBursar` with an injected `MemoryMailer` (the seed hook writes the recipient into the settings before the worker starts). The job worker polls once a second, hence the generous `waitFor` timeout:

```ts
import { mkdtempSync, rmSync } from "node:fs";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { pino } from "pino";
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";
import { loadConfig } from "../config";
import { type RunningBursar, startBursar } from "../server";
import { SettingsStore } from "../settings/store";
import { MIGRATIONS_DIR } from "../test/db";
import { notificationKeys } from "./keys";
import { MemoryMailer } from "./mailer";

describe("notifications in startBursar", () => {
  let dir: string;
  let running: RunningBursar[];

  beforeEach(() => {
    dir = mkdtempSync(path.join(tmpdir(), "bursar-notify-"));
    running = [];
  });
  afterEach(async () => {
    for (const instance of running) await instance.close();
    rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
  });

  async function boot(overrides: Parameters<typeof startBursar>[2]): Promise<RunningBursar> {
    const config = loadConfig({
      BURSAR_PUBLIC_URL: "http://127.0.0.1",
      TZ: "UTC",
      BURSAR_MASTER_KEY: Buffer.alloc(32, 3).toString("base64"),
      BURSAR_DATA_DIR: dir,
      BURSAR_MIGRATIONS_DIR: MIGRATIONS_DIR,
    });
    const instance = await startBursar(
      { ...config, port: 0 },
      pino({ level: "silent" }),
      overrides,
    );
    running.push(instance);
    return instance;
  }

  it("emails a raised notification through the injected mailer", async () => {
    const mailer = new MemoryMailer();
    const instance = await boot({
      mailer,
      seed: ({ db }) => {
        new SettingsStore(db).update({ notificationEmail: "owner@example.test" });
      },
    });
    const id = instance.notifications.raise({
      event: "backup_failing",
      dedupeKey: notificationKeys.backupFailing("2026-11-09"),
      params: { attempts: 2 },
      link: "/settings#backups",
    });
    expect(id).not.toBeNull();
    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(mailer.sent).toHaveLength(1), { timeout: 10_000, interval: 100 });
    expect(mailer.sent[0]?.to).toBe("owner@example.test");
    expect(mailer.sent[0]?.subject).toMatch(/^Bursar: /);
    expect(mailer.sent[0]?.text).toContain("http://127.0.0.1/settings#backups");
  });

  it("keeps notifications panel-only when there is no mailer", async () => {
    const instance = await boot({
      mailer: null,
      seed: ({ db }) => {
        new SettingsStore(db).update({ notificationEmail: "owner@example.test" });
      },
    });
    const id = instance.notifications.raise({
      event: "consent_expired",
      dedupeKey: notificationKeys.consentExpired(1, 1_800_000_000_000),
      params: {},
      link: "/accounts",
    });
    expect(id).not.toBeNull();
    expect(instance.notifications.list(5).items).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  it("serves /api/notifications behind the session check", async () => {
    const instance = await boot({ mailer: null });
    const response = await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${instance.port}/api/notifications`);
    expect(response.status).toBe(401);
  });
});
```
