`apps/server/src/finance/lifecycle.ts`:

```ts
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
import type {
  AccountStatus,
  DisconnectResponse,
  PurgeResponse,
  RemovalPreview,
} from "@bursar/shared";
import type { AuditLog } from "../audit";
import type { EnableBankingApi } from "../eb/client";
import { EnableBankingError } from "../eb/errors";
import type { EventBus } from "../events/bus";
import type { JobQueue } from "../jobs/queue";
import {
  DELETE_SESSION_JOB,
  type DeleteSessionPayload,
  deleteSessionPayloadSchema,
  parsePayload,
  syncDedupeKey,
} from "../jobs/types";
import { type JobHandler, PermanentJobError } from "../jobs/worker";
import type { FinanceRepository } from "./repository";

/** Enable Banking answers with one of these when the session is already over: nothing to close. */
export const SESSION_ENDED_CODES: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([
  "CLOSED_SESSION",
  "EXPIRED_SESSION",
  "SESSION_DOES_NOT_EXIST",
  "REVOKED_SESSION",
]);

/** The first retry waits a little: the bank has just failed to answer. */
export const DELETE_SESSION_RETRY_DELAY_MS = 5 * 60_000;
/** With the queue backoff: retries after 30 s, 2 min, 8 min, 32 min and 1 h. */
export const DELETE_SESSION_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 6;

const LIVE_ACCOUNT_STATUSES: readonly AccountStatus[] = ["active", "disabled", "unavailable"];

export function isSessionEnded(error: unknown): boolean {
  return (
    error instanceof EnableBankingError && error.code !== null && SESSION_ENDED_CODES.has(error.code)
  );
}

/** The provider session id stays in the job payload only; the key carries a hash of it. */
export function deleteSessionDedupeKey(providerSessionId: string): string {
  const digest = createHash("sha256").update(providerSessionId).digest("hex");
  return `delete-session:${digest.slice(0, 32)}`;
}

export function enqueueSessionDeletion(
  queue: JobQueue,
  providerSessionId: string,
  now: number,
): { id: number; created: boolean } {
  const payload: DeleteSessionPayload = { providerSessionId };
  return queue.enqueueUnique(DELETE_SESSION_JOB, deleteSessionDedupeKey(providerSessionId), payload, {
    runAfter: now + DELETE_SESSION_RETRY_DELAY_MS,
    maxAttempts: DELETE_SESSION_MAX_ATTEMPTS,
  });
}

export class AlreadyRemovedError extends Error {
  constructor() {
    super("The connection is already removed");
    this.name = "AlreadyRemovedError";
  }
}

export interface ConnectionLifecycleDeps {
  repo: FinanceRepository;
  api: EnableBankingApi | null;
  queue: JobQueue;
  bus: EventBus;
  audit: AuditLog;
  now?: () => number;
}

type RemoteSessionOutcome = "closed" | "already_ended" | "queued" | "local_only";

/**
 * Disconnecting a bank and purging what it left behind (spec §6.3). A disconnect keeps every
 * transaction; purging an account's data is a separate, explicitly confirmed action.
 */
export class ConnectionLifecycle {
  private readonly now: () => number;

  constructor(private readonly deps: ConnectionLifecycleDeps) {
    this.now = deps.now ?? Date.now;
  }

  removalPreview(connectionId: number): RemovalPreview | null {
    const { repo } = this.deps;
    const connection = repo.getConnection(connectionId);
    if (!connection) return null;
    const accounts = repo.listAccounts({ connectionId, statuses: LIVE_ACCOUNT_STATUSES });
    const transactions = accounts.reduce(
      (sum, account) => sum + repo.countTransactions(account.id).total,
      0,
    );
    return { bankName: connection.aspspName, accounts: accounts.length, transactions };
  }

  /**
   * Closes the bank session (best effort, retried by a job), then marks the connection and its
   * accounts removed in one transaction. Throws {@link AlreadyRemovedError} when it is removed.
   */
  async disconnect(connectionId: number): Promise<DisconnectResponse | null> {
    const { repo, queue, audit, bus } = this.deps;
    const connection = repo.getConnection(connectionId);
    if (!connection) return null;
    if (connection.removedAt !== null) throw new AlreadyRemovedError();

    const remoteSession = await this.closeRemoteSession(connection.providerSessionId);

    const now = this.now();
    const removedAccounts = repo.transaction((): number | null => {
      // Re-read: another disconnect may have finished while this one waited for the bank.
      const current = repo.getConnection(connectionId);
      if (!current) return null;
      if (current.removedAt !== null) throw new AlreadyRemovedError();
      repo.updateConnection(connectionId, { removedAt: now });
      const accounts = repo.listAccounts({ connectionId, statuses: LIVE_ACCOUNT_STATUSES });
      for (const account of accounts) {
        repo.updateAccount(account.id, { status: "removed", removedAt: now });
        queue.cancelQueued(syncDedupeKey(account.id));
      }
      audit.record({
        actor: "user",
        action: "connection.remove",
        target: `connection:${connectionId}`,
        details: { accounts: accounts.length, remoteSession },
      });
      return accounts.length;
    });
    if (removedAccounts === null) return null;

    // No time zone in this service: the event carries the stored status; the panel refetches.
    bus.publish({ type: "connection.updated", connectionId, status: connection.status });
    return { removedAccounts };
  }

  /** Deletes a removed account's data; deletes the connection row once its last account is gone. */
  purgeAccount(accountId: number): PurgeResponse | "not_removed" | null {
    const { repo, queue, audit } = this.deps;
    const account = repo.getAccount(accountId);
    if (!account) return null;
    if (account.status !== "removed") return "not_removed";

    queue.cancelQueued(syncDedupeKey(accountId));
    const counts = repo.purgeAccount(accountId);
    const connection = repo.getConnection(account.connectionId);
    const connectionDeleted =
      connection !== null &&
      connection.removedAt !== null &&
      repo.listAccounts({ connectionId: connection.id }).length === 0 &&
      repo.deleteConnection(connection.id);

    audit.record({
      actor: "user",
      action: "account.purge",
      target: `account:${accountId}`,
      details: {
        transactions: counts.transactions,
        balances: counts.balances,
        syncRuns: counts.syncRuns,
        connectionDeleted,
      },
    });
    return { transactions: counts.transactions, balances: counts.balances };
  }

  private async closeRemoteSession(providerSessionId: string): Promise<RemoteSessionOutcome> {
    const { api, queue } = this.deps;
    if (!api) return "local_only";
    try {
      // No PSU headers: the owner is not at the bank, and a close never needs them.
      await api.deleteSession(providerSessionId);
      return "closed";
    } catch (error) {
      if (isSessionEnded(error)) return "already_ended";
      enqueueSessionDeletion(queue, providerSessionId, this.now());
      return "queued";
    }
  }
}

/**
 * `bank.delete-session`: closes a provider session left open by a disconnect or a renewal.
 * Error messages are the reduced `EnableBankingError` messages, never the session id.
 */
export function deleteSessionJobHandler(deps: { api: EnableBankingApi | null }): JobHandler {
  return async (job) => {
    const { providerSessionId } = parsePayload(deleteSessionPayloadSchema, job);
    if (!deps.api) throw new PermanentJobError("Enable Banking is not configured");
    try {
      await deps.api.deleteSession(providerSessionId);
    } catch (error) {
      if (isSessionEnded(error)) return;
      if (error instanceof EnableBankingError) {
        if (error.kind === "retry" || error.kind === "rate_limited") throw error;
        throw new PermanentJobError(error.message);
      }
      throw new PermanentJobError("Closing the bank session failed unexpectedly");
    }
  };
}
```

`apps/server/src/finance/lifecycle-routes.ts`:

```ts
import { purgeRequestSchema } from "@bursar/shared";
import { Hono } from "hono";
import type { AppEnv } from "../http/app";
import { AlreadyRemovedError, type ConnectionLifecycle } from "./lifecycle";

const ID_PATTERN = /^[1-9]\d{0,14}$/;
const NOT_FOUND = { error: "Not found", code: "not_found" } as const;

/** A positive integer id from the path, or null; the raw value is never echoed back. */
function parseId(value: string): number | null {
  return ID_PATTERN.test(value) ? Number(value) : null;
}

export function lifecycleRoutes(deps: { lifecycle: ConnectionLifecycle }): Hono<AppEnv> {
  const routes = new Hono<AppEnv>();

  routes.get("/connections/:connectionId/removal-preview", (c) => {
    const id = parseId(c.req.param("connectionId"));
    const preview = id === null ? null : deps.lifecycle.removalPreview(id);
    return preview ? c.json(preview) : c.json(NOT_FOUND, 404);
  });

  routes.delete("/connections/:connectionId", async (c) => {
    const id = parseId(c.req.param("connectionId"));
    if (id === null) return c.json(NOT_FOUND, 404);
    try {
      const result = await deps.lifecycle.disconnect(id);
      return result ? c.json(result) : c.json(NOT_FOUND, 404);
    } catch (error) {
      if (error instanceof AlreadyRemovedError) {
        return c.json({ error: "The connection is already removed", code: "already_removed" }, 409);
      }
      throw error;
    }
  });

  routes.post("/accounts/:accountId/purge", async (c) => {
    const id = parseId(c.req.param("accountId"));
    if (id === null) return c.json(NOT_FOUND, 404);
    const body = purgeRequestSchema.safeParse(await c.req.json().catch(() => null));
    if (!body.success) {
      return c.json(
        { error: "Purging needs an explicit confirmation", code: "confirmation_required" },
        400,
      );
    }
    const result = deps.lifecycle.purgeAccount(id);
    if (result === null) return c.json(NOT_FOUND, 404);
    if (result === "not_removed") {
      return c.json(
        { error: "Only a removed account can be purged", code: "account_not_removed" },
        409,
      );
    }
    return c.json(result);
  });

  return routes;
}
```

```ts
import { calendarDaysUntil, EXPIRING_THRESHOLD_DAYS, URGENT_THRESHOLD_DAYS } from "@bursar/shared";
import type { Logger } from "pino";
import type { EnableBankingApi } from "../eb/client";
import { EnableBankingError } from "../eb/errors";
import type { EbSessionStatus } from "../eb/schemas";
import type { EventBus } from "../events/bus";
import { notificationKeys } from "../notifications/keys";
import type { NotificationService } from "../notifications/service";
import type { ScheduledTask } from "../scheduler";
import { markConnectionEnded } from "./connection-status";
import type { ConnectionRow, FinanceRepository } from "./repository";

/** `GET /sessions/{id}` is asked at most this often per connection. */
export const SESSION_STATUS_CHECK_INTERVAL_MS = 24 * 3_600_000;

type EndedStatus = "expired" | "revoked" | "error";

/**
 * Session states that end a connection (eb-api-notes.md §6, medium confidence). AUTHORIZED,
 * PENDING_AUTHORIZATION and RETURNED_FROM_BANK leave it alone.
 */
export const SESSION_STATUS_OUTCOMES: Readonly<
  Partial<Record<EbSessionStatus["status"], EndedStatus>>
> = {
  EXPIRED: "expired",
  REVOKED: "revoked",
  CLOSED: "error",
  CANCELLED: "error",
  INVALID: "error",
};

/** Same mapping as the sync job (Task 13) for a reauth-kind Enable Banking error. */
export function endedStatusForReauthCode(code: string | null): EndedStatus {
  if (code === "EXPIRED_SESSION") return "expired";
  if (code === "REVOKED_SESSION") return "revoked";
  return "error";
}

export interface ConsentTaskDeps {
  repo: FinanceRepository;
  api: EnableBankingApi | null;
  notifications: NotificationService;
  bus: EventBus;
  timezone: string;
  now: () => number;
  logger: Logger;
}

/**
 * Runs on every scheduler tick and decides from stored state alone: consent expiry by date, a
 * daily bank-side session check, and the 14- and 3-day notices (spec §6.3, §6.9). Notices are
 * keyed by `validUntil`, so a renewal starts the thresholds over.
 */
export function consentTask(deps: ConsentTaskDeps): ScheduledTask {
  async function sessionHasEnded(connection: ConnectionRow, now: number): Promise<boolean> {
    const { api } = deps;
    if (!api) return false;
    if (
      connection.statusCheckedAt !== null &&
      now - connection.statusCheckedAt < SESSION_STATUS_CHECK_INTERVAL_MS
    ) {
      return false;
    }
    // Recorded before the call, so a failing check is retried the next day, not on every tick.
    deps.repo.updateConnection(connection.id, { statusCheckedAt: now });
    let status: EbSessionStatus["status"];
    try {
      status = (await api.getSession(connection.providerSessionId)).status;
    } catch (error) {
      if (error instanceof EnableBankingError && error.kind === "reauth") {
        markConnectionEnded(deps, connection.id, endedStatusForReauthCode(error.code), {
          code: error.code,
          message: null,
        });
        return true;
      }
      const ebError = error instanceof EnableBankingError ? error : null;
      deps.logger.warn(
        {
          connectionId: connection.id,
          status: ebError ? ebError.status : null,
          code: ebError ? ebError.code : null,
        },
        "Bank session status check failed",
      );
      return false;
    }
    const ended = SESSION_STATUS_OUTCOMES[status];
    if (!ended) return false;
    markConnectionEnded(deps, connection.id, ended, { code: `SESSION_${status}`, message: null });
    return true;
  }

  function raiseExpiryNotice(connection: ConnectionRow, now: number): void {
    const days = calendarDaysUntil(connection.validUntil, now, deps.timezone);
    // Only the most urgent threshold applies to one evaluation.
    const threshold =
      days <= URGENT_THRESHOLD_DAYS ? 3 : days <= EXPIRING_THRESHOLD_DAYS ? 14 : null;
    if (threshold === null) return;
    deps.notifications.raise({
      event: "consent_expiring",
      dedupeKey: notificationKeys.consentExpiring(connection.id, connection.validUntil, threshold),
      params: { bankName: connection.aspspName, days },
      link: "/accounts",
    });
  }

  return {
    name: "consent-lifecycle",
    async run() {
      const now = deps.now();
      for (const connection of deps.repo.listConnections()) {
        if (connection.removedAt !== null || connection.status !== "active") continue;
        if (connection.validUntil <= now) {
          markConnectionEnded(deps, connection.id, "expired");
          continue;
        }
        if (await sessionHasEnded(connection, now)) continue;
        raiseExpiryNotice(connection, now);
      }
    },
  };
}
```

```ts
import { accountDisplayName, effectiveConnectionStatus, toLocalDate } from "@bursar/shared";
import { notificationKeys } from "../notifications/keys";
import type { NotificationService } from "../notifications/service";
import type { ScheduledTask } from "../scheduler";
import type { SettingsStore } from "../settings/store";
import type { FinanceRepository } from "./repository";

/** An account whose last success (or creation) is this old and whose latest run failed is failing. */
export const SYNC_FAILING_AFTER_MS = 48 * 3_600_000;

export interface SyncHealthTaskDeps {
  repo: FinanceRepository;
  notifications: NotificationService;
  /** The panel language names the account in the notification. */
  settings: SettingsStore;
  timezone: string;
  now: () => number;
}

/**
 * Raises `sync_failing` (spec §6.9: "sync failing for more than 2 days"). The key carries the
 * local date of the last success, so one outage raises once and a later outage raises again.
 */
export function syncHealthTask(deps: SyncHealthTaskDeps): ScheduledTask {
  return {
    name: "sync-health",
    run() {
      const now = deps.now();
      const locale = deps.settings.get().locale;
      const connections = new Map(deps.repo.listConnections().map((c) => [c.id, c]));
      for (const account of deps.repo.listAccounts({ statuses: ["active"] })) {
        const connection = connections.get(account.connectionId);
        if (!connection || connection.removedAt !== null) continue;
        const status = effectiveConnectionStatus(
          connection.status,
          connection.validUntil,
          now,
          deps.timezone,
        );
        if (status !== "active" && status !== "expiring") continue;
        if (now - (account.lastSyncedAt ?? account.createdAt) < SYNC_FAILING_AFTER_MS) continue;
        const latest = deps.repo.listSyncRuns(account.id, 1)[0];
        if (latest?.status !== "failed") continue;
        const since =
          account.lastSyncedAt === null ? "never" : toLocalDate(account.lastSyncedAt, deps.timezone);
        deps.notifications.raise({
          event: "sync_failing",
          dedupeKey: notificationKeys.syncFailing(account.id, since),
          params: {
            accountName: accountDisplayName(account, locale),
            bankName: connection.aspspName,
          },
          link: `/accounts/${account.id}`,
        });
      }
    },
  };
}
```

**Additions to the contract** (new names and optional parameters only; every Interface above keeps its name and signature):
- `BackupRunItem` gains `setId: string | null` (the CLI prints the set id of the run and the panel can show which set a run produced; null while running or when the run failed before a copy existed).
- `@bursar/shared`: `backupTriggerSchema` / `BackupTrigger`, `backupTargetSchema` / `BackupTarget`, `backupRunItemSchema`, `backupStatusResponseSchema`, `backupRunResponseSchema` / `BackupRunResponse` (`{ queued: true }`); the contract's types are inferred from these.
- `object-store.ts`: `class ObjectNotFoundError extends Error { key }` (thrown by `get` of a missing key, by both stores), `assertSafeKey(key)`, `assertSafePrefix(prefix)`.
- `s3-store.ts`: `class S3Error extends Error { status: number | null; code: string | null }`, `parseListObjectsV2(xml)` (exported for tests), `S3StoreOptions`.
- `backup.ts`: `DB_FILE = "bursar.db"`, `MANIFEST_FILE = "manifest.json"`, `backupManifestSchema`, `parseSetId(setId): number | null`, `sha256Hex(data)`, `reduceError(error): string` (first line, at most 300 characters), `class BackupUploadError extends Error { setId; sizeBytes; failures }`, `listBackupSets(store): Promise<string[]>` (complete sets, newest first).
- `retention.ts`: `RetentionPolicy`, `DEFAULT_RETENTION`.
- `restore.ts`: `type RestoreErrorCode`, `RestoreOptions`; `RestoreError` takes `(code, message)`.
- `service.ts`: `BackupService.isRunning(): boolean`, `class BackupInProgressError`, constants `BACKUP_FAILURE_THRESHOLD = 2`, `BACKUP_WORK_DIR = ".work"`, `STALE_BACKUP_MESSAGE = "Interrupted by a restart"`, `BACKUP_STATUS_LIMIT = 10`, `BackupServiceDeps`.
- `task.ts`: `NIGHTLY_BACKUP_TASK = "nightly-backup"`, `BackupTaskDeps`.
- `cli.ts`: `USAGE`, `EXIT_CONFIG = 78`, `interface CliContext { env; log; error }`, `backupCommand(args, ctx?)`, `restoreCommand(args, ctx?)`, `runCli(argv, ctx?): Promise<number>` (the in-process entry the tests and Task 16 use; `initCommand` keeps its signature and its own usage line).
- `server.ts`: `StartOverrides` gains `backupS3?: ObjectStore | null` (`null` forces local-only backups; omit it to use `config.backup.s3`). Server tests that configure `BACKUP_S3_*` pass `backupS3: null`, because the nightly task can run a backup right after boot (see "Behaviour decided here") and tests never use the network.

**Behaviour decided here** (the contract leaves it open):
- One set = `<setId>/bursar.db` + `<setId>/manifest.json`, uploaded in that order to the local store first, then S3. Every store is attempted; if any fails the run is `failed` (message `Upload failed for s3 (S3 put failed: HTTP 403 AccessDenied)`), the run row still records the set id and size of the local copy, and no retention runs. Retention runs per store only after every store took the set.
- Retention uses calendar windows in `config.timezone` ending at `now` (today and the 6 days before; this ISO week and the 3 before; this month and the 5 before), the newest set of each window bucket is kept, and the newest set overall is always kept. `pruneStore` deletes every object of every set id not kept, incomplete sets included (the leftovers of a failed upload); objects whose first segment is not a set id are never touched; manifests are deleted first, so a half-pruned set is never offered for restore.
- The nightly task enqueues once per local day: nothing when any `scheduled` run started that local day, whatever its status. The contract's wording ("no successful or running scheduled run") would re-enqueue a failed run on every 60 s tick and raise `backup_failing` within two minutes; spec §9 says a failed backup is "retried next night". Manual and CLI runs do not count. Jobs are enqueued with `maxAttempts: 1` (manual ones too): a failure is recorded, not retried by the queue.
- Because the scheduler ticks at boot, a server started after `backupTime` without a scheduled run that day backs up within a few seconds (catch-up after downtime). `server.test.ts` boots therefore may run a local backup into their temporary data directory; that is harmless, and the S3 case is covered by the `backupS3` override.
- `run()` resolves with the recorded run in every case except a second concurrent call (`BackupInProgressError`); the job handler turns that one into `PermanentJobError`. `POST /api/backups/run` answers 409 while the service runs or a backup job is queued or running.
- `backup_failing` is raised when the count of failed runs since the last success reaches 2, keyed by the local date (`notificationKeys.backupFailing`), params `{ failures }`, link `/settings#backups`: at most one notification per local day while backups keep failing.
- Audit: `backup.run` for every finished run, actor `system` for `scheduled` and `user` for `manual`/`cli`, target the set id (absent when none), details `{ status, trigger, target, sizeBytes? }` (no paths, no error text).
- `failStaleRuns()` also deletes `<backup dir>/.work` (the copy of an interrupted run). A database restored from a set contains that set's own `running` row (the copy is taken while the run is in progress); the restored server's first boot marks it failed with "Interrupted by a restart". Task 23's restore guide mentions it.
- The CLI opens the same database as a running server (WAL allows it) and runs the migrations (a no-op when current). A `backup_failing` raised by `bursar backup run` queues its email for the running server's worker. Two runs in the same second (CLI and server) write the same set id; the copies use distinct temporary files, so the later upload simply replaces identical names.
- `restoreBackup` order: set id format → manifest (missing or invalid → `set_not_found`) → existing `bursar.db` without `force` → `target_not_empty` → database object (missing → `set_not_found`) → size and SHA-256 (`checksum_mismatch`) → written to a hidden temporary file in the target directory, opened with the derived key (`wrong_key`) → `PRAGMA integrity_check` (a result other than `ok`, or the `SQLITE_CORRUPT` that SQLCipher raises for a page failing its HMAC → `integrity_failed`) → with `force`, the old `bursar.db-wal`/`-shm` are removed (a stale WAL would be replayed onto the restored file) → rename into place. A failed restore leaves no file behind.
- Empirical basis, reproduced while writing this task (better-sqlite3-multiple-ciphers 13.0.3, the repo's `cipher='sqlcipher'`, `legacy=4` open sequence, scratch script outside the repository): `VACUUM INTO` produces an encrypted copy (no plaintext header) that opens with the same key and passes `integrity_check`; a wrong key fails with `SQLITE_NOTADB file is not a database`; flipping one byte in the last page or in a middle page makes `integrity_check` throw `SQLITE_CORRUPT database disk image is malformed`; `VACUUM INTO` an existing file fails with `output file already exists`; inside a transaction it fails with `cannot VACUUM from within a transaction`; opening the copy switches it to WAL and closing it removes the `-wal`/`-shm` files. `aws4fetch` 1.0.20 sets `x-amz-content-sha256: UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD` for `s3` unless the header is given, signs `host;x-amz-content-sha256;x-amz-date` and leaves `content-type` unsigned; `AwsClient.sign()` returns a `Request`, so the store sends it with the injected `fetch` and does not use `AwsClient.fetch` (which retries 10 times by default and always uses the global `fetch`). The code of steps 9, 13, 17 and 21 and its tests also ran green in that scratch copy against stand-ins for the Task 6 to 9 modules; Steps 10, 14, 18, 22 and 26 are the verification against the real ones.
- No UI in this task: the Settings page section `#backups` that consumes `GET`/`POST /api/backups` is Task 22, so the Playwright QA step does not apply here.

import { z } from "zod";
import { backupRunStatusSchema } from "./finance";

/** What started a backup run: the nightly task, the panel button, or `bursar backup run`. */
export const backupTriggerSchema = z.enum(["scheduled", "manual", "cli"]);
export type BackupTrigger = z.infer<typeof backupTriggerSchema>;

/** Where backup sets go: the local directory only, or the local directory plus S3. */
export const backupTargetSchema = z.enum(["local", "s3"]);
export type BackupTarget = z.infer<typeof backupTargetSchema>;

export const backupRunItemSchema = z.object({
  id: z.number().int().positive(),
  trigger: backupTriggerSchema,
  status: backupRunStatusSchema,
  target: backupTargetSchema,
  /** `YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ`; null while running or when the run failed before the copy existed. */
  setId: z.string().nullable(),
  startedAt: z.number().int(),
  finishedAt: z.number().int().nullable(),
  sizeBytes: z.number().int().nonnegative().nullable(),
  errorMessage: z.string().nullable(),
});
export type BackupRunItem = z.infer<typeof backupRunItemSchema>;

export const backupStatusResponseSchema = z.object({
  target: backupTargetSchema,
  lastSuccessAt: z.number().int().nullable(),
  consecutiveFailures: z.number().int().nonnegative(),
  runs: z.array(backupRunItemSchema),
});
export type BackupStatusResponse = z.infer<typeof backupStatusResponseSchema>;

/** `POST /api/backups/run` answers 202 with this body. */
export const backupRunResponseSchema = z.object({ queued: z.literal(true) });
export type BackupRunResponse = z.infer<typeof backupRunResponseSchema>;

The mocked `fetch` receives the signed `Request`; the test checks the SigV4 header shape, the path-style URL, the body hash, pagination with an XML-escaped continuation token, and that errors carry only the operation, the status and the S3 `Code` (never the `<Message>`, the host or the secret):

```ts
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { ObjectNotFoundError } from "./object-store";
import { parseListObjectsV2, S3Error, S3Store } from "./s3-store";

const SECRET = "s3-secret-access-key-value-0123456789";

type Responder = (request: Request) => Response | Promise<Response>;

function harness(responder: Responder, prefix = "bursar") {
  const requests: Request[] = [];
  const fetchMock = (async (input: RequestInfo | URL, init?: RequestInit) => {
    const request = input instanceof Request ? input : new Request(input, init);
    requests.push(request.clone());
    return responder(request);
  }) as typeof fetch;
  const store = new S3Store({
    endpoint: new URL("https://s3.example.test"),
    region: "auto",
    bucket: "bursar-backups",
    prefix,
    accessKeyId: "AKIDEXAMPLE",
    secretAccessKey: SECRET,
    fetch: fetchMock,
  });
  return { store, requests };
}

const errorXml = (code: string) =>
  `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><Error><Code>${code}</Code><Message>Detail that must not leak: ${SECRET}</Message><RequestId>REQ123</RequestId></Error>`;

describe("S3Store", () => {
  it("puts an object path-style with a SigV4 Authorization header and the body hash", async () => {
    const { store, requests } = harness(() => new Response(null, { status: 200 }));
    const body = Buffer.from("encrypted database bytes");
    await store.put("20261109T020000Z/bursar.db", body);

    expect(requests).toHaveLength(1);
    const request = requests[0] as Request;
    expect(request.method).toBe("PUT");
    expect(request.url).toBe(
      "https://s3.example.test/bursar-backups/bursar/20261109T020000Z/bursar.db",
    );
    const authorization = request.headers.get("authorization") ?? "";
    expect(authorization).toMatch(
      /^AWS4-HMAC-SHA256 Credential=AKIDEXAMPLE\/\d{8}\/auto\/s3\/aws4_request, SignedHeaders=[a-z0-9;-]+, Signature=[0-9a-f]{64}$/,
    );
    const signed = /SignedHeaders=([a-z0-9;-]+)/.exec(authorization)?.[1]?.split(";") ?? [];
    expect(signed).toEqual(expect.arrayContaining(["host", "x-amz-content-sha256", "x-amz-date"]));
    expect(request.headers.get("x-amz-date")).toMatch(/^\d{8}T\d{6}Z$/);
    expect(request.headers.get("x-amz-content-sha256")).toBe(
      createHash("sha256").update(body).digest("hex"),
    );
    expect(Buffer.from(await request.arrayBuffer())).toEqual(body);
    for (const [, value] of request.headers) expect(value).not.toContain(SECRET);
  });

  it("gets an object and maps 404 to ObjectNotFoundError", async () => {
    const { store, requests } = harness((request) =>
      request.url.endsWith("/present.db")
        ? new Response(Uint8Array.from(Buffer.from("payload")), { status: 200 })
        : new Response(errorXml("NoSuchKey"), { status: 404 }),
    );
    expect((await store.get("20261109T020000Z/present.db")).toString()).toBe("payload");
    await expect(store.get("20261109T020000Z/missing.db")).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(
      ObjectNotFoundError,
    );
    expect(requests.map((r) => r.method)).toEqual(["GET", "GET"]);
  });

  it("lists every page with ListObjectsV2 and returns keys relative to the prefix", async () => {
    const pages = [
      `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><ListBucketResult><Name>bursar-backups</Name>
        <Contents><Key>bursar/20261108T020000Z/bursar.db</Key><Size>4096</Size></Contents>
        <Contents><Key>bursar/20261108T020000Z/manifest.json</Key><Size>210</Size></Contents>
        <IsTruncated>true</IsTruncated><NextContinuationToken>page-2&amp;more</NextContinuationToken>
      </ListBucketResult>`,
      `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><ListBucketResult><Name>bursar-backups</Name>
        <Contents><Key>bursar/20261109T020000Z/bursar.db</Key><Size>8192</Size></Contents>
        <IsTruncated>false</IsTruncated>
      </ListBucketResult>`,
    ];
    let page = 0;
    const { store, requests } = harness(() => new Response(pages[page++], { status: 200 }));

    expect(await store.list("2026")).toEqual([
      { key: "20261108T020000Z/bursar.db", size: 4096 },
      { key: "20261108T020000Z/manifest.json", size: 210 },
      { key: "20261109T020000Z/bursar.db", size: 8192 },
    ]);
    const urls = requests.map((r) => new URL(r.url));
    expect(urls.map((u) => `${u.origin}${u.pathname}`)).toEqual([
      "https://s3.example.test/bursar-backups",
      "https://s3.example.test/bursar-backups",
    ]);
    expect(urls[0]?.searchParams.get("list-type")).toBe("2");
    expect(urls[0]?.searchParams.get("prefix")).toBe("bursar/2026");
    expect(urls[0]?.searchParams.has("continuation-token")).toBe(false);
    expect(urls[1]?.searchParams.get("continuation-token")).toBe("page-2&more");
    for (const request of requests) {
      expect(request.headers.get("authorization")).toMatch(/^AWS4-HMAC-SHA256 /);
    }
  });

  it("works without a key prefix", async () => {
    const { store, requests } = harness(() => new Response(null, { status: 200 }), "");
    await store.put("20261109T020000Z/manifest.json", Buffer.from("{}"));
    expect(requests[0]?.url).toBe(
      "https://s3.example.test/bursar-backups/20261109T020000Z/manifest.json",
    );

  it("deletes with DELETE and treats 404 as already gone", async () => {
    const { store, requests } = harness((request) =>
      request.url.endsWith("/gone.db")
        ? new Response(errorXml("NoSuchKey"), { status: 404 })
        : new Response(null, { status: 204 }),
    );
    await store.delete("20261101T020000Z/bursar.db");
    await store.delete("20261101T020000Z/gone.db");
    expect(requests.map((r) => r.method)).toEqual(["DELETE", "DELETE"]);
  });

  it("reduces an S3 error to the operation, the status and the error code", async () => {
    const { store } = harness(() => new Response(errorXml("AccessDenied"), { status: 403 }));
    const error = await store.put("20261109T020000Z/bursar.db", Buffer.from("x")).catch((e) => e);
    expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(S3Error);
    expect(error.message).toBe("S3 put failed: HTTP 403 AccessDenied");
    expect(error).toMatchObject({ status: 403, code: "AccessDenied" });
    expect(error.message).not.toContain(SECRET);
    expect(error.message).not.toContain("s3.example.test");
  });

  it("keeps the status alone when the error body is not an S3 error document", async () => {
    const { store } = harness(() => new Response("<html>gateway</html>", { status: 502 }));
    await expect(store.list("")).rejects.toThrow(/^S3 list failed: HTTP 502$/);
  });

  it("reduces a network failure to its error code", async () => {
    const { store } = harness(() => {
      throw new TypeError("fetch failed", { cause: { code: "ECONNREFUSED" } });
    });
    await expect(store.get("20261109T020000Z/bursar.db")).rejects.toThrow(
      /^S3 get failed: network error \(ECONNREFUSED\)$/,
    );
  });

  it("rejects unsafe keys before sending anything", async () => {
    const { store, requests } = harness(() => new Response(null, { status: 200 }));
    await expect(store.put("../outside.db", Buffer.from("x"))).rejects.toThrow(
      "Invalid object key",

    await expect(store.get("/absolute")).rejects.toThrow("Invalid object key");
    await expect(store.list("a//")).rejects.toThrow("Invalid object key");
    expect(requests).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});

describe("parseListObjectsV2", () => {
  it("decodes XML entities in keys and tokens and ignores incomplete entries", () => {
    expect(
      parseListObjectsV2(
        "<ListBucketResult><Contents><Key>a&amp;b&#47;c&#x2F;d</Key><Size>7</Size></Contents>" +

      ),
    ).toEqual({
      contents: [{ key: "a&b/c/d", size: 7 }],
      isTruncated: false,
      nextContinuationToken: null,
    });
  });
});

Create `apps/server/src/backup/object-store.ts`:

```ts
import { randomBytes } from "node:crypto";
import type { Dirent } from "node:fs";
import { mkdir, open, readdir, readFile, rename, rm, rmdir, stat } from "node:fs/promises";
import path from "node:path";

/** A flat key/value blob store. Keys are relative POSIX paths such as `<setId>/bursar.db`. */
export interface ObjectStore {
  readonly kind: "local" | "s3";
  put(key: string, body: Buffer): Promise<void>;
  get(key: string): Promise<Buffer>;
  /** Every object whose key starts with `prefix` (`""` lists everything), sorted by key. */
  list(prefix: string): Promise<{ key: string; size: number }[]>;
  /** Deleting a missing key is not an error. */
  delete(key: string): Promise<void>;
}

/** `get` of a key that does not exist. */
export class ObjectNotFoundError extends Error {
  constructor(readonly key: string) {
    super(`Object not found: ${key}`);
    this.name = "ObjectNotFoundError";
  }
}

// A segment never starts with a dot: this rules out ".", "..", hidden files and the temporary
// files and work directory the local store keeps next to the sets.
const SEGMENT = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$/;

/** Throws unless every `/`-separated segment of `key` is a plain name (no traversal, no root). */
export function assertSafeKey(key: string): void {
  if (key.length === 0 || key.length > 512 || !key.split("/").every((s) => SEGMENT.test(s))) {
    throw new Error("Invalid object key");
  }
}

/** `""`, or a safe key optionally ending with `/`. */
export function assertSafePrefix(prefix: string): void {
  if (prefix === "") return;
  assertSafeKey(prefix.endsWith("/") ? prefix.slice(0, -1) : prefix);
}

/**
 * Stores objects as files under `rootDir`: directories 0700, files 0600, every write goes to a
 * hidden temporary file that is synced and then renamed over the target, so a reader never sees
 * half a file. Entries whose name starts with a dot are never listed.
 */
export class LocalDirStore implements ObjectStore {
  readonly kind = "local" as const;
  private readonly root: string;

  constructor(rootDir: string) {
    this.root = path.resolve(rootDir);
  }

  async put(key: string, body: Buffer): Promise<void> {
    const file = this.resolve(key);
    const dir = path.dirname(file);
    await mkdir(dir, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
    const temp = path.join(dir, `.${path.basename(file)}.${randomBytes(6).toString("hex")}.tmp`);
    try {
      const handle = await open(temp, "wx", 0o600);
      try {
        await handle.writeFile(body);
        await handle.sync();
      } finally {
        await handle.close();
      }
      await rename(temp, file);
    } catch (error) {
      await rm(temp, { force: true });
      throw error;
    }
  }

  async get(key: string): Promise<Buffer> {
    try {
      return await readFile(this.resolve(key));
    } catch (error) {
      if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT") throw new ObjectNotFoundError(key);
      throw error;
    }
  }

  async list(prefix: string): Promise<{ key: string; size: number }[]> {
    assertSafePrefix(prefix);
    const found: { key: string; size: number }[] = [];
    const walk = async (dir: string, keyPrefix: string): Promise<void> => {
      let entries: Dirent[];
      try {
        entries = await readdir(dir, { withFileTypes: true });
      } catch (error) {
        if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT") return;
        throw error;
      }
      for (const entry of entries) {
        if (entry.name.startsWith(".")) continue;
        const key = `${keyPrefix}${entry.name}`;
        const full = path.join(dir, entry.name);
        if (entry.isDirectory()) await walk(full, `${key}/`);
        else if (entry.isFile() && key.startsWith(prefix)) {
          found.push({ key, size: (await stat(full)).size });
        }
      }
    };
    await walk(this.root, "");
    return found.sort((a, b) => (a.key < b.key ? -1 : a.key > b.key ? 1 : 0));
  }

  async delete(key: string): Promise<void> {
    const file = this.resolve(key);
    await rm(file, { force: true });
    const dir = path.dirname(file);
    // Drop the set directory once it is empty; rmdir refuses a non-empty directory.
    if (dir !== this.root) await rmdir(dir).catch(() => {});
  }

  private resolve(key: string): string {
    assertSafeKey(key);
    const file = path.join(this.root, ...key.split("/"));
    if (!file.startsWith(`${this.root}${path.sep}`)) throw new Error("Invalid object key");
    return file;
  }
}
```

Create `apps/server/src/backup/s3-store.ts`:

```ts
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
import { AwsClient } from "aws4fetch";
import {
  assertSafeKey,
  assertSafePrefix,
  ObjectNotFoundError,
  type ObjectStore,
} from "./object-store";

export interface S3StoreOptions {
  endpoint: URL;
  region: string;
  bucket: string;
  /** Key prefix inside the bucket, without a leading or trailing slash (may be empty). */
  prefix: string;
  accessKeyId: string;
  secretAccessKey: string;
  /** Injected in tests; defaults to the global `fetch`. */
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
}

/**
 * A failed S3 call. The message carries only the operation, the HTTP status and the S3 error
 * `Code` (or a network error code): never the response body, the URL or a credential.
 */
export class S3Error extends Error {
  constructor(
    message: string,
    readonly status: number | null,
    readonly code: string | null,
  ) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "S3Error";
  }
}

/** The parts of a ListObjectsV2 response the store needs. Exported for tests. */
export function parseListObjectsV2(xml: string): {
  contents: { key: string; size: number }[];
  isTruncated: boolean;
  nextContinuationToken: string | null;
} {
  const contents: { key: string; size: number }[] = [];
  for (const match of xml.matchAll(/<Contents>([\s\S]*?)<\/Contents>/g)) {
    const body = match[1] ?? "";
    const key = /<Key>([\s\S]*?)<\/Key>/.exec(body)?.[1];
    const size = /<Size>(\d+)<\/Size>/.exec(body)?.[1];
    if (key !== undefined && size !== undefined) {
      contents.push({ key: decodeXml(key), size: Number(size) });
    }
  }
  const token = /<NextContinuationToken>([\s\S]*?)<\/NextContinuationToken>/.exec(xml)?.[1];
  return {
    contents,
    isTruncated: /<IsTruncated>\s*true\s*<\/IsTruncated>/i.test(xml),
    nextContinuationToken: token === undefined ? null : decodeXml(token),
  };
}

function decodeXml(text: string): string {
  return text.replace(
    /&(lt|gt|quot|apos|amp|#(\d+)|#x([0-9a-fA-F]+));/g,
    (_match, name: string, dec?: string, hex?: string) => {
      if (dec) return String.fromCodePoint(Number(dec));
      if (hex) return String.fromCodePoint(Number.parseInt(hex, 16));
      return { lt: "<", gt: ">", quot: '"', apos: "'", amp: "&" }[name] ?? "";
    },
  );
}

async function s3ErrorCode(response: Response): Promise<string | null> {
  const text = await response.text().catch(() => "");
  return /<Code>([A-Za-z0-9.]{1,64})<\/Code>/.exec(text)?.[1] ?? null;
}

function networkReason(error: unknown): string {
  const code =
    error instanceof Error ? (error.cause as { code?: unknown } | undefined)?.code : null;
  return typeof code === "string" && /^[A-Z0-9_]{2,40}$/.test(code)
    ? `network error (${code})`
    : "network error";
}

const MAX_LIST_PAGES = 1_000;

/**
 * An S3-compatible bucket (AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, MinIO, …) addressed path-style:
 * `<endpoint>/<bucket>/<prefix>/<key>`. Requests are signed with SigV4 by `aws4fetch`; uploads
 * carry their SHA-256 in `x-amz-content-sha256`, so the service rejects a corrupted body. No
 * retries here: a failed nightly run is retried the next night.
 */
export class S3Store implements ObjectStore {
  readonly kind = "s3" as const;
  private readonly client: AwsClient;
  private readonly fetchImpl: typeof fetch;
  private readonly bucketUrl: string;
  private readonly prefix: string;

  constructor(options: S3StoreOptions) {
    this.client = new AwsClient({
      accessKeyId: options.accessKeyId,
      secretAccessKey: options.secretAccessKey,
      service: "s3",
      region: options.region,
      retries: 0,
    });
    this.fetchImpl = options.fetch ?? fetch;
    this.bucketUrl = `${options.endpoint.origin}/${encodeURIComponent(options.bucket)}`;
    this.prefix = options.prefix.replace(/^\/+|\/+$/g, "");
  }

  async put(key: string, body: Buffer): Promise<void> {
    const url = this.objectUrl(key);
    const response = await this.send("put", url, {
      method: "PUT",
      headers: {
        "content-type": "application/octet-stream",
        "x-amz-content-sha256": createHash("sha256").update(body).digest("hex"),
      },
      body: Uint8Array.from(body),
    });
    await response.arrayBuffer();
  }

  async get(key: string): Promise<Buffer> {
    const response = await this.send("get", this.objectUrl(key), { method: "GET" }, true);
    if (response.status === 404) {
      await response.arrayBuffer();
      throw new ObjectNotFoundError(key);
    }
    return Buffer.from(await response.arrayBuffer());
  }

  async list(prefix: string): Promise<{ key: string; size: number }[]> {
    assertSafePrefix(prefix);
    const strip = this.prefix ? `${this.prefix}/` : "";
    const items: { key: string; size: number }[] = [];
    let token: string | null = null;
    for (let page = 0; page < MAX_LIST_PAGES; page++) {
      const query = new URLSearchParams({ "list-type": "2", prefix: `${strip}${prefix}` });
      if (token) query.set("continuation-token", token);
      const response = await this.send("list", `${this.bucketUrl}?${query}`, { method: "GET" });
      const parsed = parseListObjectsV2(await response.text());
      for (const item of parsed.contents) {
        if (item.key.startsWith(strip))
          items.push({ key: item.key.slice(strip.length), size: item.size });
      }
      if (!parsed.isTruncated) {
        return items.sort((a, b) => (a.key < b.key ? -1 : a.key > b.key ? 1 : 0));
      }
      if (!parsed.nextContinuationToken) {
        throw new S3Error(
          "S3 list failed: truncated listing without a continuation token",
          null,
          null,
        );
      }
      token = parsed.nextContinuationToken;
    }
    throw new S3Error("S3 list failed: too many pages", null, null);
  }

  async delete(key: string): Promise<void> {
    const response = await this.send("delete", this.objectUrl(key), { method: "DELETE" }, true);
    await response.arrayBuffer();
  }

  private objectUrl(key: string): string {
    assertSafeKey(key);
    const full = this.prefix ? `${this.prefix}/${key}` : key;
    return `${this.bucketUrl}/${full.split("/").map(encodeURIComponent).join("/")}`;
  }

  /** Signs and sends one request; any status other than 2xx (and 404 when allowed) throws. */
  private async send(
    operation: "put" | "get" | "list" | "delete",
    url: string,
    init: RequestInit,
    allowNotFound = false,
  ): Promise<Response> {
    let response: Response;
    try {
      response = await this.fetchImpl(await this.client.sign(url, init));
    } catch (error) {
      throw new S3Error(`S3 ${operation} failed: ${networkReason(error)}`, null, null);
    }
    if (response.ok || (allowNotFound && response.status === 404)) return response;
    const code = await s3ErrorCode(response);
    throw new S3Error(
      `S3 ${operation} failed: HTTP ${response.status}${code ? ` ${code}` : ""}`,
      response.status,
      code,
    );
  }
}

Create `apps/server/src/test/backup.ts`. `createTestDatabase()` keys its database with a fixed passphrase, but a backup is verified and restored with the key derived from the master key, so these tests need a database keyed the way `startBursar` keys the real one. The seed uses raw SQL with the Task 6 column names (if Task 6 named a column differently, adjust the `INSERT` statements and nothing else):

```ts
import { mkdtempSync, rmSync } from "node:fs";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { deriveKey } from "../crypto";
import { openDatabase, runMigrations, type Sqlite } from "../db";
import { MIGRATIONS_DIR, type TestDatabase } from "./db";

/** Fixed test master key; the database passphrase is derived from it as in production. */
export const TEST_MASTER_KEY = Buffer.alloc(32, 7);

export function databasePassphrase(masterKey: Buffer): string {
  return deriveKey(masterKey, "database").toString("hex");
}

export interface KeyedTestDatabase extends TestDatabase {
  masterKey: Buffer;
  passphrase: string;
}

/**
 * Like `createTestDatabase()`, but keyed the way `startBursar` keys the real database (with
 * `deriveKey(masterKey, "database")`), so backups of it can be verified and restored with the
 * master key. The file is `<dir>/bursar.db`.
 */
export function createKeyedTestDatabase(masterKey: Buffer = TEST_MASTER_KEY): KeyedTestDatabase {
  const dir = mkdtempSync(path.join(tmpdir(), "bursar-backup-test-"));
  const file = path.join(dir, "bursar.db");
  const passphrase = databasePassphrase(masterKey);
  const opened = openDatabase(file, passphrase);
  runMigrations(opened.db, MIGRATIONS_DIR);
  return {
    ...opened,
    dir,
    file,
    masterKey,
    passphrase,
    dispose: () => {
      opened.close();
      rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
    },
  };
}

/**
 * Fictional rows in several M1 tables (raw SQL with the column names of the Task 6 schema):
 * 1 setting, 1 connection, 1 account, 3 transactions, 1 audit entry.
 */
export function seedBackupRows(sqlite: Sqlite, now: number): void {
  sqlite
    .prepare("INSERT INTO settings (key, value, updated_at) VALUES ('locale', '\"en\"', ?)")
    .run(now);
  const connection = sqlite
    .prepare(
      `INSERT INTO bank_connections (aspsp_name, aspsp_country, provider_session_id, valid_until, created_at, updated_at)
       VALUES ('Banca Esempio', 'IT', 'session-fixture-0001', ?, ?, ?)`,
    )
    .run(now + 90 * 86_400_000, now, now);
  const account = sqlite
    .prepare(
      `INSERT INTO accounts (connection_id, identification_hash, currency, product, created_at, updated_at)
       VALUES (?, 'hash-fixture-0001', 'EUR', 'Conto Esempio', ?, ?)`,
    )
    .run(connection.lastInsertRowid, now, now);
  const insertTransaction = sqlite.prepare(
    `INSERT INTO transactions (account_id, fingerprint, status, booking_date, sort_date, amount_minor, currency,
       counterparty, search_text, raw_json, first_seen_at, last_seen_at)
     VALUES (?, ?, 'booked', ?, ?, ?, 'EUR', ?, ?, '{}', ?, ?)`,
  );
  const rows = [
    ["fp-1", "2026-11-02", 250_000, "Example Employer"],
    ["fp-2", "2026-11-03", -4_590, "Grocery Store"],
    ["fp-3", "2026-11-05", -12_000, "Utility Company"],
  ] as const;
  for (const [fingerprint, date, amount, counterparty] of rows) {
    insertTransaction.run(
      account.lastInsertRowid,
      fingerprint,
      date,
      date,
      amount,
      counterparty,
      counterparty.toLowerCase(),
      now,
      now,
    );
  }
  sqlite
    .prepare(
      "INSERT INTO audit_log (actor, action, target, details, at) VALUES ('user', 'settings.update', NULL, '{\"keys\":\"locale\"}', ?)",
    )
    .run(now);
}

/** Row count of every table, read the same way `restoreBackup` reports them. */
export function tableCounts(sqlite: Sqlite): Record<string, number> {
  const names = sqlite
    .prepare(
      "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' AND name NOT LIKE 'sqlite_%' ORDER BY name",
    )
    .all() as { name: string }[];
  return Object.fromEntries(
    names.map(({ name }) => [
      name,
      (sqlite.prepare(`SELECT count(*) AS n FROM "${name}"`).get() as { n: number }).n,
    ]),
  );
}

Create `apps/server/src/test/fake-s3.ts` (an in-memory bucket behind an injected `fetch`, used by the restore round trip and the service tests; no network):

```ts
/** Test double for an S3-compatible bucket, reached through an injected `fetch`. No network. */
export interface FakeS3 {
  fetch: typeof fetch;
  /** Objects by full key inside the bucket (store prefix included), e.g. `bursar/<setId>/bursar.db`. */
  objects: Map<string, Buffer>;
  requests: Request[];
  /** Every following request answers `status` with an S3 error document carrying `code`. */
  failWith(status: number, code: string): void;
  recover(): void;
}

const escapeXml = (text: string) =>
  text.replaceAll("&", "&amp;").replaceAll("<", "&lt;").replaceAll(">", "&gt;");

const xml = (status: number, body: string) =>
  new Response(`<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>\n${body}`, {
    status,
    headers: { "content-type": "application/xml" },
  });

/**
 * Path-style bucket `bucket` with PUT, GET, DELETE and ListObjectsV2 (`pageSize` keys per page,
 * continuation token = index of the next key). It does not check signatures: `s3-store.test.ts`
 * checks the request shape.
 */
export function createFakeS3(options: { bucket?: string; pageSize?: number } = {}): FakeS3 {
  const bucket = options.bucket ?? "bursar-backups";
  const pageSize = options.pageSize ?? 1_000;
  const objects = new Map<string, Buffer>();
  const requests: Request[] = [];
  let failure: { status: number; code: string } | null = null;

  const handle = async (request: Request): Promise<Response> => {
    if (failure) {
      return xml(
        failure.status,
        `<Error><Code>${failure.code}</Code><Message>Refused by the fake</Message></Error>`,
      );
    }
    const url = new URL(request.url);
    const [, bucketName, ...rest] = url.pathname.split("/");
    if (bucketName !== bucket) return xml(404, "<Error><Code>NoSuchBucket</Code></Error>");
    const key = rest.map(decodeURIComponent).join("/");
    if (request.method === "GET" && url.searchParams.get("list-type") === "2") {
      const prefix = url.searchParams.get("prefix") ?? "";
      const keys = [...objects.keys()].filter((k) => k.startsWith(prefix)).sort();
      const start = Number(url.searchParams.get("continuation-token") ?? "0");
      const page = keys.slice(start, start + pageSize);
      const truncated = start + pageSize < keys.length;
      const contents = page
        .map(
          (k) =>
            `<Contents><Key>${escapeXml(k)}</Key><Size>${objects.get(k)?.length ?? 0}</Size></Contents>`,
        )
        .join("");
      return xml(
        200,
        `<ListBucketResult><Name>${bucket}</Name><KeyCount>${page.length}</KeyCount>${contents}` +
          `<IsTruncated>${truncated}</IsTruncated>` +
          (truncated ? `<NextContinuationToken>${start + pageSize}</NextContinuationToken>` : "") +
          "</ListBucketResult>",
      );
    }
    if (request.method === "PUT") {
      objects.set(key, Buffer.from(await request.arrayBuffer()));
      return new Response(null, { status: 200 });
    }
    if (request.method === "GET") {
      const object = objects.get(key);
      return object
        ? new Response(Uint8Array.from(object), { status: 200 })
        : xml(404, "<Error><Code>NoSuchKey</Code></Error>");
    }
    if (request.method === "DELETE") {
      objects.delete(key);
      return new Response(null, { status: 204 });
    }
    return xml(405, "<Error><Code>MethodNotAllowed</Code></Error>");
  };

  const fakeFetch = (async (input: RequestInfo | URL, init?: RequestInit) => {
    const request = input instanceof Request ? input : new Request(input, init);
    requests.push(request.clone());
    return handle(request);
  }) as typeof fetch;

  return {
    fetch: fakeFetch,
    objects,
    requests,
    failWith: (status, code) => {
      failure = { status, code };
    },
    recover: () => {
      failure = null;
    },
  };
}

```ts
import { readdirSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { openDatabase } from "../db";
import { createKeyedTestDatabase, type KeyedTestDatabase, seedBackupRows } from "../test/backup";
import {
  type BackupManifest,
  BackupUploadError,
  createBackup,
  DB_FILE,
  formatSetId,
  listBackupSets,
  MANIFEST_FILE,
  parseSetId,
  reduceError,
  sha256Hex,
} from "./backup";
import { LocalDirStore, type ObjectStore } from "./object-store";

const NOW = Date.UTC(2026, 10, 9, 2, 0, 0, 345);

/** Records the order of `put` calls; can be told to refuse every write. */
class RecordingStore implements ObjectStore {
  readonly puts: string[] = [];
  readonly objects = new Map<string, Buffer>();
  constructor(
    readonly kind: "local" | "s3",
    private readonly failure: Error | null = null,
  ) {}
  async put(key: string, body: Buffer): Promise<void> {
    if (this.failure) throw this.failure;
    this.puts.push(key);
    this.objects.set(key, body);
  }
  async get(key: string): Promise<Buffer> {
    const body = this.objects.get(key);
    if (!body) throw new Error("missing");
    return body;
  }
  async list(prefix: string): Promise<{ key: string; size: number }[]> {
    return [...this.objects]
      .filter(([key]) => key.startsWith(prefix))
      .map(([key, body]) => ({ key, size: body.length }));
  }
  async delete(key: string): Promise<void> {
    this.objects.delete(key);
  }
}

describe("set ids", () => {
  it("formats the UTC instant to the second", () => {
    expect(formatSetId(Date.UTC(2026, 10, 9, 3, 4, 5, 678))).toBe("20261109T030405Z");
  });

  it("parses canonical ids only", () => {
    expect(parseSetId("20261109T030405Z")).toBe(Date.UTC(2026, 10, 9, 3, 4, 5));
    for (const bad of ["20261340T000000Z", "20261109T030405", "../20261109T030405Z", "x", ""]) {
      expect(parseSetId(bad)).toBeNull();
    }
  });
});

describe("reduceError", () => {
  it("keeps the first line and caps the length", () => {
    expect(reduceError(new Error("first line\nsecond line"))).toBe("first line");
    expect(reduceError("x".repeat(400))).toHaveLength(300);
    expect(reduceError(new Error(""))).toBe("Unknown error");
  });
});

describe("createBackup", () => {
  let t: KeyedTestDatabase;
  let workDir: string;
  let local: LocalDirStore;

  beforeEach(() => {
    t = createKeyedTestDatabase();
    seedBackupRows(t.sqlite, NOW);
    workDir = path.join(t.dir, "backups", ".work");
    local = new LocalDirStore(path.join(t.dir, "backups"));
  });
  afterEach(() => t.dispose());

  it("uploads an encrypted, verified copy and a manifest that describes it", async () => {
    const result = await createBackup({
      sqlite: t.sqlite,
      dbPassphrase: t.passphrase,
      workDir,
      stores: [local],
      now: () => NOW,
    });

    expect(result.setId).toBe("20261109T020000Z");
    const stored = await local.get(`20261109T020000Z/${DB_FILE}`);
    expect(stored.subarray(0, 15).toString("latin1")).not.toBe("SQLite format 3");
    const migrations = (
      t.sqlite.prepare("SELECT count(*) AS n FROM __drizzle_migrations").get() as { n: number }
    ).n;
    const expected: BackupManifest = {
      version: 1,
      setId: "20261109T020000Z",
      createdAt: "2026-11-09T02:00:00.345Z",
      schema: { migrations },
      files: [{ name: DB_FILE, size: stored.length, sha256: sha256Hex(stored) }],
    };
    expect(result.manifest).toEqual(expected);
    expect(result.sizeBytes).toBe(stored.length);
    const manifest = JSON.parse((await local.get(`20261109T020000Z/${MANIFEST_FILE}`)).toString());
    expect(manifest).toEqual(expected);
    expect(readdirSync(workDir)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("produces a copy that opens with the database key and holds the rows", async () => {
    await createBackup({
      sqlite: t.sqlite,
      dbPassphrase: t.passphrase,
      workDir,
      stores: [local],
      now: () => NOW,
    });
    const copy = path.join(t.dir, "restored-copy.db");
    writeFileSync(copy, await local.get(`20261109T020000Z/${DB_FILE}`));
    const opened = openDatabase(copy, t.passphrase);
    try {
      const row = opened.sqlite.prepare("SELECT count(*) AS n FROM transactions").get();
      expect(row).toEqual({ n: 3 });
    } finally {
      opened.close();
    }
    expect(() => openDatabase(copy, "another-passphrase-0123456789")).toThrow(
      /file is not a database/,
    );
  });

  it("uploads the database before the manifest, to every store in order", async () => {
    const first = new RecordingStore("local");
    const second = new RecordingStore("s3");
    await createBackup({
      sqlite: t.sqlite,
      dbPassphrase: t.passphrase,
      workDir,
      stores: [first, second],
      now: () => NOW,
    });
    const keys = ["20261109T020000Z/bursar.db", "20261109T020000Z/manifest.json"];
    expect(first.puts).toEqual(keys);
    expect(second.puts).toEqual(keys);
  });

  it("keeps the local copy when a later store fails, then reports the failed store", async () => {
    const failing = new RecordingStore("s3", new Error("S3 put failed: HTTP 403 AccessDenied"));
    const error = await createBackup({
      sqlite: t.sqlite,
      dbPassphrase: t.passphrase,
      workDir,
      stores: [local, failing],
      now: () => NOW,
    }).catch((e) => e);
    expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(BackupUploadError);
    expect(error.message).toBe("Upload failed for s3 (S3 put failed: HTTP 403 AccessDenied)");
    expect(error).toMatchObject({ setId: "20261109T020000Z" });
    expect(error.sizeBytes).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(await listBackupSets(local)).toEqual(["20261109T020000Z"]);
    expect(readdirSync(workDir)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("refuses to run inside a transaction", async () => {
    t.sqlite.exec("BEGIN");
    try {
      await expect(
        createBackup({
          sqlite: t.sqlite,
          dbPassphrase: t.passphrase,
          workDir,
          stores: [local],
          now: () => NOW,
        }),
      ).rejects.toThrow("Cannot back up from inside a transaction");
    } finally {
      t.sqlite.exec("ROLLBACK");
    }
  });

  it("fails without uploading when the copy does not open with the given passphrase", async () => {
    const store = new RecordingStore("local");
    await expect(
      createBackup({
        sqlite: t.sqlite,
        dbPassphrase: "not-the-database-passphrase-000",
        workDir,
        stores: [store],
        now: () => NOW,
      }),
    ).rejects.toThrow(/Cannot open encrypted database/);
    expect(store.puts).toEqual([]);
    expect(readdirSync(workDir)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("captures a row written just before the backup", async () => {
    t.sqlite
      .prepare("INSERT INTO settings (key, value, updated_at) VALUES ('country', '\"IT\"', ?)")
      .run(NOW);
    await createBackup({
      sqlite: t.sqlite,
      dbPassphrase: t.passphrase,
      workDir,
      stores: [local],
      now: () => NOW,
    });
    const copy = path.join(t.dir, "check.db");
    writeFileSync(copy, await local.get(`20261109T020000Z/${DB_FILE}`));
    const opened = openDatabase(copy, t.passphrase);
    try {
      expect(
        opened.sqlite.prepare("SELECT value FROM settings WHERE key = 'country'").get(),
      ).toEqual({ value: '"IT"' });
    } finally {
      opened.close();
    }
  });
});

    await put("notes/manifest.json");

  });
});

Create `apps/server/src/backup/retention.test.ts`. The fixture is 40 nightly sets at 03:00 in Rome from 2026-09-20 to 2026-10-29 across the end of summer time (Sunday 2026-10-25), plus two sets just after local midnight whose UTC date is the day before: a UTC-day implementation would keep them, the local-day one must not. Expected with `now` = 2026-10-29 03:00 local: daily Oct 23–29, weekly the newest of the ISO weeks starting Oct 26, 19, 12 and 5 (Oct 29, 25, 18, 11), monthly October and September (Oct 29, Sep 30): 10 sets.

```ts
import { mkdtempSync, rmSync } from "node:fs";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { addDays, toLocalDate } from "@bursar/shared";
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { listBackupSets, parseSetId } from "./backup";
import { LocalDirStore } from "./object-store";
import { pruneStore, retainedSetIds } from "./retention";

const ROME = "Europe/Rome";

/**
 * One set per day at 03:00 in Rome from 2026-09-20 to 2026-10-29 (40 sets). Summer time ends on
 * Sunday 2026-10-25, so 03:00 local is 01:00Z before that day and 02:00Z from that day on.
 */
function nightlySets(): string[] {
  const ids: string[] = [];
  for (let day = "2026-09-20"; day <= "2026-10-29"; day = addDays(day, 1)) {
    const hour = day >= "2026-10-25" ? "02" : "01";
    ids.push(`${day.replaceAll("-", "")}T${hour}0000Z`);
  }
  return ids;
}

describe("retainedSetIds", () => {
  it("keeps 7 daily, 4 weekly and 6 monthly sets across two months and a DST change", () => {
    const ids = nightlySets();
    expect(ids).toHaveLength(40);
    // Sanity check of the fixture: every set falls on its own local day.
    expect(new Set(ids.map((id) => toLocalDate(parseSetId(id) ?? 0, ROME))).size).toBe(40);
    // Two extra sets just after local midnight: on the UTC calendar they belong to the day before.
    const extra = ["20261024T223000Z", "20261027T233000Z"]; // 00:30 on Oct 25 (CEST) and Oct 28 (CET)
    const now = Date.parse("2026-10-29T02:00:00Z");

    const kept = retainedSetIds([...ids, ...extra], now, ROME);

    expect([...kept].sort()).toEqual([
      "20260930T010000Z", // monthly: September
      "20261011T010000Z", // weekly: ISO week of Oct 5
      "20261018T010000Z", // weekly: ISO week of Oct 12
      "20261023T010000Z", // daily ×7 (Oct 23–29); Oct 25 is also the newest of the week of Oct 19
      "20261024T010000Z",
      "20261025T020000Z",
      "20261026T020000Z",
      "20261027T020000Z",
      "20261028T020000Z",
      "20261029T020000Z", // newest, this week, this month
    ]);
  });

  it("always keeps the newest set, however old", () => {
    expect(
      retainedSetIds(
        ["20240101T020000Z", "20230101T020000Z"],
        Date.parse("2026-11-09T02:00:00Z"),
        ROME,
      ),
    ).toEqual(new Set(["20240101T020000Z"]));
    expect(
      retainedSetIds(
        ["20261108T020000Z", "20261109T020000Z"],
        Date.parse("2026-11-09T03:00:00Z"),
        ROME,
        { daily: 0, weekly: 0, monthly: 0 },
      ),
    ).toEqual(new Set(["20261109T020000Z"]));
  });

  it("buckets by the local day of the configured time zone", () => {
    const ids = ["20261024T213000Z", "20261024T223000Z"]; // 23:30 on Oct 24, 00:30 on Oct 25 in Rome
    const now = Date.parse("2026-10-25T12:00:00Z");
    const policy = { daily: 2, weekly: 0, monthly: 0 };
    expect(retainedSetIds(ids, now, ROME, policy)).toEqual(new Set(ids));
    expect(retainedSetIds(ids, now, "UTC", policy)).toEqual(new Set(["20261024T223000Z"]));
  });

  it("ignores ids that are not set ids and returns nothing for no sets", () => {
    expect(retainedSetIds(["notes", "2026-11-09"], Date.now(), ROME)).toEqual(new Set());
    expect(retainedSetIds([], Date.now(), ROME)).toEqual(new Set());
  });
});

describe("pruneStore", () => {
  let dir: string;
  let store: LocalDirStore;
  beforeEach(() => {
    dir = mkdtempSync(path.join(tmpdir(), "bursar-prune-"));
    store = new LocalDirStore(dir);
  });
  afterEach(() => rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }));

  it("deletes every set outside `keep`, incomplete ones included, and nothing else", async () => {
    const put = (key: string) => store.put(key, Buffer.from("x"));
    for (const id of ["20261101T020000Z", "20261108T020000Z", "20261109T020000Z"]) {

    await put("notes/readme.txt");

This is the automated restore test of spec §6.12 and §12: a database with rows in several M1 tables is backed up to a temporary target and restored into a new temporary directory, then compared table by table and on a sampled row; the same round trip runs through `S3Store` and the fake bucket (one key per list page, so pagination is exercised); every `RestoreError` code is produced from a real set:

```ts
import {
  existsSync,
  mkdirSync,
  mkdtempSync,
  readdirSync,
  readFileSync,
  rmSync,
  statSync,
  writeFileSync,
} from "node:fs";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { openDatabase } from "../db";
import {
  createKeyedTestDatabase,
  databasePassphrase,
  type KeyedTestDatabase,
  seedBackupRows,
  tableCounts,
} from "../test/backup";
import { createFakeS3 } from "../test/fake-s3";
import { createBackup, DB_FILE, MANIFEST_FILE, sha256Hex } from "./backup";
import { LocalDirStore, type ObjectStore } from "./object-store";
import { RestoreError, restoreBackup } from "./restore";
import { S3Store } from "./s3-store";

const NOW = Date.UTC(2026, 10, 9, 2, 0, 0);
const SET_ID = "20261109T020000Z";

describe("backup and restore round trip", () => {
  let t: KeyedTestDatabase;
  let scratch: string;
  let storeDir: string;
  let store: LocalDirStore;
  let target: string;

  beforeEach(async () => {
    t = createKeyedTestDatabase();
    seedBackupRows(t.sqlite, NOW);
    scratch = mkdtempSync(path.join(tmpdir(), "bursar-restore-"));
    storeDir = path.join(scratch, "store");
    store = new LocalDirStore(storeDir);
    target = path.join(scratch, "target");
    await backupTo(store);
  });
  afterEach(() => {
    t.dispose();
    rmSync(scratch, { recursive: true, force: true });
  });

  const backupTo = (destination: ObjectStore) =>
    createBackup({
      sqlite: t.sqlite,
      dbPassphrase: t.passphrase,
      workDir: path.join(scratch, "work"),
      stores: [destination],
      now: () => NOW,
    });

  const restore = (overrides: Partial<Parameters<typeof restoreBackup>[0]> = {}) =>
    restoreBackup({
      source: store,
      setId: SET_ID,
      targetDir: target,
      masterKey: t.masterKey,
      ...overrides,
    });

  const codeOf = (promise: Promise<unknown>) =>
    promise.then(
      () => "resolved",
      (error: unknown) => (error instanceof RestoreError ? error.code : String(error)),
    );

  /** The target holds no database and no temporary file. */
  const expectTargetUntouched = () => {
    expect(existsSync(path.join(target, DB_FILE))).toBe(false);
    if (existsSync(target)) {
      expect(readdirSync(target).filter((name) => name.includes("restore"))).toEqual([]);
    }
  };

  it("restores every row into a private file that opens with the master key", async () => {
    const result = await restore();

    expect(result.setId).toBe(SET_ID);
    const expectedCounts = tableCounts(t.sqlite);
    expect(result.tables).toEqual(expectedCounts);
    expect(result.tables).toMatchObject({
      settings: 1,
      bank_connections: 1,
      accounts: 1,
      transactions: 3,
      audit_log: 1,
    });
    const file = path.join(target, DB_FILE);
    expect(statSync(file).mode & 0o777).toBe(0o600);
    expect(readdirSync(target)).toEqual([DB_FILE]);

    const restored = openDatabase(file, databasePassphrase(t.masterKey));
    try {
      expect(tableCounts(restored.sqlite)).toEqual(expectedCounts);
      const sample = "SELECT * FROM transactions WHERE fingerprint = 'fp-2'";
      expect(restored.sqlite.prepare(sample).get()).toEqual(t.sqlite.prepare(sample).get());
    } finally {
      restored.close();
    }
  });

  it("round-trips through an S3-compatible target too", async () => {
    const fake = createFakeS3({ pageSize: 1 });
    const s3 = new S3Store({
      endpoint: new URL("https://s3.example.test"),
      region: "auto",
      bucket: "bursar-backups",
      prefix: "bursar",
      accessKeyId: "AKIDEXAMPLE",
      secretAccessKey: "s3-secret-access-key-value-0123456789",
      fetch: fake.fetch,
    });
    await backupTo(s3);
    expect([...fake.objects.keys()].sort()).toEqual([
      `bursar/${SET_ID}/${DB_FILE}`,
      `bursar/${SET_ID}/${MANIFEST_FILE}`,
    ]);

    const result = await restore({ source: s3 });
    expect(result.tables).toEqual(tableCounts(t.sqlite));
  });

  it("refuses a database file that does not match the manifest", async () => {
    const file = path.join(storeDir, SET_ID, DB_FILE);
    const bytes = readFileSync(file);
    bytes[bytes.length - 100] = (bytes[bytes.length - 100] ?? 0) ^ 0xff;
    writeFileSync(file, bytes);

    expect(await codeOf(restore())).toBe("checksum_mismatch");
    expectTargetUntouched();
  });

  it("refuses a master key that does not open the backup", async () => {
    expect(await codeOf(restore({ masterKey: Buffer.alloc(32, 9) }))).toBe("wrong_key");
    expectTargetUntouched();
  });

  it("reports a database that fails the integrity check", async () => {
    // Corrupt the last page and rewrite the manifest so that the checksum still matches.
    const file = path.join(storeDir, SET_ID, DB_FILE);
    const bytes = readFileSync(file);
    bytes[bytes.length - 100] = (bytes[bytes.length - 100] ?? 0) ^ 0xff;
    writeFileSync(file, bytes);
    const manifestFile = path.join(storeDir, SET_ID, MANIFEST_FILE);
    const manifest = JSON.parse(readFileSync(manifestFile, "utf8"));
    manifest.files[0].sha256 = sha256Hex(bytes);
    writeFileSync(manifestFile, JSON.stringify(manifest));

    expect(await codeOf(restore())).toBe("integrity_failed");
    expectTargetUntouched();
  });

  it("reports a set without a manifest, an unknown set and a malformed id as not found", async () => {
    expect(await codeOf(restore({ setId: "20991231T000000Z" }))).toBe("set_not_found");
    expect(await codeOf(restore({ setId: "../../etc" }))).toBe("set_not_found");
    rmSync(path.join(storeDir, SET_ID, MANIFEST_FILE));
    expect(await codeOf(restore())).toBe("set_not_found");
    expectTargetUntouched();
  });

  it("reports a manifest without its database file as not found", async () => {
    rmSync(path.join(storeDir, SET_ID, DB_FILE));
    expect(await codeOf(restore())).toBe("set_not_found");
  });

  it("refuses an existing database unless forced, and then drops its stale WAL", async () => {
    mkdirSync(target, { recursive: true });
    writeFileSync(path.join(target, DB_FILE), "an older database");
    writeFileSync(path.join(target, `${DB_FILE}-wal`), "a stale write-ahead log");

    expect(await codeOf(restore())).toBe("target_not_empty");
    expect(readFileSync(path.join(target, DB_FILE), "utf8")).toBe("an older database");

    const result = await restore({ force: true });
    expect(result.tables.transactions).toBe(3);
    expect(existsSync(path.join(target, `${DB_FILE}-wal`))).toBe(false);
    const restored = openDatabase(path.join(target, DB_FILE), databasePassphrase(t.masterKey));
    restored.close();
  });
});
