```ts
/**
 * Screenshots the reviewer looks at (UX doc §9) and checks the pieces no story covers: the
 * Settings page with an unsaved edit, the live "Backup completed" toast, the notifications
 * popover with the seeded events and the `#backups` deep link. Each gallery is desktop light,
 * desktop dark and 390 px (which also fails on horizontal overflow).
 */
async function gallery(ctx: StoryContext, name: string): Promise<void> {
  const { page } = ctx;
  await ctx.shot(`${name}-desktop-light`);
  await page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme: "dark" });
  await delay(500);
  await ctx.shot(`${name}-desktop-dark`);
  await page.setViewportSize({ width: 390, height: 844 });
  await page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme: "light" });
  await delay(500);
  const overflow = await page.evaluate(
    () => document.documentElement.scrollWidth - window.innerWidth,
  );
  check(overflow <= 1, `${name}: the page is ${overflow}px wider than the 390 px viewport`);
  await ctx.shot(`${name}-phone-light`);
  await page.setViewportSize({ width: 1440, height: 900 });
  await delay(300);
}

async function reviewShots(ctx: StoryContext): Promise<void> {
  const { page } = ctx;
  await useEnglish(ctx);
  await step("open Settings: five cards, one of them the #backups anchor", async () => {
    await page.goto(`${ctx.baseUrl}/settings`, { waitUntil: "load" });
    await page.getByRole("heading", { level: 1, name: "Settings" }).first().waitFor();
    for (const id of ["settings-general", "settings-banking", "settings-notifications", "settings-display", "backups"]) {
      check((await page.locator(`#${id}`).count()) === 1, `the card #${id} is missing`);
    }
  });
  await step("an unsaved edit shows the sticky bar, then Discard clears it", async () => {
    await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Edit section Banking" }).click();
    await page.getByLabel("Consent length (days)").fill("90");
    await page.getByRole("region", { name: "Unsaved changes" }).waitFor();
    await gallery(ctx, "settings-unsaved");
    await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Discard changes" }).click();
    await page.getByRole("region", { name: "Unsaved changes" }).waitFor({ state: "detached" });
  });
  await step("Back up now ends with the live 'Backup completed' toast and a new row", async () => {
    await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Back up now" }).click();
    await page.getByText("Backup completed").first().waitFor({ timeout: BACKUP_TIMEOUT_MS });
    await page.getByRole("cell", { name: "Manual" }).first().waitFor();
  });
  await step("the popover lists the seeded events with their parameters filled in", async () => {
    await page.getByRole("button", { name: /^Notifications/ }).click();
    const popover = page.getByRole("dialog", { name: "Notifications" });
    await popover.getByText("Consent expiring").waitFor();
    const text = await popover.innerText();
    check(text.includes("Northwind Bank"), "the bank name is missing from the consent text");
    check(!text.includes("{{") && !/undefined/.test(text), "a placeholder is visible");
    check(!/see all/i.test(text), "the popover has a 'see all' footer");
    await gallery(ctx, "notifications-popover");
    await popover.getByRole("button", { name: /Consent expiring/ }).click();
    await page.waitForURL(/\/accounts$/);
    await pollUntil("the unread count to reach zero", async () => {
      const feed = await ctx.get<NotificationListResponse>("/api/notifications?limit=6");
      return feed.unread === 0;
    });
  });
  await step("the #backups link scrolls the card into view", async () => {
    await page.goto(`${ctx.baseUrl}/settings#backups`, { waitUntil: "load" });
    await page.locator("#backups").waitFor();
    await delay(800);
    const { scrolled, top, height } = await page.evaluate(() => ({
      scrolled: window.scrollY,
      top: document.getElementById("backups")?.getBoundingClientRect().top ?? -1,
      height: window.innerHeight,
    }));
    check(scrolled > 0 && top >= 0 && top < height - 100, `the card sits ${Math.round(top)} px down after scrolling ${Math.round(scrolled)} px`);
    await gallery(ctx, "settings-backups");
  });
}

/** A fresh QA server and browser context around `body`; returns the failures (empty when clean). */
async function inFreshApp(
  browser: Browser,
  slug: string,
  body: (ctx: StoryContext) => Promise<void>,
): Promise<string[]> {
  const failures: string[] = [];
  const server = await startQaServer({ owner: true });
  let context: BrowserContext | null = null;
  try {
    const token = server.sessionToken;
    check(token !== null, "the QA server returned no session token");
    const capture = CAPTURES[0];
    check(capture !== undefined, "the desktop-light capture is missing");
    context = await newCaptureContext(browser, capture, { baseUrl: server.baseUrl, token });
    const page = await context.newPage();
    page.setDefaultTimeout(STEP_TIMEOUT_MS);
    const probe = attachProbe(page);
    const ctx = createStoryContext(page, context, server.baseUrl, slug);
    try {
      await body(ctx);
    } catch (error) {
      failures.push(errorMessage(error));
      await ctx.shot("failure").catch(() => undefined);
    }
    failures.push(...probe.failures);
    if ((await page.locator("[data-error-boundary]").count()) > 0) {
      failures.push("boundary: an error boundary is rendered");
    }
  } catch (error) {
    failures.push(errorMessage(error));
  } finally {
    await context?.close().catch(() => undefined);
    await server.stop();
  }
  return failures;
}

async function main(): Promise<void> {
  const { values } = parseArgs({
    options: {
      "skip-build": { type: "boolean", default: false },
      only: { type: "string" },
    },
  });
  const only = values.only ? new Set(values.only.split(",").map((id) => Number(id.trim()))) : null;
  const selected = STORIES.filter((story) => only === null || only.has(story.id));
  if (selected.length === 0) throw new Error(`No story matches --only ${values.only ?? ""}`);
  if (values["skip-build"] !== true) buildWeb();

  const browser = await launchBrowser();
  let passed = 0;
  let failed = 0;
  let reviewFailures: string[] | null = null;
  try {
    for (const story of selected) {
      const started = Date.now();
      const failures = await inFreshApp(browser, `${story.id}-${story.slug}`, story.run);
      const seconds = ((Date.now() - started) / 1000).toFixed(1);
      if (failures.length === 0) {
        passed += 1;
        console.log(`ok   ${story.id} ${story.title} (${seconds} s)`);
      } else {
        failed += 1;
        console.log(`FAIL ${story.id} ${story.title} (${seconds} s)`);
        for (const failure of [...new Set(failures)]) console.log(`       ${failure}`);
      }
    }
    if (only === null) reviewFailures = await inFreshApp(browser, "review", reviewShots);
  } finally {
    await browser.close();
  }

  console.log(`Stories: ${passed} passed, ${failed} failed`);
  if (reviewFailures !== null) {
    if (reviewFailures.length === 0) {
      console.log(`Review shots: ok (screenshots in ${path.relative(process.cwd(), STORIES_DIR)})`);
    } else {
      console.log("Review shots: FAILED");
      for (const failure of [...new Set(reviewFailures)]) console.log(`       ${failure}`);
    }
  }
  process.exitCode = failed > 0 || (reviewFailures?.length ?? 0) > 0 ? 1 : 0;
}

main().catch((error: unknown) => {
  console.error(`Stories failed to run: ${errorMessage(error)}`);
  process.exit(1);
});
```

Notes on the file:
- `connectBank` jumps to the consent step by URL (the wizard's URL state is a Task 20 contract: `QA_EXTRA_PATHS` there uses the same form) and clicks everything else. Story 2 sets `consentDays` to 10 through the API before connecting, because the wizard's default duration is `min(bank maximum, settings consentDays)`; that makes the connection `expiring` immediately, so "Renew" is its primary action, and the renewal then runs against the fake bank's stable account identities (the seeded QA connections use different identities, so renewing one of them would not exercise the mapping).
- Story 3 disconnects a seeded connection ("Polaris Finance", state `error`, account "Compte Courant") and purges it; the fake bank's `deleteSession` accepts unknown sessions.
- Story 5 waits for a page text that has the mask and no amount at all (`!AMOUNT.test(text) && text.includes(MASK)`), so a page that masks some amounts but leaks one (a chart summary, a KPI) keeps waiting and fails on the timeout with the page text in the message.
- If a story fails on a locator, open `apps/web/qa/out/stories/<id>-<slug>-failure.png` first: a wording difference in a Task 17 to 21 control is fixed in the `UI` table, a real defect in the page that owns the control.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

Tasks 6 to 22 are merged on the branch. The test reads the deploy files and documents from the repository root (`import.meta.dirname` is `apps/server/src`, three levels below it), runs `deploy/remote-update.sh` against a stub `docker` executable that only records its arguments, and, when `docker compose` is installed, asks Compose to merge the base file with every overlay. It imports `loadConfig` from Task 8 to prove that the empty strings Compose passes for unset integrations load as "off". The documents are read inside each test so that a missing document fails its own test.

Create `apps/server/src/deploy-files.test.ts`:

```ts
import { execFileSync, spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
import { chmodSync, mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, readFileSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { afterEach, describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { loadConfig } from "./config";

const repoRoot = path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, "..", "..", "..");
const read = (relative: string): string => readFileSync(path.join(repoRoot, relative), "utf8");

/** Non-secret values that compose.yaml passes to the app with an empty default (Task 8 names). */
const NON_SECRET_VARIABLES = [
  "EB_APPLICATION_ID",
  "SMTP_HOST",
  "SMTP_PORT",
  "SMTP_SECURITY",
  "SMTP_USER",
  "SMTP_FROM",
  "BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT",
  "BACKUP_S3_REGION",
  "BACKUP_S3_BUCKET",
  "BACKUP_S3_PREFIX",
  "BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID",
] as const;

/** One optional integration per overlay: its secret file and the `_FILE` variable it fills. */
const OVERLAYS = [
  { file: "compose.banking.yaml", secret: "eb_private_key", variable: "EB_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE" },
  { file: "compose.smtp.yaml", secret: "smtp_password", variable: "SMTP_PASSWORD_FILE" },
  {
    file: "compose.backup.yaml",
    secret: "backup_s3_secret_key",
    variable: "BACKUP_S3_SECRET_KEY_FILE",
  },
] as const;

const LOGGING = ["driver: json-file", 'max-size: "10m"', 'max-file: "3"'];

const emptyDefault = (name: string): string => `${name}: \${${name}:-}`;

const noFiles = (file: string): string => {
  throw new Error(`unexpected read of ${file}`);
};

const cleanup: string[] = [];
afterEach(() => {
  for (const dir of cleanup.splice(0)) rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
});

function scratchDir(prefix: string): string {
  const dir = mkdtempSync(path.join(tmpdir(), prefix));
  cleanup.push(dir);
  return dir;
}

describe("compose.yaml", () => {
  const compose = read("deploy/compose.yaml");
  const appBlock = compose.slice(compose.indexOf("\n  app:"), compose.indexOf("\n  cloudflared:"));
  const cloudflaredBlock = compose.slice(
    compose.indexOf("\n  cloudflared:"),
    compose.indexOf("\nsecrets:"),
  );

  it.each(NON_SECRET_VARIABLES)("passes %s to the app with an empty default", (name) => {
    expect(appBlock).toContain(emptyDefault(name));
  });

  it("rotates the container logs of app and cloudflared", () => {
    for (const block of [appBlock, cloudflaredBlock]) {
      expect(block).toContain("logging:");
      for (const line of LOGGING) expect(block).toContain(line);
    }
  });

  it("leaves every optional secret to its overlay", () => {
    for (const { secret } of OVERLAYS) expect(compose).not.toContain(secret);
    expect(compose).not.toContain("claude_credential");
  });

  it("loads with every empty default and reports no optional integration", () => {
    const empties = [...compose.matchAll(/^\s+([A-Z0-9_]+): \$\{\1:-\}$/gm)].map((m) => m[1] ?? "");
    for (const name of NON_SECRET_VARIABLES) expect(empties).toContain(name);
    const env = {
      BURSAR_PUBLIC_URL: "https://bursar.example.com",
      TZ: "Europe/Rome",
      BURSAR_MASTER_KEY: Buffer.alloc(32, 5).toString("base64"),
      ...Object.fromEntries(empties.map((name) => [name, ""])),
    };
    const config = loadConfig(env, noFiles);
    expect(config.enableBanking).toBeNull();
    expect(config.smtp).toBeNull();
    expect(config.backup.s3).toBeNull();
  });
});

describe("compose overlays", () => {
  it.each(OVERLAYS)("$file adds the $secret secret and $variable", ({ file, secret, variable }) => {
    const overlay = read(`deploy/${file}`);
    expect(overlay).toContain(`- ${variable}=/run/secrets/${secret}`);
    expect(overlay).toContain(`      - ${secret}\n`);
    expect(overlay).toContain(
      `  ${secret}:\n    file: \${BURSAR_SECRETS_DIR:-./secrets}/${secret}`,
    );
    expect(overlay.match(/^\s+[a-z0-9_]+:\n\s+file:/gm)).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  const dockerAvailable =
    spawnSync("docker", ["compose", "version"], { stdio: "ignore" }).status === 0;
  it.skipIf(!dockerAvailable)("merges with the base file into a valid compose model", () => {
    const secrets = scratchDir("bursar-compose-secrets-");
    for (const name of ["master_key", "claude_credential", ...OVERLAYS.map((o) => o.secret)]) {
      writeFileSync(path.join(secrets, name), "");
    }
    const files = ["compose.yaml", "compose.claude.yaml", ...OVERLAYS.map((o) => o.file)].flatMap(
      (file) => ["-f", path.join(repoRoot, "deploy", file)],
    );
    const model = execFileSync("docker", ["compose", ...files, "--profile", "tunnel", "config"], {
      encoding: "utf8",
      env: {
        ...process.env,
        BURSAR_PUBLIC_URL: "https://bursar.example.com",
        TZ: "Europe/Rome",
        BURSAR_SECRETS_DIR: secrets,
      },
    });
    for (const { secret, variable } of OVERLAYS) {
      expect(model).toContain(`${variable}: /run/secrets/${secret}`);
    }
    expect(model.match(/max-size: 10m/g)).toHaveLength(2);
  });
});

describe("env.example", () => {
  const example = read("deploy/env.example");

  it.each(NON_SECRET_VARIABLES)("documents %s as a commented entry", (name) => {
    expect(example).toMatch(new RegExp(`^# ${name}=`, "m"));
  });

  it("never holds a secret value, only the names of the secret files", () => {
    expect(example).not.toMatch(
      /^#?\s*(EB_PRIVATE_KEY|SMTP_PASSWORD|BACKUP_S3_SECRET_KEY)(_FILE)?=/m,
    );
    for (const { secret } of OVERLAYS) expect(example).toContain(secret);
  });

  it("reminds operators to trust CF-Connecting-IP behind a tunnel", () => {
    expect(example).toMatch(/^#.*BURSAR_TRUST_CF_CONNECTING_IP=true/m);
    expect(example).toMatch(/^BURSAR_TRUST_CF_CONNECTING_IP=false$/m);
  });
});

describe("remote-update.sh", () => {
  const script = path.join(repoRoot, "deploy", "remote-update.sh");

  /** Runs the script against a stub `docker` and returns the compose files of the `up` call. */
  function composeFilesFor(options: { secrets: readonly string[]; relative?: boolean }): string[] {
    const base = scratchDir("bursar-remote-update-");
    const dir = path.join(base, "deploy-dir");
    const releaseDeploy = path.join(dir, "releases", "r1", "deploy");
    const secretsDir = options.relative
      ? path.join(releaseDeploy, "secrets")
      : path.join(base, "secrets");
    mkdirSync(releaseDeploy, { recursive: true });
    mkdirSync(secretsDir, { recursive: true });
    writeFileSync(
      path.join(dir, ".env"),
      options.relative ? "TZ=UTC\n" : `BURSAR_SECRETS_DIR=${secretsDir}\n`,
    );
    for (const name of ["master_key", ...options.secrets]) {
      writeFileSync(path.join(secretsDir, name), "secret-stub");
    }
    const bin = path.join(base, "bin");
    mkdirSync(bin);
    const log = path.join(base, "docker.log");
    writeFileSync(path.join(bin, "docker"), '#!/bin/sh\necho "$*" >> "$DOCKER_LOG"\n');
    chmodSync(path.join(bin, "docker"), 0o755);
    execFileSync("bash", [script, dir, "r1"], {
      env: {
        ...process.env,
        PATH: `${bin}${path.delimiter}${process.env.PATH ?? ""}`,
        DOCKER_LOG: log,
      },
      stdio: "pipe",
    });
    const upCall = readFileSync(log, "utf8")
      .split("\n")
      .find((line) => line.includes(" up "));
    expect(upCall).toBeDefined();
    return [...(upCall ?? "").matchAll(/-f (\S+)/g)].map((m) => path.basename(m[1] ?? ""));
  }

  it("is valid bash", () => {
    expect(() => execFileSync("bash", ["-n", script])).not.toThrow();
  });

  it("uses only the base file when no optional secret exists", () => {
    expect(composeFilesFor({ secrets: [] })).toEqual(["compose.yaml"]);
  });

  it("adds every overlay whose secret file exists, in a fixed order", () => {
    expect(
      composeFilesFor({
        secrets: ["backup_s3_secret_key", "smtp_password", "eb_private_key", "claude_credential"],
      }),
    ).toEqual([
      "compose.yaml",
      "compose.claude.yaml",
      "compose.banking.yaml",
      "compose.smtp.yaml",
      "compose.backup.yaml",
    ]);
  });

  it("skips the overlays whose secret file is missing", () => {
    expect(composeFilesFor({ secrets: ["smtp_password", "backup_s3_secret_key"] })).toEqual([
      "compose.yaml",
      "compose.smtp.yaml",
      "compose.backup.yaml",
    ]);
  });

  it("resolves a relative secrets directory against the release's deploy directory", () => {
    expect(composeFilesFor({ secrets: ["eb_private_key"], relative: true })).toEqual([
      "compose.yaml",
      "compose.banking.yaml",
    ]);
  });
});
```

```yaml
services:

      CF_ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN: ${CF_ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN:-}
      CF_ACCESS_AUD: ${CF_ACCESS_AUD:-}
      BURSAR_TRUST_CF_CONNECTING_IP: ${BURSAR_TRUST_CF_CONNECTING_IP:-false}
      # Optional integrations. Empty means off. The secrets for them (EB_PRIVATE_KEY,
      # SMTP_PASSWORD, BACKUP_S3_SECRET_KEY) come from the overlays compose.banking.yaml,
      # compose.smtp.yaml and compose.backup.yaml, which the deploy adds when the secret exists.
      EB_APPLICATION_ID: ${EB_APPLICATION_ID:-}
      SMTP_HOST: ${SMTP_HOST:-}
      SMTP_PORT: ${SMTP_PORT:-}
      SMTP_SECURITY: ${SMTP_SECURITY:-}
      SMTP_USER: ${SMTP_USER:-}
      SMTP_FROM: ${SMTP_FROM:-}
      BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT: ${BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT:-}
      BACKUP_S3_REGION: ${BACKUP_S3_REGION:-}
      BACKUP_S3_BUCKET: ${BACKUP_S3_BUCKET:-}
      BACKUP_S3_PREFIX: ${BACKUP_S3_PREFIX:-}
      BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID:-}
    secrets:
      - master_key
    volumes:
      - bursar-data:/data
    read_only: true
    tmpfs:
      - /tmp
      - /home/node:uid=1000,gid=1000,mode=700
    mem_limit: ${BURSAR_MEM_LIMIT:-3g}
    logging:
      driver: json-file
      options:
        max-size: "10m"
        max-file: "3"
    healthcheck:
      test:
        - CMD
        - node
        - -e
        - "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz').then(r=>process.exit(r.ok?0:1)).catch(()=>process.exit(1))"
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 20s

  cloudflared:
    image: cloudflare/cloudflared:2026.10.7
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: tunnel --no-autoupdate run
    environment:
      TUNNEL_TOKEN: ${TUNNEL_TOKEN:-}
    depends_on:
      app:
        condition: service_healthy
    mem_limit: 128m
    logging:
      driver: json-file
      options:
        max-size: "10m"
        max-file: "3"
    profiles: [tunnel]

secrets:
  master_key:
    file: ${BURSAR_SECRETS_DIR:-./secrets}/master_key

volumes:
  bursar-data:
```

Create `deploy/compose.banking.yaml`:

```yaml
services:
  app:
    environment:
      - EB_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE=/run/secrets/eb_private_key
    secrets:
      - eb_private_key

secrets:
  eb_private_key:
    file: ${BURSAR_SECRETS_DIR:-./secrets}/eb_private_key
```

Create `deploy/compose.smtp.yaml`:

```yaml
services:
  app:
    environment:
      - SMTP_PASSWORD_FILE=/run/secrets/smtp_password
    secrets:
      - smtp_password

secrets:
  smtp_password:
    file: ${BURSAR_SECRETS_DIR:-./secrets}/smtp_password
```

Create `deploy/compose.backup.yaml`:

```yaml
services:
  app:
    environment:
      - BACKUP_S3_SECRET_KEY_FILE=/run/secrets/backup_s3_secret_key
    secrets:
      - backup_s3_secret_key

secrets:
  backup_s3_secret_key:
    file: ${BURSAR_SECRETS_DIR:-./secrets}/backup_s3_secret_key
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Include each overlay when its secret file exists**

Replace `deploy/remote-update.sh` with the following (executable bit unchanged: edit the file in place, do not recreate it with a different mode; check with `ls -l deploy/remote-update.sh` that it still shows `-rwxr-xr-x`). The Claude overlay keeps its behaviour; the three new ones follow the same lookup in the secrets directory, in a fixed order.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs on the Docker host: points "current" at a release and (re)starts the stack.
# Usage: remote-update.sh <deploy dir> <release name>
set -euo pipefail

dir="$1"
release="$2"
release_dir="$dir/releases/$release"

[[ -f "$dir/.env" ]] || { echo "Missing $dir/.env" >&2; exit 1; }

# Same lookup as compose: BURSAR_SECRETS_DIR from .env, default ./secrets,
# relative paths resolved against the compose project directory.
secrets_dir="$(sed -n 's/^BURSAR_SECRETS_DIR=//p' "$dir/.env" | tail -n 1)"
secrets_dir="${secrets_dir%[\"\']}"
secrets_dir="${secrets_dir#[\"\']}"
secrets_dir="${secrets_dir:-./secrets}"
[[ "$secrets_dir" == /* ]] || secrets_dir="$release_dir/deploy/$secrets_dir"

[[ -f "$secrets_dir/master_key" ]] || { echo "Missing $secrets_dir/master_key" >&2; exit 1; }

# Optional integrations: each overlay adds one secret and is included only when that secret
# file exists (compose fails on a declared secret whose file is missing).
# Format: <secret file name>:<overlay file name>
overlays=(
  "claude_credential:compose.claude.yaml"
  "eb_private_key:compose.banking.yaml"
  "smtp_password:compose.smtp.yaml"
  "backup_s3_secret_key:compose.backup.yaml"
)

compose=(docker compose --env-file "$dir/.env" -f "$release_dir/deploy/compose.yaml")
for entry in "${overlays[@]}"; do
  secret="${entry%%:*}"
  overlay="${entry#*:}"
  if [[ -f "$secrets_dir/$secret" ]]; then
    echo "Including $overlay ($secret found)"
    compose+=(-f "$release_dir/deploy/$overlay")
  fi
done

"${compose[@]}" --profile tunnel up -d --build --remove-orphans --wait --wait-timeout 180
ln -sfn "$release_dir" "$dir/current"
"${compose[@]}" --profile tunnel ps
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Document the variables in `deploy/env.example`**

Replace `deploy/env.example` with the following. The new entries are commented out (Compose would otherwise pass half-configured integrations), `BURSAR_TRUST_CF_CONNECTING_IP` keeps the safe value `false` and carries the reminder to set `true` behind a tunnel, and `BURSAR_BACKUP_DIR` is deliberately not offered: the container default `/data/backups` lives on the data volume and `compose.yaml` does not pass the variable.

```bash
# Copy to deploy/.env for local use, or to <deploy dir>/.env on a host. Never commit the copy.
BURSAR_PUBLIC_URL=https://bursar.example.com
TZ=Europe/Rome

# Directory holding master_key and the optional secret files: claude_credential, eb_private_key,
# smtp_password and backup_s3_secret_key (each one switches on its compose overlay when present).
# Compose mounts these files with their host owner and mode, and the app runs as uid 1000, so
# each file must be readable by uid 1000: chown 1000:1000 <file> && chmod 600 <file>. Under
# rootless Docker, Podman or userns-remap, uid 1000 in the container maps to a different host
# uid; set the owner to that mapped uid instead. Docker Desktop ignores the host owner; for local
# development there, chmod 644 <file> if the app reports EACCES. To create the master key with
# the right owner, generate it inside the image (the secrets directory must be writable by
# uid 1000 meanwhile):
#   docker run --rm --user 1000:1000 -v "$PWD/secrets:/out" bursar:local \
#     node dist/cli.js init --out /out/master_key
BURSAR_SECRETS_DIR=./secrets

BURSAR_MEM_LIMIT=3g

# Cloudflare Access (optional, recommended): set both or neither. Defence in depth on top of
# the app login. The team domain is a bare hostname, for example <team>.cloudflareaccess.com.
# Without Access on a non-loopback URL, the app logs a warning at startup.
CF_ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN=
CF_ACCESS_AUD=

# Cloudflare Tunnel token, used by the "tunnel" profile.
TUNNEL_TOKEN=

# Use the CF-Connecting-IP header as the client address (login rate limit and the address that
# "Sync now" forwards to the bank as the user's).
# Behind a Cloudflare Tunnel every request arrives from cloudflared, so set
# BURSAR_TRUST_CF_CONNECTING_IP=true there: with false, "Sync now" sees a private address, sends
# no user headers and counts against the banks' background limit like a scheduled sync.
# Leave false when the app is reachable without Cloudflare: clients could forge the header.
BURSAR_TRUST_CF_CONNECTING_IP=false

# Which variable compose.claude.yaml fills: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN.
BURSAR_CLAUDE_CREDENTIAL_ENV=ANTHROPIC_API_KEY

# --- Bank accounts through Enable Banking (read-only) ---
# Setup guide: docs/enable-banking.md. Set the application id here and put the RSA private key in
# <secrets dir>/eb_private_key; the deploy then adds compose.banking.yaml. Set both or neither:
# a half-configured integration stops the app at startup, naming the variable.
# Application id (a uuid) shown in the Enable Banking Control Panel after you upload the certificate.
# EB_APPLICATION_ID=

# --- Email notifications (SMTP) ---
# Optional. Notification emails carry an event title and a link to the panel, never financial data.
# Put the SMTP password in <secrets dir>/smtp_password (compose.smtp.yaml). Leave the password
# file out for a relay that needs no login (then leave SMTP_USER empty too).
# Mail server host name.
# SMTP_HOST=
# Port: 587 with starttls (default), 465 with tls.
# SMTP_PORT=587
# Connection security: starttls (default), tls (implicit TLS) or none (accepted only for a
# loopback host).
# SMTP_SECURITY=starttls
# Login name; empty when the server needs no login.
# SMTP_USER=
# Sender address of the notification emails (required when SMTP_HOST is set).
# SMTP_FROM=bursar@example.com

# --- Backups ---
# Setup guide: docs/backup-restore.md. Nightly encrypted copies are always kept on the data
# volume in /data/backups (the default; not set through compose). The variables below add an
# S3-compatible target, for example Cloudflare R2. Put the secret access key in
# <secrets dir>/backup_s3_secret_key (compose.backup.yaml). The endpoint, bucket, access key id
# and secret key go together (all or none); the region and the prefix are optional.
# Endpoint URL; for R2 it is https://<account id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com
# BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT=
# Region; R2 uses auto (default).
# BACKUP_S3_REGION=auto
# Bucket name (create it private).
# BACKUP_S3_BUCKET=
# Key prefix inside the bucket, without leading or trailing slash (default bursar).
# BACKUP_S3_PREFIX=bursar
# Access key id of an API token that can read, write, list and delete objects in that bucket.
# BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID=
```

````markdown
# Enable Banking setup

Bursar reads balances and transactions of your bank accounts through [Enable Banking](https://enablebanking.com), a licensed account-information provider. Access is read-only: the server can call a fixed list of account-information operations (banks, authorisation, sessions, balances, transactions), and every payment operation is rejected before a request leaves the process.

This guide uses placeholders: `<host>` (ssh alias of the Docker host), `<dir>` (deploy directory on the host), `<hostname>` (public hostname of the panel). Secrets are never written in documents or commands: the private key lives in a file on the host.

## 1. Sandbox or production

An Enable Banking application belongs to one environment, and it cannot be moved to the other. Both environments use the same API address; the environment is a property of the application (its id), not of the URL.

| | Sandbox | Production (restricted mode) |
|---|---|---|
| Banks | Test banks such as "Mock ASPSP", with test users | Your real banks |
| Activation | Automatic | By linking your own accounts in the Control Panel (see section 5) |
| Data | Fake transactions, returned in batches of 10, newest first | Your real accounts, only the linked ones |
| Caveats | Sessions can expire before the requested date, date filters are unreliable, some test banks are unstable | Real banks, real strong customer authentication |

Use a Sandbox application to try Bursar and to test the renewal of a consent before connecting a real bank. Use a production application, in restricted mode, for your own accounts.

## 2. Create the key and the certificate

Enable Banking authenticates every request with a signed token (RS256). You keep an RSA private key; you upload only the matching certificate. The private key never leaves your server and is never committed, logged or shown by Bursar.

On the Docker host, create the key straight into the secrets directory (readable by uid 1000, mode 600) and the certificate next to it:

    ssh <host> 'test ! -e <dir>/secrets/eb_private_key && (umask 077; openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:4096 -sha256 -nodes -days 3650 -subj "/CN=bursar" -keyout <dir>/secrets/eb_private_key -out <dir>/eb_certificate.pem) && chown 1000:1000 <dir>/secrets/eb_private_key && chmod 600 <dir>/secrets/eb_private_key'

The `test ! -e` guard refuses to replace an existing key. Check that the key parses without printing it, and copy the public certificate to your workstation to upload it:

    ssh <host> 'openssl pkey -in <dir>/secrets/eb_private_key -noout && echo key-ok'
    scp <host>:<dir>/eb_certificate.pem .

The certificate is public and can be deleted from the host after the upload. Keep an offline copy of the private key next to the offline copy of the master key: without it you create a new key and a new certificate, and upload the certificate again.

For local development with a Sandbox application, create the key outside the repository, for example in a private directory of your home, with the same `openssl req` command and `umask 077`, and point `EB_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE` at it in `apps/server/.env`. The repository's `.gitignore` also excludes `*.pem` and `*.key`, but a key never belongs inside the working tree.

The Control Panel can also generate the key in your browser and offer it for download once. That works, but the key then passes through your workstation; if you use it, move the file to the host, set the owner and mode as above, and delete the download.

## 3. Register the application

1. Open the Enable Banking Control Panel (https://enablebanking.com/cp/applications) and add an application.
2. Choose the environment: Sandbox or Production.
3. Name it, upload `eb_certificate.pem`, and fill the other fields the form asks for. In restricted mode Enable Banking does not verify the terms, privacy and data protection fields.
4. Add the redirect URL (see below).
5. Copy the **application id** (a uuid) that the Control Panel shows.

### Redirect URL

Enable Banking sends the browser back to a redirect URL that you whitelist per application. Bursar always uses `<BURSAR_PUBLIC_URL>/api/banks/callback`:

- Production and a deployed Sandbox: `https://<hostname>/api/banks/callback`
- Local development against the Sandbox (the panel dev server on port 5173 proxies `/api` to the server, and `BURSAR_PUBLIC_URL` is `http://localhost:5173` in `apps/server/.env.example`): `http://localhost:5173/api/banks/callback`

The URL must match exactly: scheme, host, port and path, without a trailing slash. If Enable Banking refuses an `http://localhost` redirect URL for a Sandbox application, run the Sandbox application on a deployed host instead, with the `https://<hostname>` URL. A mismatch is reported as `REDIRECT_URI_NOT_ALLOWED` (see the troubleshooting section). The panel shows whether the URL is accepted under Settings, Banking ("Redirect URL allowed").

## 4. Configure Bursar

On a host, set the application id in `<dir>/.env` and make sure the key file exists at `<dir>/secrets/eb_private_key`:

    EB_APPLICATION_ID=<application id>
    BURSAR_TRUST_CF_CONNECTING_IP=true

The deploy adds `deploy/compose.banking.yaml` automatically when `eb_private_key` exists in the secrets directory, and passes the key to the app as `EB_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE`. Set the application id and place the key in the same deploy: with only one of them the app refuses to start and names the missing variable in `docker logs bursar-app-1`.

`BURSAR_TRUST_CF_CONNECTING_IP=true` is required behind a Cloudflare Tunnel. Every request then reaches the app from cloudflared, and the address of the person using the panel comes from the `CF-Connecting-IP` header. Without it, "Sync now" sees a private address and syncs as a background job (see section 7). Leave it `false` when the app is reachable without Cloudflare, because clients could forge the header.

For local development, put `EB_APPLICATION_ID` and `EB_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE` (the path of the key) in `apps/server/.env`.

After the deploy, open Settings, Banking in the panel: it shows the environment, whether the application is active and whether the redirect URL is allowed. `docker exec bursar-app-1 node dist/cli.js banking status` lists the connections and accounts later on (masked identifiers only).

## 5. Restricted mode: link your accounts first

A production application starts as pending. Without a contract, Enable Banking activates it for personal use when you link (whitelist) your own bank accounts in the Control Panel (the "activate by linking accounts" option of the application; the labels may change). In restricted mode:

- The authorisation flow works for anyone, but only the linked accounts return data. Accounts that are not linked are stripped from the response.
- Link every account you want in Bursar before you authorise the bank. The identifier to link is the IBAN of the account (as the Control Panel asks for it).
- If you authorise a bank and none of the shared accounts is linked, the list of accounts comes back empty.

### What an empty account list means

Bursar treats an empty list as its own outcome, not as a success: the wizard shows "no accounts were shared, or they are not linked in the Enable Banking Control Panel", closes the session at the bank so no unused consent stays open, and creates no connection. Link the missing accounts in the Control Panel and connect the bank again.

## 6. Connect a bank, consent duration and renewal

1. In the panel, open Accounts and start the Connect wizard.
2. Pick the country and the bank. Bursar asks the bank list from Enable Banking for that country.
3. Authorise at the bank (strong customer authentication). The bank sends you back to Bursar, which shows the accounts it found and starts the first sync.

Complete the flow in a browser where you are signed in to the panel: the code exchange is an authenticated request, because session cookies are not sent on the cross-site redirect back from the bank. If the bank's app opens a different browser, sign in there and start again.

The first sync runs immediately. Many banks give the full transaction history only for a short time after authorisation (about an hour is typical) and limit later access to roughly the last 90 days, so connect when you have a few minutes and wait for the first sync to finish.

The **consent duration** is set in Settings, Banking (default 180 days). Each bank has a maximum (180 days for most); Bursar asks for the shorter of the two, minus a few minutes of margin. There is no refresh: when a consent ends you authorise again. Bursar warns by notification 14 days and 3 days before the end. A consent can also end early (see `EXPIRED_SESSION`).

To renew, use Renew on the connection in the Accounts page and authorise at the bank again. Accounts are matched to the existing ones through the identifier the bank provides (and the IBAN as a fallback), so names, history and settings stay attached. An account that the bank no longer returns becomes unavailable instead of disappearing.

## 7. Limits, background sync and "Sync now"

Banks limit how often a service can read an account while the customer is not present. Many allow 4 background fetches per account per day, and the figure can differ per bank. Bursar therefore:

- syncs once a day at the time set in Settings, Banking, and never more than the configured number of background syncs per account per day (default 2, from 1 to 4);
- after `ASPSP_RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, pauses that account for 6 hours;
- treats "Sync now" as a request from the person using the panel: it forwards your IP address and browser details to the bank as the user's, which banks count differently from background access. This only happens when the app sees a public client address, which behind Cloudflare Tunnel needs `BURSAR_TRUST_CF_CONNECTING_IP=true`; otherwise "Sync now" behaves like a background sync and counts against the limit.

Your address and browser details are sent to the bank with that request, which is a privacy consideration of its own. Avoid pressing "Sync now" repeatedly: the bank decides what it allows.

## 8. The Terms of restricted mode (gate V5)

Restricted mode is free. The project's research found that Enable Banking's Terms limit it to evaluation or personal use by private individuals; the Terms themselves are the authority. Before you connect real accounts (gate V5 of the project):

1. Read the Enable Banking Terms that apply to restricted mode in full.
2. Confirm that your use, which is read-only access to your own accounts for yourself, is within them.
3. Write down the date and the result (the reference deployment records it in `docs/decisions/0004-enable-banking-production.md`).

Do not link accounts of other people or of a company with this setup. If the Terms are unclear to you, stay on the Sandbox and ask Enable Banking before going further.

## 9. Troubleshooting by error code

Bursar logs and shows only the HTTP status, the error code and Enable Banking's message. Match on the code, not on the status: the same status can carry different codes.

### `REDIRECT_URI_NOT_ALLOWED`

Seen when starting a connection or a renewal. The redirect URL is not whitelisted for the application. Compare the URL shown under Settings, Banking with the list in the Control Panel; they must match exactly (scheme, host, port, path, no trailing slash). Fix `BURSAR_PUBLIC_URL` if the host is wrong, or add the URL in the Control Panel, then try again.

### `EXPIRED_SESSION`

Seen during a sync. The consent has ended, often before the date you asked for (Sandbox banks are known to expire sessions early, and a customer can revoke at the bank). The connection shows as expired and Bursar sends a notification. Renew the consent (section 6); history is kept.

### `ASPSP_RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`

Seen during a sync, usually with HTTP 429. The bank refuses more reads while you are not present. Bursar pauses the account for 6 hours and tries again later by itself. If it recurs, lower the number of background syncs per account in Settings, Banking, and avoid repeated "Sync now".

### `PSU_HEADER_NOT_PROVIDED`

Seen during a manual sync, with HTTP 422. Some banks require the whole set of user headers, or none. Bursar retries the same sync once without the headers (as a background sync, counted against the limit) and the sync completes. If it appears for scheduled syncs, which never send those headers, report it as a bug. The related `PSU_HEADER_INVALID` means a header had an unusable value.

### Other messages you may meet

- `NO_ACCOUNTS_ADDED`: the application is in restricted mode and no allowed accounts are linked yet. Link them (section 5).
- `WRONG_ASPSP_PROVIDED`: the bank name or country does not match the bank list. Reload the Connect page and pick the bank again.
- `EXPIRED_AUTHORIZATION_CODE`, `WRONG_AUTHORIZATION_CODE`, `ALREADY_AUTHORIZED`: the code from the bank was used too late, is wrong, or was already used (for example after reloading the callback page). Start the connection again; nothing is created from a failed attempt.
- `AUTHORIZATION_NOT_PROVIDED`, `UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS`, `ACCESS_DENIED`: the request was not accepted as coming from your application. Check that the key matches the uploaded certificate, that `EB_APPLICATION_ID` is the id of that application, and that the host clock is correct.
- The app does not start and `docker logs bursar-app-1` shows `Invalid configuration` with `EB_APPLICATION_ID` or the key: the id and the key file must be configured together, and the file must contain an RSA private key.
````

- [ ] **Step 8: Write `docs/backup-restore.md`**

Create `docs/backup-restore.md`. The set layout, retention and CLI are Task 15's contract; the swap procedure runs the CLI in a one-off container of the `app` service (same image, secrets and volume, read-only root filesystem) while the app is stopped.

````markdown
# Backups and restore

Bursar copies its encrypted database every night, keeps the copies on the data volume, and uploads them to an S3-compatible bucket if you configure one. This guide covers what a backup holds, how long copies are kept, how to set up Cloudflare R2, the command-line tools, how to put a restored database in place, and the restore test that proves it all works.

This guide uses placeholders: `<host>` (ssh alias of the Docker host), `<dir>` (deploy directory on the host), `<setId>` (a backup set id such as `20261109T030000Z`).

## 1. What a backup set contains

A backup set is a folder named by its UTC creation time, `YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ`, with two files:

- `bursar.db`: a consistent copy of the database, made with SQLite's `VACUUM INTO`. It is still encrypted with the SQLCipher key derived from the master key, so neither the local disk copy nor the bucket ever holds plaintext data. Before upload, Bursar opens the copy with the derived key and runs an integrity check; a copy that fails is not uploaded.
- `manifest.json`: the format version, the set id, the creation time, the number of schema migrations, and the name, size and SHA-256 of every file. It is uploaded last, so a set without a manifest is incomplete and is ignored by `backup list` and `restore`.

The master key is never stored in a backup. You need it to read any set: keep an offline copy of `<dir>/secrets/master_key` (for example in a password manager), and keep it apart from the bucket. A backup without the key cannot be decrypted, and a stolen bucket without the key is ciphertext.

The documents archive arrives with a later milestone; the manifest has room for more files.

## 2. Schedule and retention

- A backup runs once a day at the time set in Settings, Backups (default 03:00 in the server's time zone). You can also run one on demand with "Back up now" in Settings, Backups, or from the command line.
- Every backup is kept on the data volume in `/data/backups`, and also uploaded to the bucket when one is configured. The local copies live on the same disk as the database: they protect against mistakes and corruption, not against losing the disk or the host. Settings, Backups shows a persistent warning while no remote target is configured.
- Retention keeps 7 daily, 4 weekly and 6 monthly sets (the newest set of each of the last 7 days, 4 weeks and 6 months; the newest set is always kept). It is applied to the local folder and to the bucket after every successful backup.
- After two failed backups in a row, Bursar raises a notification linking to Settings, Backups. The same page lists the recent runs.

## 3. Remote target: Cloudflare R2

Cloudflare R2 is the reference target; any S3-compatible service that supports path-style addresses and AWS Signature Version 4 should work the same way, but only R2 is documented here.

1. In the Cloudflare dashboard, open R2 and create a bucket. Keep it private: no public access, no custom domain.
2. Create an R2 API token with the Object Read and Write permission, restricted to that one bucket. Bursar lists, uploads, downloads and deletes objects (retention deletes old sets), so the token must allow all four. The labels in the dashboard may differ from these names.
3. Copy the **Access Key ID**, the **Secret Access Key** (shown once) and the S3 endpoint, which looks like `https://<account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`.
4. Put the non-secret values in `<dir>/.env`:

        BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT=https://<account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com
        BACKUP_S3_REGION=auto
        BACKUP_S3_BUCKET=<bucket name>
        BACKUP_S3_PREFIX=bursar
        BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID=<access key id>

5. Write the secret access key into `<dir>/secrets/backup_s3_secret_key` (owner 1000, mode 600) without putting it in a command line or shell history, then check ownership and modes only:

        ssh <host> 'set -C; umask 077; cat > <dir>/secrets/backup_s3_secret_key && chown 1000:1000 <dir>/secrets/backup_s3_secret_key && chmod 600 <dir>/secrets/backup_s3_secret_key'
        ssh <host> 'ls -la <dir>/secrets'

   Paste the key, press Enter, then Ctrl-D. `set -C` makes the command fail instead of replacing an existing file.
6. Deploy. `deploy/remote-update.sh` adds `deploy/compose.backup.yaml` when `backup_s3_secret_key` exists. The endpoint, bucket, access key id and secret key go together: with only some of them the app refuses to start and names the missing variables.

Do not add an R2 lifecycle rule that deletes objects: Bursar prunes by its own retention policy.

Settings, Backups now shows the target as remote. Run a first backup to check it:

    ssh <host> 'docker exec bursar-app-1 node dist/cli.js backup run'

Expected: a JSON line with `setId`, `sizeBytes` and `"target":"s3"`.

## 4. Command line

The commands run inside the container, as the app user, with the app's own configuration (master key, bucket settings). On a host:

    ssh <host> 'docker exec bursar-app-1 node dist/cli.js backup run'
    ssh <host> 'docker exec bursar-app-1 node dist/cli.js backup list'
    ssh <host> 'docker exec bursar-app-1 node dist/cli.js backup list --remote'
    ssh <host> 'docker exec bursar-app-1 node dist/cli.js restore --set <setId> --from s3 --to <target dir>'

- `backup run` makes a backup now and prints `{"setId":…,"sizeBytes":…,"target":…}`.
- `backup list` prints the set ids in the local folder, newest first; `--remote` lists the bucket.
- `restore --set <setId> --to <dir> [--from local|s3] [--force]` writes `<dir>/bursar.db` (mode 600) from the chosen set, after checking the manifest checksums, opening the database with the master key and running an integrity check. It prints `{"restored":"<setId>","tables":{…}}` with the row count of each table. It refuses to overwrite an existing `bursar.db` unless you pass `--force`. Pass `--from` explicitly.
- `banking status [--data-dir <dir>]` prints the connections and accounts with their transaction counts (masked identifiers only). With `--data-dir` it reads the database in that directory.

In development, run the same commands with `pnpm --filter @bursar/server bursar backup run` and so on.

A failed restore exits with status 1 and one of these codes:

- `set_not_found`: the set does not exist or has no manifest.
- `checksum_mismatch`: a file differs from the manifest (corrupted or tampered).
- `wrong_key`: the database cannot be opened with this master key.
- `integrity_failed`: the database opens but fails its integrity check.
- `target_not_empty`: the target already holds a `bursar.db`.

## 5. The restore test

A backup you have never restored is a hope, not a backup. Run this test after the first remote backup, after changing the target, the bucket or the key handling, and from time to time afterwards. It restores into a scratch directory in the container's memory-backed `/tmp` and never touches the live database.

    ssh <host> 'docker exec bursar-app-1 node dist/cli.js backup run'
    ssh <host> 'docker exec bursar-app-1 node dist/cli.js restore --set <setId> --from s3 --to /tmp/restore-test'
    ssh <host> 'docker exec bursar-app-1 node dist/cli.js banking status --data-dir /tmp/restore-test'
    ssh <host> 'docker exec bursar-app-1 node dist/cli.js banking status'
    ssh <host> 'docker exec bursar-app-1 rm -rf /tmp/restore-test'

It passes when:

- the backup reports `"target":"s3"` and the restore exits with status 0;
- the table counts printed by `restore` are plausible for your data (accounts, transactions);
- `banking status --data-dir /tmp/restore-test` lists the same connections and accounts as the live `banking status`, with the same transaction counts (a sync that ran between the two commands can add a few).

The project's automated tests also run a backup and a restore against temporary folders on every change, including the failure cases above. They prove the code path, not your bucket, your token or your key, which is why the manual test matters.

## 6. Put a restored database in place

Use this to recover from a damaged database or to move to a new host. It replaces the live database with the one from a backup set, so everything written after that backup is lost. The previous files are moved aside, not deleted.

Run the commands in a shell on the host (not through nested `ssh '…'` quoting). `compose` is the same set of files the deploy uses; add `-f` for the overlays whose secret files exist:

    cd <dir>
    compose=(docker compose --env-file <dir>/.env -f <dir>/current/deploy/compose.yaml \
      -f <dir>/current/deploy/compose.banking.yaml -f <dir>/current/deploy/compose.smtp.yaml \
      -f <dir>/current/deploy/compose.backup.yaml)

1. Choose the set: `"${compose[@]}" exec app node dist/cli.js backup list --remote` (or without `--remote`).
2. Stop the app: `"${compose[@]}" stop app`.
3. Restore the set into a new folder on the data volume, next to the live database:

        "${compose[@]}" run --rm --no-deps app node dist/cli.js restore --set <setId> --from s3 --to /data/restore-<setId>

4. Check it: `"${compose[@]}" run --rm --no-deps app node dist/cli.js banking status --data-dir /data/restore-<setId>`.
5. Swap the files. The live database has companion files, `bursar.db-wal` and `bursar.db-shm`; they must move with it, because a leftover `-wal` file would be applied to the wrong database:

        "${compose[@]}" run --rm --no-deps --entrypoint sh app -c '
          set -eu
          cd /data
          stamp="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
          mkdir "replaced-$stamp"
          mv bursar.db "replaced-$stamp/"
          for f in bursar.db-wal bursar.db-shm; do [ ! -e "$f" ] || mv "$f" "replaced-$stamp/"; done
          mv "restore-<setId>/bursar.db" bursar.db
          rmdir "restore-<setId>"
          echo "previous database kept in /data/replaced-$stamp"
        '

6. Start the stack and wait until it is healthy: `"${compose[@]}" --profile tunnel up -d --wait --wait-timeout 180`.
7. Check: open the panel and sign in (sessions and the password come back with the database), run `docker exec bursar-app-1 node dist/cli.js banking status`, and read `docker logs --since 5m bursar-app-1` for errors.

After a restore:

- Syncs fetch what is missing since the backup, within what each bank still provides (often about 90 days).
- A bank consent renewed after the backup points the restored database at the old, closed session. That connection shows as expired: renew it from the Accounts page.
- The restored database is the one the master key opens. With a different master key the restore stops with `wrong_key`.
- Keep `/data/replaced-<stamp>` until you are satisfied. When you want it gone, remove it deliberately, for example with a `run --rm --no-deps --entrypoint sh app -c 'rm -r /data/replaced-<stamp>'`.

### On a new host

Prepare the host and the secrets as in `docs/deployment.md`, with the **same** `master_key` file and the `BACKUP_S3_*` values (and the `backup_s3_secret_key` file), deploy once, then follow the steps above from step 1 with `--from s3`.
````

````markdown
# Deployment (reference: Docker host + Cloudflare Tunnel, optional Access)

This guide uses placeholders: `<host>` (ssh alias), `<dir>` (absolute deploy directory, for example `/opt/bursar`), `<hostname>` (public hostname of the panel).

Images are never pulled from a registry: they are built from source on the host (see `docs/decisions/0003-sdk-redistribution.md`).

## 1. Cloudflare

1. The hostname's zone must be on Cloudflare.
2. Zero Trust, Networks, Tunnels: create a Cloudflared tunnel named `bursar`. Copy its token.
3. In the tunnel, add a public hostname `<hostname>` with service `http://app:8080`.
4. Optional but recommended (defence in depth on top of the app login): Zero Trust, Access, Applications: add a self-hosted application for `<hostname>` with an Allow policy for your email. Copy the **Application Audience (AUD) tag** and note your team domain (`<team>.cloudflareaccess.com`).

Cloudflare Access is optional. Set `CF_ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN` and `CF_ACCESS_AUD` together or leave both empty. Without Access on a non-loopback URL the app logs a warning at startup.

## 2. Host preparation

The app runs as uid 1000 inside the container, so every secret file must be owned by uid 1000 with mode 600 (under rootless Docker, Podman or userns-remap, use the mapped uid instead).

The commands below and `deploy/deploy.sh` expect to log in as root on the host: setting ownership to uid 1000 needs root, and the deploy reads the root-owned `.env`. With a sudo user instead, prefix the preparation commands with `sudo` and run the deploy as a user that can read `<dir>/.env`, write `<dir>/releases` and `<dir>/current`, and use Docker.

    ssh <host> 'install -d -m 755 <dir> <dir>/releases && install -d -m 700 -o 1000 -g 1000 <dir>/secrets'
    ssh <host> 'set -C; umask 077; head -c 32 /dev/urandom | base64 > <dir>/secrets/master_key && chown 1000:1000 <dir>/secrets/master_key && chmod 600 <dir>/secrets/master_key'

`set -C` makes the second command fail instead of replacing an existing key: a new key makes the existing data unreadable. Keep an offline copy of `<dir>/secrets/master_key` (for example in a password manager): without it the data cannot be decrypted.

Copy the template to `<dir>/.env` with mode 600, again without overwriting an existing file, then edit it on the host:

    ssh <host> 'set -C; umask 077; cat > <dir>/.env' < deploy/env.example

Set these values in `<dir>/.env`:

- `BURSAR_PUBLIC_URL=https://<hostname>`
- `TZ` (your time zone)
- `BURSAR_SECRETS_DIR=<dir>/secrets`
- `BURSAR_TRUST_CF_CONNECTING_IP=true`: required in tunnel deployments, where every request reaches the app from cloudflared and the client address comes from the `CF-Connecting-IP` header. Leave it `false` whenever the app is reachable without Cloudflare, because clients could forge the header.
- `TUNNEL_TOKEN`
- `CF_ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN` and `CF_ACCESS_AUD`, only if you enabled Access (both or neither)

Optional Claude credential for the agent runtime: write it to `<dir>/secrets/claude_credential` (owner 1000, mode 600) and set `BURSAR_CLAUDE_CREDENTIAL_ENV` in `.env` to `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. When the file exists, the deploy adds `deploy/compose.claude.yaml` automatically.

The other optional integrations (bank accounts, email, backups) are described in section 3.

Check ownership and modes without printing contents:

    ssh <host> 'ls -la <dir> <dir>/secrets'

Expected: `.env` is `-rw-------`; `secrets/` is `drwx------` owned by `1000`; each secret file is `-rw-------` owned by `1000`.

## 3. Optional integrations: secrets and overlays

Each integration has non-secret values in `<dir>/.env` and one secret file in `<dir>/secrets` (owner 1000, mode 600). The deploy includes an overlay file only when its secret file exists, so an integration you do not use needs nothing.

| Integration | Secret file | Overlay | Values in `.env` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude agents | `claude_credential` | `compose.claude.yaml` | `BURSAR_CLAUDE_CREDENTIAL_ENV` |
| Bank accounts (Enable Banking) | `eb_private_key` | `compose.banking.yaml` | `EB_APPLICATION_ID` |
| Email notifications (SMTP) | `smtp_password` | `compose.smtp.yaml` | `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_SECURITY`, `SMTP_USER`, `SMTP_FROM` |
| Backups to an S3-compatible bucket | `backup_s3_secret_key` | `compose.backup.yaml` | `BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT`, `BACKUP_S3_REGION`, `BACKUP_S3_BUCKET`, `BACKUP_S3_PREFIX`, `BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID` |

Set the `.env` values and place the secret file in the same deploy. An integration with only one half (the id without the key, the S3 endpoint without the secret key) makes the app stop at startup with a message that names the missing variables, never their values. The reverse also holds: if you delete a secret file, clear its values in `.env` before the next deploy, because the deploy then leaves the overlay out.

Secret values are never typed on a command line. To write one without leaving it in the shell history, let the remote shell read it from the terminal (paste, Enter, Ctrl-D); `set -C` makes the command fail instead of replacing an existing file:

    ssh <host> 'set -C; umask 077; cat > <dir>/secrets/<secret file> && chown 1000:1000 <dir>/secrets/<secret file> && chmod 600 <dir>/secrets/<secret file>'

### 3.1 Bank accounts (Enable Banking)

Follow `docs/enable-banking.md`: it creates the RSA key directly in `<dir>/secrets/eb_private_key` on the host (so you do not use the command above for this one), registers the application and its redirect URL `https://<hostname>/api/banks/callback`, and explains restricted mode. Then set in `<dir>/.env`:

- `EB_APPLICATION_ID`: the application id (a uuid) from the Enable Banking Control Panel.
- `BURSAR_TRUST_CF_CONNECTING_IP=true`, as in section 2: without it "Sync now" cannot forward your address to the bank and counts as a background sync.

### 3.2 Email notifications (SMTP)

Notification emails contain an event title and a link to the panel, never financial data. In `<dir>/.env`:

- `SMTP_HOST`: the mail server.
- `SMTP_PORT`: `587` (the default) for `starttls`, `465` for `tls`.
- `SMTP_SECURITY`: `starttls` (default), `tls` (implicit TLS) or `none` (accepted only for a loopback host).
- `SMTP_USER`: the login name; leave empty, and place no password file, for a relay that needs no login.
- `SMTP_FROM`: the sender address.

Write the password to `<dir>/secrets/smtp_password` with the command above. Check it in the panel with Settings, Notifications, "Send test email".

### 3.3 Backups

Backups to the data volume (`/data/backups`) need nothing. To upload them to Cloudflare R2 or another S3-compatible bucket, follow `docs/backup-restore.md`: create a private bucket and a token scoped to it, put the `BACKUP_S3_*` values in `<dir>/.env` and the secret access key in `<dir>/secrets/backup_s3_secret_key`. Keep an offline copy of `<dir>/secrets/master_key`: a backup is useless without it.

Container logs rotate on their own (10 MB per file, 3 files per container).

## 4. Deploy

Put `BURSAR_DEPLOY_HOST` and `BURSAR_DEPLOY_DIR` in `.env.deploy` at the repository root (gitignored), or export them, then:

    deploy/deploy.sh [git-ref]

The script uploads the chosen commit (default `HEAD`) as `<dir>/releases/<UTC timestamp>-<short sha>/`, builds the image on the host, starts the stack with the `tunnel` profile, waits until the app is healthy and then points `<dir>/current` at the release. Old releases stay under `<dir>/releases/`; remove them manually when no longer needed.

## 5. Verify

    curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://<hostname>/healthz
    ssh <host> 'docker exec bursar-app-1 node -e "fetch(\"http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz\").then(r=>console.log(r.status))"'

With Access enabled, the public request returns `302` or `403` from Cloudflare (unauthenticated requests are blocked at the edge); without Access it reaches the app. The internal health check returns `200`.

Check the startup log for configuration problems (there should be no `Invalid configuration` message):

    ssh <host> 'docker logs --since 5m bursar-app-1'

After you have connected a bank, list the connections and accounts (masked identifiers and counts only, no names or amounts):

    ssh <host> 'docker exec bursar-app-1 node dist/cli.js banking status'

With a backup target configured, make a backup and expect a JSON line with `setId`, `sizeBytes` and `"target":"s3"` (`"local"` without a bucket), then run the restore test of `docs/backup-restore.md`:

    ssh <host> 'docker exec bursar-app-1 node dist/cli.js backup run'

## 6. First run

1. Open `https://<hostname>` and pass the Access login, if enabled.
2. Read the setup code on the host: `ssh <host> 'docker exec bursar-app-1 cat /data/setup-code'`.
3. Enter it with a new password, then enrol the authenticator app.

## 7. Connect your banks

Once you are signed in, open Accounts in the panel and connect a bank (see `docs/enable-banking.md`, sections 5 to 7: link your accounts first, then authorise). The first sync runs as soon as you return from the bank.
````

````markdown
# Bursar

Bursar is a self-hosted personal finance assistant. It reads your bank accounts through the Enable Banking API (read-only), keeps an encrypted archive of your financial documents, and runs a team of Claude agents that write a daily report on how your money is managed.

> **Status:** early development. Nothing here is ready for real use yet.

## Where your data goes

Bursar stores everything on your own server, encrypted at rest. Processing still involves third parties:

- Anthropic receives everything the agents read.
- Enable Banking brokers bank data: balances and transactions of the accounts you connect, read-only.
- Your SMTP provider relays the notification emails, if you configure email. They carry an event title and a link to the panel, never financial data.
- The backup target, if you configure one (Cloudflare R2 in the reference deployment), holds only encrypted copies of the database. Without the master key they cannot be read.
- Cloudflare terminates TLS if you use a Cloudflare Tunnel.
- Your hosting provider holds the disk, together with the master key that decrypts it. Encryption at rest protects copies of the data volume and backups that leave the host without the key; it does not protect against whoever controls the host.

## Bank accounts

Bursar reads balances and transactions through Enable Banking and never moves money: the server can reach only a fixed list of account-information operations, and every payment operation is rejected before a request leaves the process. Free usage is Enable Banking's restricted mode: a production application that you activate by linking your own accounts in the Enable Banking Control Panel. Only linked accounts return data, so link every account first. Bank consents last up to 180 days for most banks and are renewed from the Accounts page. Setup, the redirect URL, limits and troubleshooting: [docs/enable-banking.md](docs/enable-banking.md).

## Backups

Every night Bursar writes an encrypted copy of its database to the data volume and, if you configure a bucket, uploads it to an S3-compatible target such as Cloudflare R2. It keeps 7 daily, 4 weekly and 6 monthly copies. The master key is never part of a backup: keep an offline copy of it. Setup, the command-line tools, restoring and the restore test: [docs/backup-restore.md](docs/backup-restore.md). Deployment of the whole stack: [docs/deployment.md](docs/deployment.md).

## Development

Requirements: Node 24, pnpm (via `packageManager`), Docker, gitleaks.

    pnpm install
    pnpm test

The panel has a visual quality check that starts a throwaway server with fictional data and walks through every page in light and dark mode and at phone width, writing screenshots and failing on console errors, layout overflow or untranslated text. It uses the Chrome installed on your machine:

    pnpm --filter @bursar/web qa

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).
````

### Task 24: Operational verification on the Sandbox and the reference host (controller)

This task is run by the controller (the session that drives the plan), not by an implementer subagent. It writes no application code, so the TDD cycle of the other tasks does not apply: every step is a check with an exact command and its expected output, and the only repository changes are the ADR and the plan appendix in Step 12. A step whose expected output does not appear stops the task: diagnose it with superpowers:systematic-debugging, fix it in the task that owns the code (a new `fix(...)` commit on this branch), re-run Step 1, then resume. After three failed attempts on the same problem, stop and report the diagnosis to the owner.

Placeholders used below, all filled at run time from the owner's private notes and never written into the repository or into a commit: `<host>` (ssh alias of the reference host), `<dir>` (absolute deploy directory on the host), `<hostname>` (public hostname of the panel), `<sandbox key path>` (absolute path of the Sandbox private key on the owner's machine, outside the repository), `<sandbox cert path>` (its certificate), `<scratchpad>` (the controller session's scratchpad directory), `<setId>` (printed by `backup run`), `<date>` (today, `YYYY-MM-DD`). `<prefix>` is the shell prefix from Global Constraints.

**Behaviour decided here** (the contract leaves it open):
- The local CLI is run as `pnpm --filter @bursar/server exec tsx --tsconfig tsconfig.runtime.json --env-file=.env src/cli.ts …` (from the package directory, so `./data` and `.env` resolve as in `pnpm --filter @bursar/server dev`). The `bursar` script in `apps/server/package.json` has no `--env-file`, so `pnpm --filter @bursar/server bursar banking status` would start without `BURSAR_PUBLIC_URL` and the master key and fail with a `ConfigError`.
- On `localhost` every manual "Sync now" comes from a loopback address, so Task 13 treats it as a background sync, which counts against the daily cap (default 2). The Sandbox run needs three syncs per account on one day (initial, renewal, manual), so Step 3 raises "background syncs per account per day" to 4 in the local settings. On the host the owner's IP arrives through `CF-Connecting-IP` and a manual sync sends PSU headers.
- The ADR and the plan record counts and masked identifiers only for the Sandbox (fictional Mock ASPSP data). For real banks they record counts only: no bank names, no masked identifiers, no last-4 digits, because which banks the owner uses is a personal identifier. The full outputs stay in the scratchpad and the owner's private notes.
- The restore comparison is done on the `banking status` JSON of the live database and of the restored copy (must be identical) plus the restore's `tables` counts. `tables` is read with SQL table names as keys (`bank_connections`, `accounts`, `transactions`), and an account's `transactions` field in `banking status` is read as the number of every stored transaction row of the account, pending included (`pending` is the subset). If Task 15 or Task 16 shipped different key names or a different meaning, adjust the two lines marked in `restore-check.mjs` and note it in the verification table.
- Comparison scripts live only in `<scratchpad>` (never in the repository).
- Sandbox redirect URLs: the owner registers both `http://localhost:5173/api/banks/callback` and `https://<hostname>/api/banks/callback` on the Sandbox application when the Control Panel accepts them, so the host fallback of Step 2 needs no change to the application.

Prepare the comparison script once:

`<scratchpad>/renewal-check.mjs`:

```js
// Compares `bursar banking status` snapshots of the Sandbox renewal test.
// Usage: node renewal-check.mjs <before.json> <after-renewal.json> [<after-manual-sync.json>] [bank name]
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";

const [beforePath, afterPath, syncPath, bankArg] = process.argv.slice(2);
const bank = bankArg ?? "Mock ASPSP";
const load = (path) => JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, "utf8"));
const connectionsOf = (status) => status.connections.filter((c) => c.bank === bank);
const ids = (connection) => connection.accounts.map((a) => a.id).sort((x, y) => x - y);
const problems = [];

const [before] = connectionsOf(load(beforePath));
const afterAll = connectionsOf(load(afterPath));
const after = afterAll[0];
if (!before) problems.push(`no ${bank} connection in the first snapshot`);
if (afterAll.length !== 1) problems.push(`expected one ${bank} connection after renewal, found ${afterAll.length}`);

if (before && after) {
  if (after.id !== before.id) problems.push(`connection id changed: ${before.id} -> ${after.id}`);
  if (after.status !== "active") problems.push(`connection status after renewal: ${after.status}`);
  if (after.renewedAt === null) problems.push("renewedAt is not set");
  if (JSON.stringify(ids(after)) !== JSON.stringify(ids(before))) {
    problems.push(`account ids differ: [${ids(before)}] -> [${ids(after)}]`);
  }
  const masked = after.accounts.map((a) => a.masked).filter((m) => m !== null);
  if (new Set(masked).size !== masked.length) problems.push("duplicate accounts (same masked identifier twice)");
  for (const account of before.accounts) {
    const renewed = after.accounts.find((a) => a.id === account.id);
    if (renewed && renewed.transactions < account.transactions) {
      problems.push(`account ${account.id}: transactions dropped ${account.transactions} -> ${renewed.transactions}`);
    }
    if (renewed && renewed.status !== "active") problems.push(`account ${account.id}: status ${renewed.status}`);
  }
}

if (syncPath && after) {
  const [synced] = connectionsOf(load(syncPath));
  if (!synced) problems.push(`no ${bank} connection after the manual sync`);
  else {
    for (const account of after.accounts) {
      const next = synced.accounts.find((a) => a.id === account.id);
      if (!next) problems.push(`account ${account.id} missing after the manual sync`);
      else if (next.transactions !== account.transactions) {
        problems.push(`account ${account.id}: ${account.transactions} -> ${next.transactions} transactions after a manual sync`);
      }
    }
  }
}

if (problems.length > 0) {
  for (const problem of problems) console.log(`renewal-check: ${problem}`);
  process.exit(1);
}
const total = after.accounts.reduce((sum, a) => sum + a.transactions, 0);
console.log(`renewal-check: ok (connection ${after.id}, ${after.accounts.length} accounts, ${total} transactions)`);
```

The Sandbox may not honour `valid_until` and its date filters are unreliable (`eb-api-notes.md` §10): a session that expires early shows as "expired" and is simply renewed again; a renewal sync that re-fetches the full history must still leave the counts unchanged (that is the deduplication under test). A count that grows after the manual sync is a failure unless the Mock ASPSP really added transactions, which the owner confirms by finding the new rows (new dates) in the Transactions page; record it in the report.

Disconnect and purge: the owner chooses "Disconnect" on the Mock ASPSP connection; the confirmation dialog lists the real counts (accounts and transactions from `removal-preview`), the owner confirms with "Yes, disconnect"; the accounts move to "Disconnected accounts". The owner purges one account ("Purge transactions", confirmed) and checks it disappears from the list; then purges the remaining ones.

Expected: `{"connections":[]}` (the connection row is deleted after its last account is purged).

Prepare the comparison script once:

`<scratchpad>/restore-check.mjs`:

```js
// Compares the live `banking status`, the restored copy's `banking status` and the restore output.
// Usage: node restore-check.mjs <live-status.json> <restored-status.json> <restore-output.json>
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";

const [livePath, restoredPath, restorePath] = process.argv.slice(2);
const load = (path) => JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, "utf8"));
const live = load(livePath);
const restored = load(restoredPath);
const restore = load(restorePath);
const problems = [];

if (JSON.stringify(live) !== JSON.stringify(restored)) {
  problems.push("banking status differs between the live database and the restored copy");
}
const accounts = live.connections.flatMap((c) => c.accounts);
const transactions = accounts.reduce((sum, a) => sum + a.transactions, 0);
const tables = restore.tables ?? {};
// Table names as printed by `bursar restore` (Task 15); adjust here if they differ.
const expected = { bank_connections: live.connections.length, accounts: accounts.length, transactions };
for (const [table, count] of Object.entries(expected)) {
  if (!(table in tables)) problems.push(`restore output has no count for ${table}`);
  else if (tables[table] !== count) problems.push(`${table}: restored ${tables[table]}, live ${count}`);
}

if (problems.length > 0) {
  for (const problem of problems) console.log(`restore-check: ${problem}`);
  process.exit(1);
}
console.log(
  `restore-check: ok (set ${restore.restored}, connections ${expected.bank_connections}, accounts ${expected.accounts}, transactions ${transactions})`,
);
```
